Building strategy[edit | edit source]

   Strategy The below is one of many player suggested strategies for Buildings. Bear in mind, due to the dynamic nature of the game, it may unfold differently for other players.

General considerations[edit | edit source]

   There are some general rules of thumb that should be taken to heart when investing in buildings:
     * Money should be invested in buildings only if it isn't needed for something more important.
     * The time needed to generate a profit should be noted; some provinces may be too poor to ever generate a profit in the remaining time-frame.^[6]
     * When considering a large building spree, it might be advisable to invest in the Infrastructure idea group.png Infrastructure idea group, and couple it with policies to reduce the building costs.
     * It's good to remember that besides Local autonomy.png local autonomy, province income can also be affected by the province's Culture icon.png culture and religion (if different than the state religion).
     * Space is limited. The number of buildings can only be increased by increasing the Development.png development level, or Dharma.png raising a center of trade to level three (only in states and trade companies), if one exists in the province. (Corollary: increase development to open more spaces.)

Building prioritization[edit | edit source]

   Buildings' positioning can have great effect on return-on-investment. It is thus recommended to build the following building types in the appropriate provinces:
     * Buildings providing a percentile bonus are best built in state provinces with high Development.png development values, low Local autonomy.png local autonomy, and targeted to increase the province's strength(s), e.g., trade buildings in provinces with modifiers benefiting Local trade power.png local trade power (such as Province trade power value.png centers of trade).
     * Buildings providing a flat bonus are best built in territorial provinces as they won't be affected by the high autonomy, or in state provinces with low Development.png development values.
     * Manufactories increase Local goods produced local goods produced, which in turn also increase both the province Trade value modifier.png trade value and its production income. In addition, coupling them with production buildings in state provinces with high value trade goods will generate high production income.
     * Manufactories are not affected by autonomy, culture, and religion as other buildings. Thus, they can be built even in high autonomy provinces. While the generated production income may not be at its fullest, they can still return the investment when also taking into account the generated Tradeview income.png trade income.
     * Prioritize building forts in provinces with defensive terrain or those with low Supply limit.png supply limit to couple them with the Local defensiveness.png local defensiveness and high Attrition attrition bonuses, and to make sure you get a terrain bonus to help break sieges. If possible, they should be built mostly in border provinces and mothballed until needed.
     * Other manufactory level buildings introduced in 1.30 may be more useful than increasing production. For example: Ramparts in a province with a fort improve its defensiveness; Soldiers' Houses greatly increase available manpower if built in Grain provinces, likewise Impressment Offices in Fish provinces, both being trade goods of low value.

Avoidance[edit | edit source]

   Since buildings cost money, their cost-benefit ratio should be considered. Thus, an important step is to know when not to invest in a building type:
     * Trade buildings are unnecessary in trade nodes dominated by the nation, and you don't need more trade power propagated upstream.
     * Army/Navy buildings can be avoided if the nation maintains large forces and there are no nations of similar or stronger power.
     * Due to forts' initial high cost and ongoing Fort maintenance modifier.png fort maintenance, it's best to avoid building them in the inner provinces of the nation where they are far from enemy borders and forces. If the area is prone to rebellions, several low level forts might be more successful in slowing the rebels down until other forces arrive.

Destroying buildings[edit | edit source]

   Occasionally it is beneficial to destroy a building:
     * Excess forts cost money to maintain even when mothballed. Forts that aren't strategically useful - those in the interior if the enemy never reaches it, or multiple forts in a small space after annexing several small countries, for example - can be worth destroying.
     * Occasionally a building other than a fort was useful when built, but becomes a waste of a slot due to changing circumstances.
     * when annexing an AI, it could be worth to destroy some non-useful buildings (such as church in low tax income province) to build better one (like manufactories).

Is borrow-to-build worthwhile?[edit | edit source]

   Is it worthwhile to take out loans in order to construct a certain building? Equivalently, if there is an on-going loan, should the loan be paid off first before initiating on any construction project? Just like in real life, theoretically, the answer is yes if the income provided by the building per year divided by the sum of build cost and interest accrued during construction is higher than interest per annum. This can be the case for highly developed provinces or for manufactories in a highly productive province that produces expensive trade goods. (For manufactories, the player should also include trade income.) However, the player would also need to make sure there is enough income to pay off the loan before inflation gets out of hand. A player considering using debt to build, however, is cautioned to carefully consider these trade-offs, for in many cases, it is not profitable. A safe guide is whether the income before constructing the building is able to cover the principal part of
   the loan within a reasonable time frame.

   However, if you have a mission to build a basic structure that offers +1 development, then it is definitely worth it because each dev upgrade is about 50 monarch points and that is similar to 50 ducats in comparison.

When will increased income cover building costs?[edit | edit source]

   The increase in income is dynamically influenced by provincial and national modifiers such as tax efficiency, production efficiency as well as the development in the province, all of which are bound to increase as technology progresses. Therefore, early game, whether a building will pay for itself is not usually the question. The question is how long and thus if the ducat can be better spent elsewhere. The following table lists the required increase in monthly income (displayed in-game in the building interface) for a certain number of years before the building breaks even.

Colonization

   From Europa Universalis 4 Wiki
   Jump to navigation Jump to search

   Please help with verifying or updating older sections of this article.
   At least some were last verified for version 1.33.

   As EU4 starts during the age of discovery, Colonization is an important feature available. Nations can explore and colonize the continents of the Americas (or a Random New World with Conquest of Paradise.png Conquest of Paradise enabled), Asia, Africa and Austrahttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/lia, as well as Siberia and islands in the Pacific.
   [ ]

Objectives and prerequisites[edit | edit source]

   Thhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/e main benefit of colonialism is to improve the income generation and military logistics of the colonizing country. This is because colonized territories overseas can provide large boosts in trade income to the colonizing nation, as well as provide staging points for naval and lanhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/d warfare around the world.

   This is accomplished primarily by creating colonial nations, which are AI-controlled subject nations that will produce their own military and navy but will provide trade power and other benefits to the colonizer, and creating trade companies, which are semi-autonomous provinces that provide substantial trade bonuses in thttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/rade nodes that the colonizer can control. The type of subject nation created depends on its location in the world.

   Any nation can benefit fully from overseas territorieshttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/, even very distant ones, if they choose to make that territory into a state. However, provinces in oversehttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/as colonial regions should not be made into states, as https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/the provinces are eventually ceded to the new colonial nation. Western technology nations will most likely prefer to make trade company provinces if possible instead of creating new ohttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/verseas states, due to the bonus trade power and the abilityhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ to ignore religious differences. However, for many other natiohttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ns, overseas states can sometimes be very profitable.

   In order to colonize a nation must have:
     * a Colonists.png colonist (from national ideas, ihttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/dea groups, a Parliamentary issue, or a religious reform)
          + A special case https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/is Flag of Russia Russia with the Third Rome.png Third Rome DLC, who can establish certain colonies without a colonist.
     * an empty province to colonize (either adjacent to a core province, or within colonial range of a port)

   It is recommended that a nation have:
     * Gold Icon.png Ducats to cover maintenance of the colony (which rises quadratically if the number of colonies exceeds the number of colonists)
     * a means of pacifying the natives (troops to guard it, or policies to lower their aggressiveness)

   /eu4.paradoxwikis.com/>Discovery[edit | edit source]

   Ambox outdated info.png
   Please help withhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ verifying or updating this section. It was last verified for version 1.33.

   Although some uncolonized provinces may be visible at the beginning of the game, much of both land and wathttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/er is covered by terra incognita. Discovering these areas is essential to finding provinces to colonize.

   How a nation goes about exhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ploring depends on whether El Dorado.png El Dorado is enabled or not. That said, the following factors are true regardless of DLC:
     * A Conquistador https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/conquistador is required to explore on land (unless the country is at war; see below), and an Explorhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/er explorer is required to explore at sea. These are special military leaders that are given https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/pips as though the country had 80% as much tradition as it really does, in exchange for being able to explore.
     * The “Quest for the New World” Icon ideas.png idea, the first idea in the Exploration idea group.png Exploration idea group, is required to hire explorers and conquistadors. A handful of countries (notably /eu4.paradoxwikis.com/n style="white-space:nowrap;"> Flag of Portugal Portugal) have an explorer in 1444 despite not having the idea; these leaders cannot explore in ocean provinces until Quest for the New World is unlocked.

     * Somehttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ countries have a national idea allowing to recruit explorers and conquistadors and allows them to explore without taking Exploration idea group.png Exploration ideas; see the table below. Some countries additionally have missions that give temporary modifiers with the ability.

     While at war, armies can enter all enemy provinces, even those hidden by terra incognita, assuming movement isn't blocked by forts or blockades. This can be done by clicking to move the army into a suspected province within the terra incognita; the army will begin to move regardless of whether they are able to complete the move. Movement into the https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/province takes just as long as if it was being explored with a conquihttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/stador. When the move completes, the army either enters the province, or discovers that movement is blocked and stops moving; either way, the province is revealed.

     Conquistadors with high army tradition have a chance to discover adjacent provinces.

     Undiscovered land provinces have a chance per month to be discovered by owners of adjacent provinces (typically taking 3–5 years). Flag of Russia Russia, colonial nations, nations with the Offensive-Expansion: The Pioneer Policy, https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/and potentially custom nations have national ideas that make this discovery instant.

     Discovery of individual provinces will occur based on contact with other nations. In general, a province will be revealed to a country if:
     * The country in question explored any adjacent province at least 25 years ago
     * Any country that owns provinces undiscovered by the original country discovered the capital province of the original country at least 30 years ago.
     * Ahttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ny neighbouring country, in the same culture or religious grhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/oup as the original country, explored a province at least 75 years ago.

   Mare Nostrum.png Available only with the Mare Nostrum DLC enabled.

   Map exploration can also be accomplished via the diplomatic action to Share Maps, which will reveal entire regions to the requesting nation at the cost of Prestige.png prestige if the nation beihttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ng asked to Share Maps has already explored that region, and the nation requesting the maps has units in an adjacent region. Additionally, the diplomatic action Steal Maps (unlocked at Diplomatic tech.png diplomatic technology level 6 and which requires a spy network of 50 on that country) can be used to reveal regions in the same manner, but without the prestige cost.

   Some idehttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/as allow recruiting explorers and conquistadors:

   May explore Traditions Ideas Bonuses Policies
   yes
     * Icelandic traditions

     * Exploration idea 1: Quest for the New World
     * Norse idea 6: Leif's Legacy
     * Norwegian idea 1: The Chttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/all of our Forefathers
     * Samoan idea 7: Polynesian Triangle Trade
     * Tongan idea 7: The Oceanic Empire

     * Hawaiian ambition

   —

   Domination.png Available only with the Dominahttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/tion DLC enabled.

     * The Flag of England English mission “Found the Royal Nhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/avy” gives a temporary modifier allowing the country to recruit explorers and conquistadors for 25 years.
     * The Flag of Russia Russian mission “Push into Eastern Siberia” gives gives a temporary modifier allowing the country to recruit explorershttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ and conquistadors for 100 years.

  Exploration without El Dorado.png El Dorado[edit | edit source]

     * An army (of any size) led by a Conquistador conquistador can be moved into land provinces covered by terra incognita, thus discovering them. If that land is owned by another country, the conquistador will merely discover the province when movement finishes instead of actually moving into it, unless that country grants military access. Conquistadors can move through primitive nations (those in New World technology groups that have not yet reformed their governments/religions) even without access.
     * A fleet (of any size) led by an Explorehttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/r explorer can be moved into sea zones covehttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/red by terra incognita, thus discovering them. Upon entering a https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/sea zone, they also have a chance to discover coastal provinces adjacent in that zone (increased by the explorer's Maneuver skill).

  Exploration with El Dorado.png El Dorado[edit | edit source]

     * Land exploration largely follows the same process as it does without El Dorado.png El Dorado, as listed above.
     * If the country's own capital is not in a colonial region, an army (of any size) led by a Conquistador conquistador in a colonial region can be sent on a mission to Hunt for the Seven Cities of Gold via the ahttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/rmy interface. The army will then automatically move through terrahttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ incognita in the region, uncovering it as it moves, with a chance to trigger various special events. Exploring provinces owned by primitives, whether using Hunt for the Seven Cities or not, does not require military access.
     * Any fleet led by an Explorer explorer and containing at least three Light ship.png light and/or Heavy ship.png heavy ships can be sent on an exploration mission via the fleet interface and will do so automatically once assigned.
          + The fleet can be sent to explore 'thhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/e waters' of a region, meaning the explorer will discoverhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ open sea and coastal sea zones, but will not discover land provinces; or they can be sent to explore 'the coast' of a region, meaning the explorer will explore and reveal coastal land provinces in that region. Typically, 'the waters' of a region must be explored first before 'the coast' becomes avahttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ilable as a mission. While exploring open sea, the explorhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/er will discover all sea zones in that region that are in range before returning (not necessarily to its starting province). While exploring a coastal sea zone, they will discover all coastal provinces bordering that sea region before returning. Right-clicking on unexplored ocean will automatically start the exploration mission for the appropriate region, as long as part of it is within range. /eu4.paradoxwikis.com/>
          + If a country has an explorer but does not havehttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ "Quest for the New World" or an equivalent national idea, the explorer will be limited to exploring coastal sea zones. This is still usually sufficient to reach new continents (e.g., the east coast of North America can be reached from Europe via coastal zohttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/nes around Iceland and Greenland)
          + Fleets on exploration missions do not suffer attrition, but only missions to regions within their country's Range.png colonial range can be explored this way. Fleets on exploration missions cannot be recalled or reashttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/signed during the mission, only disbanded, which may kill the explorer. Explorers may trigger certain random events while on missions. If the explorer dies, the fleet will automatically return home but will take attrition while doing so.
     * An explorer https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/can also be sent to circumnavigate the globe. The fleet will take Naval attrition.png /eu4.paradoxwikis.com/a> naval attrition as normal while on this mission, and may sink, killing the explorer as well. Like other exploration missions, fleets sent on missions to circumnavigate the globe cannot be recalled orhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ reassigned during the mission; ample preparation beforehand is advised before beginning the mission. The first nation worldwide to have an explorer successfully circumnavigate the globe receives [28px-Yearly_prestige.png] +100 prestige. Any other nation that completes this mission afterwards receives Prestige.png +10 prestige. This exploration mission can only be completed once per nation, though it can be repeated if failed.

  Native policies[edit | edit source]

   The Cossacks.png Available only with the The Cossacks DLC enabled.

   An example of native policies in game

   Native policies allow a nation to decide on their foreign policy regarding indigenous natives in colonizable provinces around the world. Ahttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ native policy must be chosen when a nation unlocks their first colonist (from any source). The orihttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ginal selection is free. Changing native policies afterwards costs −1 Icon stability.png stabilithttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/y, but has no cooldown.

   Native Coexistence Policy grants a −100% bonus to the chance to get a Native uprising https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/chance.png native uprising, effectively reducing aggressiveness in all colonizable provinces to 0. This policy is beneficial for when a nation's armies are busy elsewhere and can't be wasted sitting on a colony, when manpower is too precarious for constant skirmishes, when a nation is too poor to maintain a garrison, or for native and Sub-Saharan nations who may actually lose battles with natives in the early game. This policy also prevents natives from attacking exploring armies led by conquistadors, negating the need thttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/o field more than one unit in an exploring army or spend ducats on maintenance for said army.

   Native Trading Policy grants a −50% bonus to Native uprising chance.png native uprising chance (effectively reducing aggressiveness by half) and +50% to Native assimilationhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/.png native assimilation.

   Native assimilation means that the goods produced in a colonized province will increase by a factor equal to
   [MATH: <semantics> <mrow class="MJX-TeXAtom-ORD"> <mstyle displaystyle="true" scriptlevel="0"> <mrow class="MJX-TeXAtom-ORD"> <mtext>native population</mtext> </mrow> <mo>÷</mo> <mn>20</mn> <mo>,</mo> <mn>000</mnhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/> </mstyle> </mrow> <annotation encoding="applicatiohttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/n/x-tex">{\displaystyle {\text{native population}}\div 20,000}</annotation> </semantics> :MATH]
   {\displaystyle {\text{native population}}\div 20,000} , rounded down, once that colony becomes a full province. The native trading policy increases this bonus by +50%. This choice could be useful if playing Flag of France France, which also has a bonus to native assimilation in their national ideas (and also receives a reduction to native uprising chance that makes it a more advantageous Native Coexistence Policy), or for any nation that can handle a few revolts and will be coring and taking full control of the province when completed, or any nation controlling a significant percentage of the generated trade value.

   Native Repression Policy grants a bonus Global colonial growth.png +20 global settler increase. While this policy makes for more rapid early colonization, the bonus is not overwhelming at higher technology levels. The provinces will require garrisons as Native uprising chance.png native uprising chance is not reduced.

  Range.png Colonial range[edit | edit source]

   Ambox outdated info.png
   Please help with verifying or updating this section. It was last verified for version 1.30.

   The range from which a nation can establish a https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/colony from a chttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ore is called the colonial range. It is measured from that nation's nearest unoccupied core province (hence, during war, coring range may be significantly reduced until key provinces are unsieged from enemy occupation), and it expands depending on the diplomatic technology level of the nation as well as events, advisers, missionshttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/, policies, ideas, and other bonuses. Fleet basing rights from third countries do not extend this range.

   This range also controls how far explorers can go on exploration missions. If a nathttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ion has no ports, they can only colonize adjacent land provinces, rehttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/gardless of colonial range.

   To check the range to a given province, chhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ange the map mode to "Colonial Range", and hover over the province of interest. The map will show green for in range and red for out of range.

  Colonist time.png Travel time[edit | edit source]

   The speed at which a nation's colonists travel to claim and establish colonial territory is related to the travel time of merchants and diplomats. It is based primarily on distance from the capital but, unless the target province is directly land connected to the capital, colonists travel by sea. The actual route taken is the shortest sea distance from either the capital's port (or, if ihttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/t is inland, a port that is directly connected to it) to either the target province's future port location or the port that is closest to the target province.

   Example: Flag of Portugal Portugal's capital is Lisboa. In order to colonize Pipil (839), a province next to the Mayan nation of Flag of Kiche Kiche on the west coast of Central America, a colonist would first travel all the way south to Cape Horn in South America, then back north to rhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/each Central America again. However, if Portugal colonized Chortli (2637) first, which is the provinchttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/e north of Pipil but on the east coast of Central America, then a Colonist subsequently travelling to Pipil would have its travel time dramatically reduced.

   Colonist travel time can be difficult to predict due to their coded preferences for travel. https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/For port provinces not directly connected to one's capital, colonists will always travel bhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/y sea to where the port will be located, even if it would be faster to travel overland from another port (or the province borders both coasts like in Centhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ral America). For inland provinces not directly connected to the capital, colonists always travel to the closest non-blockaded port to the target province even if it would be quicker to travel cross country from a port on a different coast. These unusual rules can shttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ometimes account for extended colonist travel time.

   Nations in colonial regions, especially North America, can experience unusually long travel times for colonists. Normally, this is because if a nation's capital is coastal, colonists will always prefer to travel by sea, even if travelling by land would be faster. It may be prhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/udent to move the capital inland if this becomes an issue.

   Colonists travel across open sea much faster than through land or coastal sea provinces. For example, European colonists can reach thttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/he Caribbean faster than Sub-Saharan West Africa, evenhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ though it is physically much farther away.

   All modifiers to Envoy travel time.png envoy travel timehttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ also change the travel time for colonists. Colonists return instantly the day after either the colony becomes a city or they are recalled.

   As soon as any nation chooses to send a colonist to a province, no other nation can send a colonist to that province unless the colony is later destroyed before completion, even if the colonist will actually arrive two years later. Two nations cannot 'race' and see which colonist will arrive first to the province.

    Population[edit | edit source]

       Ambox outdated info.png

   Please helphttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ with verifying or updating this section. It was last verified for version 1.33.
       Once a colonist arrives in an unowned province the population starts at 10. Colony populations grow at a base rate depending on the nation's Global colonial growth.png global settler increase value, which is largely dependent on Diplomatic tech.png diplomatic technology level but also by some ideas and other modifiers.
       In addition, as long as a colonist remains in a colony, they have a chance each month (modified by Colonist placement chance.png colonist chance) of bringing in 25 additional population, speeding growth greatly.
       Once a colony reaches a population of 400, it will be randomly assigned a trade good based on a weighted list of goods available in that geographical region. This list can be seen via hovering over the large Unknown question mark icon in the uncolonized province screen, or by hovering over the province in the Trade Goods map mode. If the colony is abandoned or otherwise destroyed at this stage, the trade good reverts to Unknown Unknown (i.e. the weighted list), meaning that a different trade good may be randomly assigned in following attempts at colonising the province.
       A colony becomes a full city when its population reaches 1000, and is destroyed if its population reaches 0; this will happen if a colony is abandoned, but can also happen due to attacks by natives, events and colonies being destroyed by other countries in a war. Resending a colonist is required to restart these colonies.
       Colonists can be sent and recalled to other colonies in progress as many times as is warranted. Colonists can even be sent to colonies of enemy nations that have been seized by using the Seize colony.png “Seize Colony” army option (which costs Military power.png 25 military power). A captured colony retains the culture and religion that it had previously, but a colonist will convert to those of its new owner in the same circumstances as it would otherwise.
       Global settler increahttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/se[edit/eu4.paradoxwikis.com/span class="mw-editsection-divider"> | edit source]
       Colonies grow by a flat numhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ber of settlers each month. This number is the nation's Global colonial growth.png global settler increase, whhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ich is the number of additional colonists added to a colhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ony per year. Settlers are distributed unevenly per month if the yearly increase isn't divisible by 12, rather than there being "partial" settlers and rounding. For example, if the country's global settler increase plus the province's local settler increase is 15 per year, the colony will get one settler most months but two settlers every fourth month, for a total of 15 for the year. Dhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/iplomatic technology provides additional global settler increase:

    Important modifiers to colony growth[edit | edit source]
    Climate[edit | edit source]
       The locathttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ion and climate of a potential colony will affect the rate of growth of the cohttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/lony. Colonies in arid, tropical or arctic locations will receive a Global colonial growth.png −10 global settler increase penalty, and a colony with no adjacent colonies of that nation will receive a further Global colonial growth.png −5 penalty. Several nations have burgher estate privileges that partially or fully negate these penalties for specific climates.
       If controlling an area ahead of other colonizers is a concern, a nation can prefer to colonize locations with favorable terrain, but other major factors such as the number of hostile natives and the presence of a Center of Trade need to be considered as well.
       Events[edit | edit source]

                Main articles: Exploration idea group events, Expansion idea group events

       The Exploration and Expansion idea groups unlock several events that can trigger to mohttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/dify colony growth rate or size directly, and can be either beneficial or detrimential. The events Colonist Rush and Colonial Enthusiasmhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ give the following powerful, but temporary, modifiers to colony growth:
          + Gain “Colonial Enthusiasm” modifier for 10 years:
               o Colonist placement chance.png +5% Colonist chance
               o Global colonial growth.png +25 Global settler increase
       This modifier can also be granted by several estate agendas.
       Some nations that were historical colonizers, notably Flag of Spain Spain and Flag of Portugal Portugal, have unique missions or events that will improve settler growth.
       Treaty of Tordesillas[edit | edit source]

       El Dorado.png Available only with the El Dorado DLC enabled.
       With El Dorado DLC, the first nation to form a Catholic colonial nation (that is, to core 5 provinces in a colonial region, assuminghttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ its own capital is not within a colonial region) while the Papal State's opinion of them is positive will be assigned that region. That nation and their associated colonial nation will receive a Global colonial growth.png +10 increase to settler growth within the region. A single nation can have any number of colonial regions assigned to them by the Pope.
       If another Catholic nation (even one with its capital in a colonial region) starts colonizing a province in that region, they will receive a severe penalty for having "Violated the Treaty of Tordesillas". This include a Global colonial growth.png −20 local settler increase penalty when colonizing that colonial region, as well as Papal influence.phttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ng −10 papal influence and Icon diplomacy relations.png −50 modifier (up to -200) to the Papal State's opinion of that nation every time you start colhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/onizing in violation of the treaty. Also, the nation that has the claim receives a Icon diplomacy relations.png −50 modifier (for each violation, up to -200)) to the opinion of them, with yearly decay of +1. Colonies that are in progress when the Pope assigns a colonial region to another nation do not count as having violated the Treaty of Tordesillas, only colonies started after a colonial region has been assigned.
       These modifiers can only affect Catholic nations; nations of other religions can receive neither the bonuses nor the penalties.
       If the nation owning a colonial region is completely annexed, or if the nation converts away from Catholicism, the colonial region will revert to no nation having a colonial claim, and a new nation can be assigned the region by creating a colonial nation or owning a current colonial nation in the region.
       The Treaty of Tordesillas mechanic attempts to represent, and generalize, the historical treaty made between Portugal and Spain which assigned lands east or west of a certain longitude to Portugal or Spain, respectively.
       Native policies[edit | edit source]

       The Cossacks.png Available only with the The Cossacks DLC enabled.
       With The Cossacks expansion, a nation must select a native policy that represents how that nation will interact with native peoples around the world. This only refers to the uncivilized indigenous native populations in uncolonized provinces, not to any Native American, African or Indonesian nations.
       If a nation selects Repression, they will receive a bonus Global colonhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ial growth.png +20 global settler increase, at the cost of more uprisings by the natives (although uprisings can still be prevented via some ideas, policies, and estate privileges). The other two policies do not affect settler increase.

Non-Christian nations cannot receive any of these events.

       Natives[edit | edit source]https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/

       Ambox outdated info.png

   Please help with verifying or updating this section. It was last verified for version 1.33.
       /eu4.paradoxwikis.com/p>Colonizable provinces are usually inhabited by natives, who may randomly attack a colony established there, potentially destroying it. Natives may also attack land units passing through a province, whether it is a colony or uncolonized. They also have the positive effect of a slight bonus to the Goods produced.png goods produced after the colony is finished depending on remaining native population.
       The chance of an uprising depends on the natives' Aggressiveness icon.png Aggressiveness and national Native uprising chance.png Native uprising chance modifiers. Uprising risk can be addreshttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/sed by lowering likelihood, primarily through Native Policy choice (−50% with "Trading", −100% with "Coexistence"), stationing military units in or near a province to defend against them, or outright exterminating the local natives with your troops. Native tribes do not experience native uprisings.
       Population[edit | edit source]
       Native population in 1444.
       The shttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ize of the native population determines how many native regiments attack at a time (1000 natives per regiment). The native population in a province can be reduced permanently using the Attack natives.png  Attack Natives military action, which costs a certain amount of Military phttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ower.png military power proportional to population size andhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ Native aggressiveness aggressiveness, and modified by Ferocity icon.png ferocity (exact formula needed). The cost ranges from one or two points for tiny non-warlike populations up to dozens of points for many determined combatants. The action may need to be performed multiple times in order to completely drive out the local population, as native regiments that break from combat due to low morale are not killed and so return to the 'population' of the colony.

Native uprising[edit | edit source]
       If a native uphttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/rising happens, an army of native warriors with size equal to the native population will appear and attack any military units in the province, or begin to occupy the province if it is a colhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ony without military protection. If the occhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/upation succeeds, which takes one month as usual, the settler population in the colony is reduced by −100 per regiment of natives, destroying the cohttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/lony if it reaches zero.
       After an uphttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/rising, whether successful or not, the native army disbands and the natives are guaranteed not to rise up again for one year ("Recent Native Uprising" modifier). After this period, thttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/he chance of an uprising returns to normalhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/.

Ferocity[edit | edit source]
       Ferocity icon.png Ferocity ranges from 0 to 10 and is independent of aggressiveness. Natives regiments in the province get Military tactics.png 0.2 military tactics per point of ferocity.

Units[edit | edit source]
       Native military strength remains at the equivalent of technology level 2 throughout the game, with weak units, 2.5 morale, and 100% discipline, only potentially boosted by the tactics bonus from ferocity (0.2 per point). Consequently, while small early-game armies can be seriously damaged or even defeated by large native populations − particularly if you yourself start at tech level 2 or lower! − mid- and late-game units will easily emerge victorious even outnumbered and low on morale.

Occupation[edit | edit source]

       Ambox outdated info.png

   Please help wihttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/th verifying or updating this section. It was last verified for version 1.3https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/3.
       During a war, a colony can be occupied lhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ike any province. The development of a colony through normal growth will continue unabated, but a colonist present in the province will be sent back to the colony's owner. An army standing in an occuphttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ied colony will have the option to Seize Colony for Military power.png 25 military power. Seizing a colony will make the aggressor (the nation that takes the colony) take an aggressive expansion hit, therefore decreasing relationshttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ with affected countries. The colony ownership will transfer thttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/o the nation that used the action. The colony will keep the culture and religion of the previous owner until a colonist from the new owner reaches the colony. The colony will cost its new owner money the same as if it had been colhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/onized by them, including the increasing costs of holding more colonies than the number of
       colonhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ists.
       An alternative option is the military action Burn Colony for Military power.png 5 military power. The colony is completely destroyed and the province becomes, once again, an uncolonized province.
       Since a colony keeps growing under occupation, it is possible that it will become a full colonial province while being occupied. Unless the 'Seize Colony' option was used earlier, the 'finished' province will belong to the original owner. This can be used to steal growing colonies to save war score for another action in the peace treaty or by non-colonizer natihttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ons to gain a colonial foothold.

Colonial provinces[edit | edit source]

       Ambox outdated info.png

   Please help with verifying or updating this section. It was last verhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ified for version 1.33.
       Once colonization is finished, a colony becomes a city with a territohttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/rial core. The owner will now be able to do anything that could bhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/e done with a normal territory, such as build buildings, recruit troops, build ships, and improve the province's development level. The nation will also now be able to trace coring and colonial range from it. The area can behttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ made a state and fully cored like any other province,https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ though the state upkeep is typically quite high due to distance from the capital.
       If the finished colony is in a colonial region and the countryhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/'s capital is not in a colonial region, the colonihttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/zing nation will retain control of the province until a total of 5 provinces are colonized (or conquered and made territorial cores) by that nation in the same colonial region. All provinces in the colonial region will then be ceded to a newly formed colonial nation, with the most developed province becoming the capital, and any cores converted to full cores of the colonial nation. Any fhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/urther provinces that are conquered (even if not cored) or colohttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/nized in that colonial region will be ceded to the colonial nation after one day. Territorial cores are still converted to full cores and state provinces are not immune, so making states in colonial regions is generally a waste of administrative phttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ower (unless the country's capital is itself
       in a colohttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/nial region).
       The provinces will generally keep the native religion and culture. They will change to the colonizer's (or that of a minority being ehttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/xpelled) when settlers first arrive, or when a colonishttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/t attracts additional settlers (i.e. the check for Colonist placement chance.png colonist chance succeeds), in the following situations:
         1. It is in North or South America,https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ or the random New World.
         2. It is anywhere else and neither Wealth of Nations.png /eu4.paradoxwikis.com/a> Wealth of Nations nor Dharma.png Dharma is active.
         3. The provihttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/nce has a land connection to the colonizer's capital and is on the same continent.
         4. The province has no religion or no culture (usually because it has no natives).
         5. Therhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/e are at least (natives − 100) settlers.
       The prohttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/vince will return to its native religion and culture if the colony is abandoned.
       Some important consequences follow from the above:
          + A Siberian frontier east of the Urals (i.e. in the continent https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/of Asia, rather than Russia's capital which is in Europe) willhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ not change culture and religion if it doesn't change as soon as it's established, because colonist chance does not apply there. The same is true if any different-continent old world colony grows without a colonist.
          + Provinces on another continent (besides the new world) with fewer than 1000 natives will usually change; those with about 1000 will change with a prhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/obability approximately equal to settler chance; and those with more usually will not change.
          + A same-continent colony established without a land connection may change later (but only via https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/settler chance) if a land connection is established.
          + Colonies that are conquered from another country will only change if a colonist is sent to them.
       Colonies, and provinces that became cities by colonization that are conquered from another country, do not cause overextension, even if left uncored. Provinces conquered from primitive countries (that weren't colonized, so including provinces settled by native tribes) causehttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ overextension as normal.

Colonial subject nations[https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/edit | edit source]https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/

       Ambox outdated info.png

   Please help with verifying or updating this section. It was last verified for version 1https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/.33.

                Main articles: Colonial nation, Trade company

       Colonial nations and trade companies are specialized subject nations that can be formed via colonization (or conquest of the appropriate regions). Understanding both types of colonial subject nations is key to benefitting from the colonization process.
       Using colonial nations or trade companies to produce and control trade value in nodes, as well as utilizing them to gain free merchahttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/nts or military control of overseas territories, are some of the benefits these subjects can provide a phttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/arent nation.
       With Wealth of Nations.png Wealth of Nations, a country gains Merchants.phttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ng +1https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ merchant for each trade company that controls the majority (>51%) of the provincial trade power in that region. (Non-trade company provinces in that region and sources of trade power other than directly from the provinces are not considered.)
       Apart frhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/om the 50% trade power they normally transfer to their overlord, each colonial nation comprising 10 or more provinces will provide their overlord with Global trade power.png +5% global trade power, an extra Merchants.png merchant, and variable amount of Naval fhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/orcelimit.png naval force limit, Land forcelimit.png land force limit, Saihttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/lors.png sailors and Manpower Icon.png manpower which depend on the size of the colonial nation and its designation. With the Leviathan.png Leviathan DLC, the subject relationship can be modified further to give different benefits to the colonial nation or its overlord.
       Accordingly large colonial nation subjects add significant military power to their ovhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/erlord and are therefore a potent weapon especially for smaller nations assuming such overlords maintahttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/in a sufficiently large fleet to control their subjects and manage their liberty desire.

Seven Cities of Gold and the Fountain of Youth[edit | /eu4.paradoxwikis.com/span>edit source]

                Main article: Seven Cities events

       With El Dorado.png El Dorado, using a Conquistador conquistador to explore terra incognita in a colonial region will sometimes trigger events based upon the search (and sometimes discovery!) of mythical locations in the New World. These events can provide monarch points, Gold Icon.png ducats or Prestige.png prestige and add flavor and occasionally material benefit to the exploration of the New World.
       Discovering a city gives a permanent province modifier with various local effects (except Cibola which gives Tax income.png +5 Yearly tax income), Gold Icon.png 800 ducats ( Gold Icon.png /eu4.paradoxwikis.com/a> 400 ducats for the medium outcome) and adds Tax Base Icon.png 4 base tax, Production.png 4 base production and Manpower Icon.png 4 base manpower to the province ( Tax Base Icon.png 2, Production.png 2, Manpower Icon.png 2 for the medium outcome).

Frontiers[edit | /eu4.paradoxwikis.com/a href="https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/index.php?title=Colonizatihttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/on&action=edit&section=31" title="Edit section: Frontiers">edit source]

       Third Rome.png [28px-Domination.png] Available only with the Third Rome DLC or the Domination DLC enabled.
       Frontiers (also called "Siberian frontier") are a uniquhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/e colonization system primarily for Flahttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/g of Russia Russia to model its rapid expansion into Siberia. Once a united Russia unlocks its second national idea, it mhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ay establish a Siberian Frontier colony in any empty province with a direct land connection to its capital passinhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/g through non-colony provinces. Establishing a frontier costs /eu4.paradoxwikis.com/a href="https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/Diplomatic_power" title="Diplomatihttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/c power"> Diplomatic power.png
       20 diplomatic power. The new colony will start with 5 settlers instead of the usual 10. Frontier provinces do not count towards the cohttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/lony limit or require monthly maintenance. They grow at a varying rate of /eu4.paradoxwikis.com/n class="effect-green">+5 – 15
       Local settler increase.png settlers per month, but since many Siberian Frontiers canhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ be established at the same time, https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ Flag of Russia Russia can reach the Pacific Ocean fairly quickly.
       A few misshttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ions give other countries individual colonies that grow https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/using the same system, though only Russia and custom nations, and countriehttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/s with the Great Mongol State/eu4.paradoxwikis.com/a> government reform (unlocked by forming the /eu4.paradoxwikis.com/n style="white-space:nowrap;"> Flag of Mongol Empire Mongol Empire/eu4.paradoxwikis.com/span>) may establish them in any connected province. A custom nation withhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ this ability in the New World can grow extremely rapidly.

Mouse controls tips[edit | edit source]

     * Right click on a province to go directly to diplomacy view
     * When at war, right click on the war emblem (bottom right shield symbol) to go directly to peace negotiation interface with the war leader (if there is a free diplomat)
     * Drag to select army
     * CTRL + drag to select ships over army
     * SHIFT + drag to add to selection
     * CTRL + right click to to transport troops by sea
     * SHIFT + right click to add a movement queue
     * Right click on a troop type in the reorganize army menu transfers half of the troops to the other army

Core

   From Europa Universalis 4 Wiki
   (Redirected from Coring)
   Jump to navigation Jump to search
   https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/

   Please help with verifying or updating older sections of this article.
   At least some were last verified for version 1.29.

   A core is a province that is considered a rightful part of a country. Cores give several strategically important benefits:
     * Provinces without a core add to overextension (except colonies^[1]), proport#cite_note-1">&[1&]), proportional to their development value.
     * A country will always have a casus belli if one of their core provinces is owned by another country.
     * Some missions or decisions require certain provinces to be cored
     * Core provinces get the following modifiers:

   Local tax modifier.png                                   +75%                              Local tax modifier
   Local mahttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/npower modifier.png +75%https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ Local manpower modifier
   Local sailors modifier.png                               +75%                              Local sailors modifier

   The followhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ing actions are not allowed in uncored provinces:
     * Developing
     * Exploit development
     * Moving the capital or main trading port to the province
     * Culture conversion
     * Recruiting non-mercenary units
     * Establishing a holy order (requires a full core)
     * Adding the province to the HRE
     * Create a trade post
     * Creating a state

   [ ]

States and territories[edihttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/t | edit source]

          Main article: States and territories

   States and territories are a new mechanic introduced in patch 1.16 intended to replace the old Overseas mechanic. The system introduces a 2-part coring process. A newly conquered province is considered as part of a territory (unless it already belongs to one of the nation's existing states). Turning a territory into a state requires that all owned provinces in thhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/e area be made "territorial cores" (which have a higher minimum auhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/tonomy, and are lost if the province is conquered); this costs half the base coring cost and takes the same amount of time. Once a state has been established, it is possible to instantaneously complete the coring process by paying the remaining coring costs. Administering development in states and territories costs governing capacity, which has a soft limit based on administrative technology.

Range[edit | edit source]

   Coring range is the same as colonial range, so it is often necessary to research diplomatic tech if expanding overseas without a land bridge. To check the range to a given province, change the map mode to "colonial range", and hover over the province of interest. The range will show, green for in range and red for out of range.

   The following ideas and policies increase colonial range:
   Range.png           Traditions                     Ideas           Bonuses Policies
   +50%      —
     * Exploration idea 3: Overseas Exploration

   —         —
   +40%      —
     * Hawaiian idea 7: Legendary Voyagers

   —         —
   +33%      —
     * Norwegian idea 1: The Call of our Forefathers

   —         —
   +25%      —
     * Livonian idea 5: Livonhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ian Colonization

     * Iwi idea 1: Sons of Kupe

   —         https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/��

   Colhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/onial range can also be increased by hiring a Navigator advisor. Note that navigator advisors can only appear if a couhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ntry has at least one Colonists.png colonist envoy.
   https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/
     * A country can core all provinces which have a land connection to the capitahttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/l (through owned and controlled provinces).
     * If a country has a core in province A, it can core every neighboring province. A doesn't have to be owned or controlled by that cohttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/untry.
     * If a country controls, owns and has a core in coastal province A, it chttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/an core every other coastal province that is within coring range. The ingame tooltip of rehttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/quiring an "unblockaded" province is wrong, blockades do not affect this.
     * If a cohttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/untry controls, owns and has a core in coastal province A, then it can core any province that has a "land bridge" of owned provinces to A and is within coring distance of A.
     * If a country's subject owns and has a core in province B, then the country can core any province C which is adjacent to B as long as C is not overseas for the country.
     * If a country's colonial nation owns and has a core in province C, then the country can core any province adjacent to C in all continents./eu4.paradoxwikis.com/li>

   The Imperial authority.png Holy Roman Emperor can core any province that belongs to the empire, regardless of where it is.

   The Age of Revolutions 'Unrestricted Conquest' splendor ability allows any province to be cored, regardless of range or connection. (requires Mandatehttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ of Heaven.png Mandate of Heaven).

   Tzintzuntzan at Great project level icon tier 3.png magnificient level allow to ignore coring distance.

Duration[edit | edit source]

   The base duration for coring is 36 months. All the coring-cost modifiers apply to the coring duration, except for administrative efficiency, innovativeness, and corruption. Claims apply in a different manner, as shown below.

   For example, it can be reduced by the following modifiers:
     * Adaptability idea −25% coring cost modifier
     * Country traditions or ideas thahttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/t reduce coring cost (Ottomans −20% for example)
     * Choosing Shiva as personal deity of a ruler of a Hindu nation −10% (only with Wealth of Nations.png Wealth of Nations DLC)
     * Tribal Government −5% per government rank

   Note: Hostile core-creation will not apply to coring duration.

   These modifiers above will stack additively.

   Having a claim of any type (temporary or permanent) will give a multiplicative reduction.
     * Province is claimed: −10%

   A further culture bonus may be applied multiplicatively.
     * Province in same culture group than primary culture: −50%
     * Province has promoted culture: −25%

   For example, if Rûm with Sultan al-Sharq wa al-Gharb (−20%) and Adaptability idea −25% is going to core a Greek (promoted culture) province with no claim, it will take 36 × (1 − 0.20 − 0.25) × (1 − 0.25) = 14 months to core.

   Note: Corhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ing takes a minimum of 6 months.

   Coring progress will be halted if the province is occupied by hostile forces or when the current owner is at war with any country that already has a core on the prohttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/vince. Progress will resume as soon as these conditions are lifted.

Restrictions[edit/eu4.paradoxwikis.com/a> | edit source]

   It is not possible to core a province:
     * Whihttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/le being at war with someone who also has a core in that province. The ongoing core creation will tehttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/mporarily halt if this happens.
     * While there is a missionary converting the province.https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/
     * While a building is being constructed in the province.
     * While the culture of the province is being changed.
     * Province is occupied (Progress halts, will resume if unoccupied).
     * Province is undhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/er siege (Progress halts, will resume if siege is lifted).

   Once the coring process has been started, failing the adjacency, range or land connection requirements does not revert the coring process. Coring will proceed as originally schedulhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ed. As well, gaining or losing cost modifiers or development while coring does not change the Administrative power.png cost originally deducted nor the coring duration originally scheduled.

Gaining cores through other means[edit | edit source]

   In addition to coring newly acquired provinces manually, a nation can also gain cores by diplo-annexation of vassals or integrating a junior partner of a#Incorporation_or_inheritance" title="Personal union">integrating a junior partner of a personal union. Both processes automatically give cores on all provinces of the acquired territory, making the strategy of "feeding" vassals with uncored provinces a viable strategy to save monarch points, especially Administrative power.png administrative power. However, provinces cored this way begin with high local autonomy and will be relatively unproductive for some time, depending on government type.

   When a colony becomes a city, its owner gains a free territorial core on it. https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/If the owner has a colonial nation in the same colonial region (or becomes eligible for one with the colony finished), the core is instantly granted to the colonihttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/al nation instead (and ceded to it).

   If a nation is occupying a province of their religion which is owned by a nation of a dihttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/fferent religion, they have a small chance of gaining the provincehttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ as a core; a full core, even if the province is in a territory. If the province is owned by a Tengri nation who has syncretized its faith, the event can still fire.

   Certain decisions can also give cores on specific provinces. For example, the Ottoman decision "Make Constantinople cahttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/pital" gives the ottomans a free core on Conshttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/tantinople.

Coring costs[edit | edit source]

   Ambox outdated info.png /eu4.paradoxwikis.com/d class="mbox-text" style="">
   Please help with verifying or updating this section. It was last verified for version 1.29.

Base costs[edit | edit source]

   Coring is an action which costs Administrative power.png administrative monarch points. The base cost depend on the Development.png development of the province. For each point of development, the coring cost is 10^[2] Administrative power.png administrative monarch points.

   Modifiers are summed before being applied, except the modifiers from administrative efficiency and being a territory, which are applied multiplicatively after the additive modifiers are applied.

   Note: The minimum coring cost for a province before applying multiplicative modifiers is 20% of its coring cost, or 2 Administrative power per development, up to 30 development. Even with a −100% modifier on a province, the cost is still 20% of the coring cost. Also the maximum coring cost is capped at 30 development for a province. Thttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/his means that if the province has 31 development, its coring cost will be treated as if it only had 30 development.

Hostile core-creation[edit | edit source]

   The national ideas listed below increase coring costs for a province with a core from a nation which possesses this modifier. The increase applies even if the nation with the core does not exist. These modifiers are taken into account by the AI when making decisions on which nation to attack.
                                   Enemy core creation.png                                  Traditions Ideas Bonuses Policies
   In patch 1.37 no ideas and policies have the modifier “hostile core-creation cost on us”

Losihttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ng cores[edit | edit source]

   Ambox outdated info.png
   Please help with verifying or updating this section. It was last verified for version 1.29.

   When negotiating a peace deal, some of the loser's cores may no longer exist afterwards:
     * As mentioned above, territorial cores in a province disappear if the province changes hands. This will happen even if the losing nation is the primary culture of the provinces https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/being lost.
     * The loser can be forced to 'revoke their core' on any province they do not own and that is not of their primary culture (unless the victor owns that province and hasn'thttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ cored it themselves - probably a restriction to make working around hostile coring cost increases more difficult).
     * If the loser is forced to 'release a nation', or 'return a core' to a third nation, their cores on all provinces not of their primary culture disappear.https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/
     * If a country is entirely destroyed, it loses all cores in provinces not of its primary culture group.

   Cores in uncontrolled provinces will disappear some time after the most recent of these events:
     * The owner of the core lost ownershttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/hip of the province.
     * A war between the current owner and the nation owning the core was fought.

   The time to lose a core depends on the province's culture relative to the core:^[3]
     * If the core is the primary nation for that province culture,https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ or belongs to a nation that is a subject of the current owner, it will never expire.
     * If the core shares a culture group with the province culture, the base expiration duration is 150 years, else 50 years.
     * This amount of time is affected by the current owner's Absolutism.png absolutism, scaling up to 50% reduced duration at 100 absolutism.
     * Changing the culture in a province changes the length of the core decay timer. If a change to the length of the core decay timer means that the core would already have disappeared, then the core disappears.

   Other ways to lose cores:
     * A nation can abandon a core on a province that it doesn't own (a player can do this with a button Revoke Core Icon.png on the province view. However, this action also costs some https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/"Prestige.png" prestige.
     * When a nation sells a province, they lose both the province and core. However, this action also costs some Prestige.png prestige.
     * When a nation releasehttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/s a vassal from owned provinces, or cancels an existing subject's vashttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/salage, they lose all cores in that subject's provinces.

Uncontested coreshttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/[edit | edit sourchttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/e]

   https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/

   A country has uncontested cores when it has cores on provinces thttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/hat are owned by (part of) other countries without being at wahttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/r or in a truce with those countries. They are a drain on a country's prestige: a yearlhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/y decrease of −0.1 prestigehttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ for each core province being held by another nation. Due to thttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/his prestige loss, it may be a good idea to recover such core provinces, especihttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ally if the provincial culture is already accepted in your nation. /eu4.paradoxwikis.com/p>

   This is the interface for dealing with the player's nation or a foreign nation. The player access his/her ohttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/wn nation's interface by clicking the shield (with the player's nation's name next to it) in the upper left corner. A popup will appear undhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/erneath the shield, displaying several tabs with unique information. In general, hovering over an interface item produces a tooltip givinghttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ further information; in particular, tooltips for numbers generally describe what the number represents, where the it comes from and ihttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ts current effects.

   This tab gives an overview of the country's situation.
     * 1: Rulers :
          + Current ruler, heir, consort and their stats, with information about royal marriages and succession in ruler's tooltips.
          + Ruler personalities and timers showing when the next will be assigned.
          + Abdicate and disinherit buttons.
     * 2: Hired advisor/eu4.paradoxwikis.com/a>(s) and their stats and modifiers:
          + Advisor religion and culture (details in tooltihttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ps).
          + Portrait, with a tooltip describing the type of advisor.
          + The advisor's skill and name.
          + Buttons to promote and fire the advisor. (Promotion requires /eu4.paradoxwikis.com/g alt="Cradle of Civilization.png" src="images/thumb/2/23/Cradle_of_Civilization.png/18px-Cradle_of_Civilization.png" decoding="async" loading="lazy" width="18" height="18" data-file-width="42" data-fihttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/le-height="42" /> Cradle of Civilization.)
          + The bonus provided by the advisor
          + The advisor's monthly salary
          + The advisor's age, with a tooltip showing the yearly chance of the advisor dying

   This tab gives an overview of the country's government and cultures.
     * 1: Government information:
          + Government form, type and rank.
          + Strengthen government button.
          + Absolhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/utism.png Absolutism and Maximum absolutism https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ maximum absolutism. (Displays "?" before the Age of Absolutism.)
          + Gohttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/vernment specific mechanics. (Requires specific DLC depending on the country played. Example: Res Publica.png Res Publica for the Netherlands or Third Rome.png Third Rome for Russia.)
     * 2: Country modifiers. A button in the top right opens a list giving the value of all bonuses and maluses applying to the country as a whole (e.g. Advisor Costs, Improve Relations).
     * 3: List of accepted and non-accepted cultures, with the possibility to prhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/omote or to demote a culture.

Tab domestic economy.png Echttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/onomy[edit | edit source]

   This tab shows an overview of your country's economy.
     * The country's balance sheet, showing income and expenses. Each is divided into categories; individual income or expense items can be seen in tooltips.
     * Inflation reduction.png Inflation: a graph of recent changes, an indicator of its current level and whether it's currently going up or down, and a button to spend Administrative power.png administrative power to reduce it.
     * War exhaustion.png War exhaustion and total Development.png development
     * Loans: buttons to take a loan (indicating how much money you will get), to repay one loan at a time, and to repay as many loans as possible.

Tab domestic tradhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/e.png Trade[edit/eu4.paradoxwikis.com/an class="mw-editsection-divider"> | edit source]

   This tab shows all information relating to trade.
     * National values affecting trade
     * Current trade income, with a pie chart showing what proportion of the country's total income this represents
     * This country's embargoes on others (indicating the effect on trade efficiency), embargoes by others on this country, and countries transferring trade power to this country
     * Information on all known tradehttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ nodes, with buttons to send merchants on missions.

Tab domestic ideas.png Ideas[edit | edit source]

   This tab shows your country's national ideas and idea groups.
     * National traditionhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/s and (if they've been unlocked) ambitions. Details are in a tooltip.
     * National ideas, unlocked from left to right, along with a progress bar showing progress towards the next nationahttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/l idea (3 each, one per idea from an idea group).
     * Idea groups: either a button allowing you to choose a new idea (or look at one, if the slot isn't available) or, for active groups:
          + Icon indicating the category of idea group: Administrative power.png administrative, Diplomatic power.png diplomatic or Military power.png military
          + Name of the group, whttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ith a tooltip showing possible policies when this group is fully unlocked
          + A button allowing abandonment of the idea group
          + A lightbulb icon, which is either dark or lit to indicate whether the group's bonus is active, and ahttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ tooltip to show what it is
          + A list of ideas, from left to right. When one is available to unlock, it will turn into a button.
          + Bar showing progress in accumulated power of the relevant category tohttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/wards the amount required for the next idea

   UI tab missions.png

Mission.png Missions/eu4.paradoxwikis.com/pan class="mw-editsection">[https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/edit | edit source/eu4.paradoxwikis.com/a>]

This tab shows your country's mission tree. The one shown here is for Flag of Russia Russia; other countries have different mission trees.
     * Each mission has:
          + A question mark icon with a tooltip giving the requirements for the mission to be fulfilled.
          + The country's coat of arms, if the mission is unique to that country (or a group of countries that includes it).
          + A Prestige.png prestige or Yes tick icon with a tooltip giving the effects of the mission when completed. This has a sunburst highlight if the mission can be taken now.
          + Hovering over the mission image gives its description.
     * Missions are joined together with arrows. If an arrow leads from mission A to mission B, then A must be completed before B can be completed. A mission is greyed out if its prerequisite missions have not beenhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ completed.

   UI tab decisions.png

Decision.png Policies and Decisions[edit | edit source]

   Ambox outdated info.png
   Please help with verifying or uhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/pdating this section. It was last verified for version 1.30.

   This tab shows potential policies and decisions that you may enact.
     * Policies:
          + A grid with 3 rows which allows you to choose up to 3 policies from each type ( [Administrative_power.png] Administrative, [Diplomatic_power.png] Diplomatic, Military power.png Military) or more with the right modifiers. Clicking on any box brhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ings up an interface to add policies. Right-clicking on an assigned policy allows you to revoke it. On the left of the grid is shown the max amount of policies of each type and the amount of monarch points used https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/up by policies monthly.
          + Country modifiers from enacted policies.
     * List of decisions:
          + Decisions that can be taken now are at the top, in alphabetical ordehttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/r.
          + "Important" decisions are prioritised and highlighted https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/with green instead of blue scrolls.
          + Hovering over the name gives a description.
          + When a decision can be taken an alert will be displayed. A toggle herhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/e allows you to disable the alert for that mission.
          + A question mark icon has a tooltip giving the requirements to take the decision.
          + The envelope shows the effects of that decision when hovering and also acts as a button to take the decision if https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/it isn't greyed out.

   UI tab stability.png

Tab domestic stability.png Stability and Expansion[edit | edit source]

   This tab shows information relating to the internal situation of the country.
     * War exhaustion.png War exhaustion:
          + Current level, with a bar showing progress towards the maximum of 20, and a tooltip showing its current effects
          + An arrow indicating whether it's going up or down or stayinghttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ level
          + A button to spend Diplomatic power.png diplomatic power to reduce it
     * A list of possible disasters
     * Icon stability.png Stability:
          + Current level, from -3 to +3
          + A button to spend Administrative power.png administrative power to increase it
     * Overextensionhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/.png Overextension:
          + The current level of Administrathttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ive efficiency.png administrative efficiency
          + The current level of overextension
          + A button to handle overextension (by coring provinces causing it)
     * A section relating to colonial expansion:
          + Current Range.png colonial range
          + Current Global colonialhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ growth.png global settler increase
          + Three buttons to set the country's native policy (greyed out if the country has no colonists). (Requires The Cossacks.png The Cossacks)
     * Rebels and possible rebels:
          + A bar showing the rebels' progress towards breaking the country
          + National unrest.png National unrest
          + A list of rebel factions in those provinces in the country that have either unrest or revolt progress:
               o Name of and symbol for the rebel faction (separatist rebels use the relevant country's coat of arhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ms instead)
               o The faction's demands
               o Progress towards the next uprising
               o "Handle them!" button, which shows the faction's demands in greater detail and gives options for dealing with it: accept demands, boost stability, harsh treatment, or coring relevant provinces.

   This tab gives all relevant information relating to religion in the country.
     * Top left: a button that enables the player to change the country's state religion, if permitted and posshttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ible.
     * Religion name and icon.
     * List ohttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/f the religion's general effects.
     * Tolerance towards Tohttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/lerance own.png the true fahttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ith, Tolerance heretic.png heretics, and Tolerance heathen.png heathens.
     * Mid left: details of the https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/state religion. What is shown here varies based on the specific religion.
     * Mid right: Defender of the Faith. This shows which country is currently Defender of the Faith for thttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/he state religion, if any and which level of bonuses the defendhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/er of faith has (based on the number of countries of that religion). It is also a button allowing the country to become Defender of the Faith, if possible.
     * Below religion-sphttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ecific details on the left is an indicator of current religious unity and your Global missionary strength.png missionary strength
     * Below that is a list of provinces that are not of the state religion: name, province religion, time to convert at current Global missionary strength.png missionary strength, and a button to send a missionary.

Tab domestic military.png Military[edit | edit source]

   This tab gives all information relating to the country's military situation.
     * Professihttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/onalism, with icons at each 20% increment; tooltips show its currhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ent effects. (Requires Cradle of Civilization.https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/png Cradle of Civilization)
     * List of land units: fromhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ top to bottom, Infantry.png infantry, Cavhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/alry.png https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ cavalry and Artillery.png artihttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/llery.
          + Name. This is also a button allowing you to change the currently active unit type.
          + Gold Icon.png Recruitment cost, combat ability, Icon fire.png fire and Icon shock.png shock values, and number https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/of regiments of that type currently raised (including mercenaries).
