   UI tab subjects.png

Tab domestic subject.png Subjects[edit | edit source]

   This tab contains everything the player needs to know about the country's subjects, if it has any. Most of the interface is taken up by a list of subjects. The columns are as follows:
     * The vassal's coat of arms.
     * An icon indicating the type of subject, for example Personal union.png personal union.
     * The subect's name/eu4.paradoxwikis.com/li>
     * The subject's opinion of the overlord
     * Monhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/thly income from the subject, if they provide any (i.e. vassals and colonial subjects)
     * Global tariffs.png Tariff efficiency (for colonial subjects)
     * Liberty desire.png /eu4.paradoxwikis.com/a> Liberty desire
     * Number of army regiments
     * Whether the subject provides a bonus Merchants.png merchant (for colonial https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/subjects and trade companies)
     * Subject interactions - a button bringing up a menu showing the available interactions

   At the botthttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/om are details of income from vassals and colonial subjects. Finally, at the bottom right are buttons allowing the player to change subjects' military focuhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/s or release a colonial subject.
   UI tab estates.png

Tab domestic estates.png Estates[edit | edit source]

   This tab contains all information on estates. The first row contains:
     * Land distribution between estates and crown
     * Effects from current crownland percentage and buttons for estate interactions
     * Current agenda

   Every estate is then shown in more detail. Every box contains:
     * The estate's icon
     * The estate's name
     * Current loyalty (equilibrium https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/is shown in the tooltip)
     * Current influence
     * Current country modifier from estate (not including effects from privileges) /eu4.paradoxwikis.com/>The currently assigned privileges of that estate plus an empty field to add new ones up to a maximum of 4 (Note: it is currently possible to have more than 4 privileges for an estate by assigning them at once, but that is subhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ject to change)

   Culture groups in 1444
   Individual cultures in 1444

   Culture icon.png Culture as represented in EU4 is the representation of the local populaces on a provincial level. The culture represents the combination of the local language, customs, ethnicity and nationality of the people. Religion is split from this list, as it is represented by provincial religion whihttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ch has a separate representation in the game.

   The cultures of EU4 are divided in culture groups consisting of multiple cultures which have simihttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/lar customs, have a similar language or have a shared history. EU4 has a total of 72 culture groups with multiple different cultures as represented with the twohttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ maps to the right.

Primary culture/eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ class="mw-editsection-bracket">[edit | edit source]

   /eu4.paradoxwikis.com/tr> Ambox outdated info.png
   Please help with verifying or updating this section. It was last verified for version 1.29.

   All countries have one primary culture. This is normally fixed, although it can be changed either through the culture mechanics or via certain national decisions. The main interaction of the nation with local culture is by spending diplomacy points Diplomatic power.png .
   /eu4.paradoxwikis.com/h3>Cultural shift[edit | edit source]

   Any accepted culture that has at least 50% of the development of the country’s state cores can be promoted to the primary culture of the nation. This costs 100 Diplomatic power.png diplomatic power, and replaces the previous ‘Accept Cultural Shift’^[1] decision. The previou#91;1&]
   decision. The previous primary culture will consequently become an accepted culture.

   The country cannot shift to a culture that is accepted due to the culturahttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/l union granted by Empire level government. Shifting the culture to outside the players cultural union shifts the cultural union, enabling the player to shift back to the preferred culture in the original cultural union.

   It can be advantageous for a player to set a new primary culture to be able to form a country with a different tag (with new national ideas), or to be in a larger culture group, to have more brother cultures and save promoted culture slots.

   If the nation has very few states active, it can state and de-state provinces to frequently change the primary culture to obtain Nationalism casus belli on more countries, as well as to reduce the time of coring.

Culture group shift[edit | edit source]

   Originally only available via Sinicization, the game has included several ways to switch the groups a certain culture belongs to. Mechanically this is achieved by converting all provinces of the original culture to a new (usually sihttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/milarly named) culture, which is part of a different grhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/oup. The following is a list of all cultures that can shift what group they belong to and how:
     * Korean to Sino- Korean, switches from Korean to Chinese group. Via the "Sinhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/icize our Culture" decision.
     * Oirat, Khalkha, Mongol and Korchin cultures to Sino-Altaic, switches from Altaic to Chinese group. Via forming Flag of Yuan Yuan (can be formedhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ by any Altaic culture nation but shifts only the four mentionedhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ cultures).
     * All Tibetan group cultures to Sino-Tibetan, switches from Tibetan to Chinese group. Via the "Sinicize our Culture" decision.
     * Vietnamese to Sino- Vietnamese, swhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/itches from Mon-Khmer to Chinese group. Via the "Sinicize our Culture" decision.
     * Zhuang to Sino- Zhuang, switches from Tai to Chinese group. Via the "Sinicize our Culture" decision.
     * Jurchen to Manchttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/hu, switches from Evenki to Chinese group. Via forming Flag of Manchu Manchu.
     * Georgian to Greco-Georgian, switches from Caucasian to Greek group. Via Flag of Georgia Georgias "Throne of the Romans" or Flag of Trebizond Trebizonds "Georgian Union" mhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ission
     * All British group cultures to Anglois, switches from British to French group. Via the Flag of Angevin Kingdom Angevin Kingdoms "The https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/Angevin Culture" mission (Shifts only all owned and subjects owned provinces).
     * Bosnian, Bulgarian, Byelorussian, Croatian, Czech, Muscovite, Novgorodian, Polish, Ruthenian, Ryazanian, Serbian, Silesian, Slovak, Slovene and Sorbian switch from West Slavic, East Slavic anhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/d South Slavic to Slavic group. Via the Flag of Russia Russian "Protect the South Slavs" mission (All cultures keep their names in game and are only renamed internally).
     * Turkish, Azerbaijani and Turkmenihttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ to Turco-Iranian, switches from Levantine, Iranian and Altaic to Iranian group. Via the [20px-Aq_Qoyunlu.png] Aq Qoyunlu https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ Flag of Qara Qoyunlu Qara Qoyunlu "Shahanshas of Eranshahr" missihttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/on (Shifts only all owned provinces of the three mentioned cultures).
     * Gothic switches from Byzantine to Germanic group. Potentially via [20px-Theodoro.png] Theodoros "A Merchhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ant's Family Home" mission. (Culture keeps its name in game and is only renamed internally).

   https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/

Unique Mechanics[edit | edit source]

   Mhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/any cultures have governments, events, missions, decisions, and naval doctrines associated with them. In addition,https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ some cultures also have unique mechanics at their disposal. These are:
     * Holy orders, which are available to Iberian Catholicism Catholic and Andalusian Piety Muslim nations
     * Possible Manchu banners.png Banners, which are available to Jurchen, Manchu, and Sino-Althttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/aic nations.
     * Has samurai.png Samurai, which are available to Japanese nations.
     * Marathas estate.png The Marathas Estate, which is available to Indian technology group Indian Sinhalese Nations and Indian technology group Indian Nations in the Dravidian or Western Aryan culture group (except Malvi or Rajasthani)
     * Rajputs.png The Rajputs Estate, which is available to Indian technology group Indian Malvi and Rajasthani Nations as well as Indian technology group Indian Nations ihttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/n the Hindustani, Central Indian or Eastern Aryan culture grhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/oup (except Sinhalese)

Accepted cultures [edit | edit source]

   Ambox outdated info.png
   Please help with verifying or updating this section. It was last verified for version 1.25.
   Government interface

   The playerhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ has the ability to promote a culture to make it accepted or to demote it, removing ithttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ from accepted cultures.
     * The player can promote any culture in their nation that has at least 20 cored development in a state. It costs 100 Diplomatic https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/power.png diplomatic power, but it could be advantageous in the long run.
     * Demoting a culture from 'ahttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ccepted cultures' costs 10 diplomatic and adds +5 National unrest.pnhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/g unrest in all provinces with that culture, thhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/at will decay over time.

   The cost in to promote cultures can be reduced by the following:
   Promote culture cost.png Traditions                  Ideas                   Bonuses Policies
   −30%                     —
     * Administrative idea 4: Cultural Regulations

   /eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ style="text-align:center">—
   —
   −25%                     —
     * California Native idea 1: Division as a Strength

   If the number of possible promoted cultures is reduced (e.g.:removing a polihttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/cy) and there are now more accepted cultures than possible accepted cultures, 1 culture that was most recently accepted will be demoted at the end of the month. Unlike manual demotion, this will neither cost diplomatic points nor create unrest in affected provinces.

Culturhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/al union[edit | edit source]

   Cultural unions will automatically acchttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ept all sub-cultures within their respective culture group. Any nation can become a cultural union of its culture group upon reaching the Empire rank Empire government rank, or Development.png 1000 development. As part of this change, it ihttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/s possible for several nations to be a cultural union for the same culture group. A nation can become https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/an empire as part of a mission, decision, event, reaching a certain development level or by upgrading the government rank; cultural unions make it so that sister cultures don't have to be promoted to be accepted by the country.

Culture conversion[edit | edit source]

   The culture of a province can be changed to another culture if the province is cored by its owner, has the same religion as its owner (for Confucianism Confucian, harmonized religions work as well), and has no unrest from separatism. The cost for converting culture is Diplomatic power.png 10 diplomatic power per development^[2]#91;2&] and the duration for the change https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/to take place is 10 months per development.^[3] Like coring costs, culture conversion coshttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ts are capped at 30 development, so improving a 30 development province will not increase the cost of converting its culture. Sieges and occupations will pause culture conversion https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/but will not cancel it; the culture conversion will continue as soon as https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/the province is liberated, although conversion will be cancelled if the province's ownership changes. If the conversion is cancelled before progress reaches 10%, all diplomatic
   points whttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ill be refunded.

   A province can have its culture changed to the primary culture of the province's owner. With The Cossacks.pnhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/g The Cossacks, a province's culture can also be changed to any ownehttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/d neighbouring province's culture or its culture can be restored to whatever it was originally.

   Converhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ting a province from culture A to culture B will incur a relations hit with every country whose primary culture is culture A.

Primary nhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ation[edit | edit source]

   Most cultures have a primary nation. These nation will keep uncontested cores indefinitely^[8], so long as their cores are in provinces of their culture -https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ culture conversion will force these cores to obey the normal 50/150 year expiry timers for cores depending on whether or not the new culture is the same culture group as the https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/nation with a core there. Additionally the primary nation is https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/the default separatists target of a province if no other valid target exist even with no core on it. Primary nations of each culture can be found in the list below.

Lost cultures[edit | edit source]

   Ambox outdated info.png
   Please help https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/with verifying or updating this section. It was last verified for version 1.33.

   Cultures in the Lost Cultures group do not exist at game start, but can be created as custom nations or duringhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ the invasion. The only Lost Culture that can be re-discovered is the Roman culture by Restoring the Roman Empire that changes the primary culture of the nation. All provinces with a culture in the culture group of the former natihttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/on's primary culture will change to Roman culture. Howeverhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ you can change to any Lost Culture using console commands, by typing in the console "change_culturehttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/_court ruler [Culture]" then typing "event culture_religion_events.22" this will fire an event with one of the options being changing the nation's primary culthttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ure to the ruler's culture.

   Other cultures that do not exist athttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ game start can sometimes be created by event, such as the Return of the Norse culture, emergent colonial culturehttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/s in Colonial Nations for American, Mexican, and Brazilian culture, and Anglois for those who restore the Angevin Kingdom. However, these are not in the Lost Cultures culture group (though Norse was formerly in it)

Culture groups[edit | edit source]

   Note that culture groups are not just based on linguistic criteria - for example, Romanian is grouped https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/with the Carpathian cultures due to cultural similarities and for gameplay purposes, even though Carpathian is not a linguistic family.

   Primary nhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ations of each culture are listed to the right of each culture.

   With Domination.png Domination there exists a additional culture group - Slavic. It cahttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/n be founded via the Russian missions and combines ahttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ll cultures of the East Slavic, West Slavic and South Slavic groups, except albanian, into one group.

Development

   From Europa Universalis 4 Wiki
   Jump to navigation Jump to search

   Please help with verifying or updating older sections of this article.
   At least some were last verified for version 1.24.

   Development.png Development is a province attribute, which replaces the former system of static base tax and manpower. There are three kinds of development in a province - base tax, production, and manpower, corresponding to administrative, diplomatic and military power respectively. Players can increase province development values (directly or subject owned) by using monarch power.

   Province development is involved in some Age Objectives:
     * Having a cored province with at least 30 development is an objective in the Age of Discovery.
     * Having a total development of at least 100 while the nation's capital is not in Europe, Asia and Africa is another objective in the Age of Discovery.
     * Having a capital with at least 50 development is an objective in the Age of Revolutions.
     * Having a subject with at least 250 development is another objective in the Age of Revolutions.

   Base development
   [ ]

Effects of development[edit | edit source]

   Ambox outdated info.png
   Please help with verifying or updating this section. It was last verified for version 1.24.

Provincial level[edit | edit source]

   A province gains per development level in:

   Tax Base Icon.png Base tax:
   Local recruitment time.png     −2% Local recruitment time
   Great project upgrade time.png −1% Local great project upgrade time
   Local construction time        −1% Local construction time
   Local institution spread.png   +2% Local institution spread

   Gold Icon.png +1 yearly tax income base

   Production.png Production:
   Local goods produced        +0.2 Local goods produced
   Local shipbuilding time.png −1%  Local shipbuilding time

   Local manpower modifier.png Manpower:
   Garrison growth.png +1% Garrison growth

   Manpower Icon.png +250 maximum manpower

   Irrespective of category, every point of development has the following effects on the individual province (note that only coastal provinces get sailor and naval force limit bonuses):
   Possible number of buildings.png                                    +0.1%  Possible number of buildings
   Supply limit modifier                                               +2%    Supply limit modifier
   Local missionary strength.png                                       −0.1%  Local missionary strength
   Land forcelimit.png                                                 +0.1%  Land force limit
   Naval forcelimit.png                                                +0.1%  Naval force limit
   Sailors.png                                                         +60%   Sailors
   Local trade power.png                                               +0.2%  Local trade power
   Possible Manchu banners (local)                                     +0.066 Possible Manchu banners
   Possible cawa (local)                                               +0.125 (unrecognized string “Possible Cawa infantry” for Template:DLC only)
   (unrecognized string “possible carolean (local)” for Template:Icon) +0.1%  (unrecognized string “Possible Carolean infantry” for Template:DLC only)
   (unrecognized string “possible hussars (local)” for Template:Icon)  +0.01  (unrecognized string “Possible Hussars” for Template:DLC only)
     * Development cost.png +3% local development cost per point above 10 total development. This increase rises by 3% every 10 total development (+6% at 20, +9% at 30, etc.).
     * Province war score cost.png +1% Province warscore cost
     * Overextension.png +1% Province overextension value
     * Core creation.png +10 Core creation cost
     * Diplomatic annexation cost +8 Diplomatic annexation cost
     * Culture icon.png Increases the percentage of the local province culture in the player's nation.
     * Institutions.png Increases the institution presence in the province by (new development level/6). This is capped at +10% increase.
     * Institutions.png Most institution spread modifiers scale linearly with province development.

     * Removes 5% Devastation icon.png devastation（with adjustment based on local autonomy).

   Development.png Development levels over 30 no longer contribute to higher coring and culture conversion costs. For every 10 levels of development, a province gets an additional building slot.

National level[edit | edit source]

     * A nation gains Caravan power.png +1 caravan power for each 3 total development, up to 50.
     * A nation cannot be vassalized diplomatically if total development is more than 100 (−1000 reasons).
     * The base cost of annexation of a nation (before modifiers) is Diplomatic power.png 8 diplomatic power per development of the vassal nation.
     * If the nation's government type allows for rank increases, having 300/1000 development Development.png is part of the requirement of becoming a kingdom Kingdom rank /empire Empire rank respectively.

Developing a province[edit | edit source]

   Development cost tooltip.

   Monarch points ( Administrative power.png , Diplomatic power.png or Military power.png ) can be used to increase base tax, production, and manpower values, respectively. A province's base tax, production or manpower cannot be increased if its value is already more than that of the other two combined (for example, if the province's production and manpower are 1 each, then the base tax can not be raised above 3 and only an improvement of production or manpower is possible). In other words, the cap for one development type is equal to the sum of the other 2 plus 1.

   Developing a province this way increases the crownland by 0.2% per click.

Development formula[edit | edit source]

   Development cost modifier Development Cost Modifier: 0% by default, alters the base cost (50 before being modified). This modifier is uncapped.

   Development cost.png Development Cost: 0% by default, impacts the cost to develop the province, capped at −90%.

   Local development cost modifier Local development cost modifier and Local development cost Local development cost work exactly the same as their non-local counterparts, they exist purely as to distinguish global vs province-based modifiers.

   The minimum cost of developing a province rounds down, with interesting implications described below. The final cost can be 0, but it can not become negative even with more than Development cost modifier −100% Development Cost Modifier.

Development cost[edit | edit source]

Development cost increase[edit | edit source]

   The Local development cost Local Development Cost to develop provinces increases by +3% per point above 9 total development, +3% per point above 19 total development, and so on.

   For example, a province upgrading from total development level 32 to 33 will have a total Local development cost Local Development Cost of:

   23 * 3% = 63% (23 levels above 9)

   13 * 3% = 33% (13 levels above 19)

   3 * 3% = 9% (3 levels above 29)

   63% + 33% + 9% = 105%

   This amount is added on top of the other Local development cost Local Development Cost and Development cost.png Development Cost.
   Stacking development cost modifiers map including trade center, climate, terrain and goods. Colors range from red (expensive development) to green (cheap development) with yellow for no modification. Amsterdam, Baghdad, Cairo, London, Lublin, Macedonia, Milan, Prague, Regensburg, Warszawa and Wroclaw are excellent in these respects.

Exploiting development[edit | edit source]

   Ambox outdated info.png
   Please help with verifying or updating this section. It was last verified for version 1.24.
   Cradle of Civilization.png Available only with the Cradle of Civilization DLC enabled.

   A province can be exploited for short-term benefits by permanently reducing its development by 1.
     * Exploit Tax Base Icon.png Base Tax to gain 60 months worth of that province's tax income
     * Exploit Production.png Production to gain 60 months worth of that province's sailors
     * Exploit Manpower Icon.png Base Manpower to gain 60 months worth of that province's manpower

   A province has to have at least 2 development in a category for it to be exploitable, and is required to have at least a territorial core. A province cannot be exploited within the 20 years following its last exploitation, even if it changes owners.

Settlement growth[edit | edit source]

   Ambox outdated info.png
   Please help with verifying or updating this section. It was last verified for version 1.33.
   Dharma.png Available only with the Dharma DLC enabled.

   It is also possible to develop provinces by promoting settlement growth in colonized provinces or cities. By placing the colonist on the little empty window to the top right of the province overview screen, the colonist will automatically start to improve the province. The development of that province will have a certain chance of increasing by 1 in a random category after each yearly tick in accordance to when you started to promote settlement growth. The chance of the colonist improving the base development is based on the amount of development in the province. This chance is also affected by Local Development Cost modifiers such as terrain, Universities, Expand Infrastructure, and local modifiers like those temporarily granted by events. The Settlement Growth mechanic is not affected by Global Settler Increase, New Settlers Chance, or any global development cost reductions.

   The subject interaction "Block Settlement Growth" allows the overlord to prohibit a subject from using their colonist in this way, and instantly cancels any ongoing settlement growth.

Concentrate development[edit | edit source]

   Ambox outdated info.png
   Please help with verifying or updating this section. It was last verified for version 1.33.
   Leviathan.png Available only with the Leviathan DLC enabled.

   Provinces in territories you own, or states controlled by a non-tributary subject, can be used to concentrate development in the Capital.png capital. This can be done on the state interface by selecting the Concentrate development.png concentrate development button. Some of the development from provinces in the state is turned into monarch power, which is then used to develop the capital. The tooltip over the concentrate development button shows the amount of monarch points, and the amount of development that will be gained (this usually displays higher than the actual result, explained below). Concentrate development will not be available if there is not enough development to produce enough monarch points to develop the capital.

   Concentrating development in a subject will increase their Liberty desire.png liberty desire by +3 and decrease relations by −8 per point of development taken.

Calculation[edit | edit source]

   The amount of Tax Base Icon.png base tax , Production.png production, or Manpower Icon.png base manpower removed from a province when concentrating is
   [MATH: <semantics> <mrow class="MJX-TeXAtom-ORD"> <mstyle displaystyle="false" scriptlevel="0"> <mrow class="MJX-TeXAtom-ORD"> <mfrac> <mtext>Development category</mtext> <mn>5</mn> </mfrac> </mrow> </mstyle> </mrow> <annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{\textstyle {\frac {\text{Development category}}{5}}}</annotation> </semantics> :MATH]
   {\textstyle {\frac {\text{Development category}}{5}}} rounded to the nearest whole number. For example a 3/2/2 province would become a 2/2/2 (−1/−0/−0) because only the first category rounds to at least 1. By the same logic, 13/7/4 would become 10/6/3 (−3/−1/−1). This also means if a state has no provinces with more than 2 development in any category, it cannot be used to concentrate development.

   The amount of monarch points generated from development is equal to the development cost of the province. However the calculation is redone after each development category in the order tax → production → manpower. What this means is that an 8/8/8 province with a development cost of 80, will not get 6 x 80 total points but instead get 2 × 80 + 2 × 74 + 2 × 68 total points. As a result Administrative power.png administrative will receive the most points, followed by Diplomatic power.png diplomatic, then Military power.png military. This contradicts the in game tooltip, which implies that all categories use the initial value, as a result only Administrative power.png administrative is accurate.

   Points generated from all provinces in a state are combined and then reduced by 20% (except for countries with Mandala System or Chakravarti government) and are then used to apply development to the capital. The initial development cost of the capital is what is used to apply all of the development, meaning there is no increase as points are applied.

   The ideal use of this feature would be to somehow raise development cost in a territory or vassal state as high as possible, and decrease development cost in the capital as much as possible, this will gain the most monarch points from concentrating, and make the most use of points on the capital.

AI behavior[edit | edit source]

   Ambox outdated info.png
   Please help with verifying or updating this section. It was last verified for version 1.33.

   AI generally will not develop provinces to more than original development × 2 or 10 development, whichever is higher. These numbers can be changed in defines.^[1]

   AI never exploit development, but may sometimes promote settlement growth.

   The exception to this rule emerges when the AI develops one province for the purposes of institution spread, introduced in Patch 1.18, and also when developing coal provinces (even if the trade good isn't enabled yet) which can sometimes result in these provinces reaching over 40 development. At this time the exact behaviour of the AI regarding this is not well understood. The AI does not develop provinces anywhere as efficiently as a human player may do so.

Strategy[edit | edit source]

   Strategy The below is one of many player suggested strategies for Development. Bear in mind, due to the dynamic nature of the game, it may unfold differently for other players.
     * Prioritize provinces with 9 and 19 development (followed by 8 and 18, etc.) to open an additional building slot.
     * Prioritize provinces from your own culture/culture group or culture convert before to gain the most from this development.
     * Improve production in provinces with high value trade goods before provinces with lower valued goods.
     * Evenly developing a province (4/4/4) is not as lucrative as weighting towards one type of development and reaping a greater bonus with an appropriate building (6/3/3 and a Latin temple.png church).

     * Developing a coastal province instead of an inland province also improves sailors and trade power (through the +25% coastal province modifier).
     * Consider timing: Is the province close to prosperity? Is an institution about to spawn? Is the Latin university.png University about to finish construction? Is the parliamentary issue about to expire? Has the state edict reset time elapsed? Delaying or expediting development can save vital monarch points.
     * Various missions and events give an additional cost modifier (see linked page to “development cost”).
     * Developing a province to get an institution can be expensive in terms of monarch points; it is recommended that the player choose to develop a province with multiple development costs that stack. To be specific, to attain the maximal reduction in development cost, the player should choose to locate their capital in a province with a level 2 or 3 Centre of Trade (the province has to be part of a state), temperate climate, farmlands, and that produces cloth or cotton. The following provinces have this combination of modifiers: Amsterdam, Baghdad, Cairo, London, Lublin, Macedonia, Milan, Prague, Regensburg, Warszawa and Wroclaw. These provinces have a cumulative reduction in developing cost of −20%/25% (−5% from farmlands, −5%/-10% from level 2/3 CoT, −10% from cloth or cotton).

Advanced tips[edit | edit source]

   Development formula:
   [MATH: <semantics> <mrow class="MJX-TeXAtom-ORD"> <mstyle displaystyle="true" scriptlevel="0"> <mrow class="MJX-TeXAtom-ORD"> <mtext>final cost</mtext> </mrow> <mo>=</mo> <mn>50</mn> <mo>⋅</mo> <mi>M</mi> <mi>a</mi> <mi>x</mi> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mn>0.1</mn> <mo>,</mo> <mn>1</mn> <mo>+</mo> <mi>D</mi> <mi>e</mi> <mi>v</mi> <mi>e</mi> <mi>l</mi> <mi>o</mi> <mi>p</mi> <mi>m</mi> <mi>e</mi> <mi>n</mi> <mi>t</mi> <mi>C</mi> <mi>o</mi> <mi>s</mi> <mi>t</mi> <mi>M</mi> <mi>o</mi> <mi>d</mi> <mi>i</mi> <mi>f</mi> <mi>i</mi> <mi>e</mi> <mi>r</mi> <mo>+</mo> <mi>L</mi> <mi>o</mi> <mi>c</mi> <mi>a</mi> <mi>l</mi> <mi>D</mi> <mi>e</mi> <mi>v</mi> <mi>e</mi> <mi>l</mi> <mi>o</mi> <mi>p</mi> <mi>m</mi> <mi>e</mi> <mi>n</mi> <mi>t</mi> <mi>C</mi> <mi>o</mi> <mi>s</mi> <mi>t</mi> <mi>M</mi> <mi>o</mi> <mi>d</mi> <mi>i</mi> <mi>f</mi> <mi>i</mi> <mi>e</mi> <mi>r</mi> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> <mo>⋅</mo> <mi>M</mi> <mi>a</mi> <mi>x</mi> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mn>0.1</mn> <mo>,</mo>
   <mn>1</mn> <mo>+</mo> <mi>D</mi> <mi>e</mi> <mi>v</mi> <mi>e</mi> <mi>l</mi> <mi>o</mi> <mi>p</mi> <mi>m</mi> <mi>e</mi> <mi>n</mi> <mi>t</mi> <mi>C</mi> <mi>o</mi> <mi>s</mi> <mi>t</mi> <mo>+</mo> <mi>L</mi> <mi>o</mi> <mi>c</mi> <mi>a</mi> <mi>l</mi> <mi>D</mi> <mi>e</mi> <mi>v</mi> <mi>e</mi> <mi>l</mi> <mi>o</mi> <mi>p</mi> <mi>m</mi> <mi>e</mi> <mi>n</mi> <mi>t</mi> <mi>C</mi> <mi>o</mi> <mi>s</mi> <mi>t</mi> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> </mstyle> </mrow> <annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{\displaystyle {\text{final cost}}=50\cdot Max(0.1,1+DevelopmentCostModifier+LocalDevelopmentCostModifier)\cdot Max(0.1,1+DevelopmentCost+LocalDevelopmentCost)}</annotation> </semantics> :MATH]
   {\displaystyle {\text{final cost}}=50\cdot Max(0.1,1+DevelopmentCostModifier+LocalDevelopmentCostModifier)\cdot Max(0.1,1+DevelopmentCost+LocalDevelopmentCost)}

   Given that the development formula above rounds down we have some interesting implications when Development cost.png Development Cost is -90% or less:
At 0%  Development cost modifier  Development Cost Modifier it will cost 5  All power costs.png  monarch points per point of development. Meaning that  Development cost.png  Development Cost below -90% doesn't have any effect.

At -1%  Development cost modifier  Development Cost Modifier it will cost 4  All power costs.png  monarch points per point of development. Meaning that even a -2.5%  Development cost modifier  Development Cost Modifier will be as impactful as a -20% (equivalent to  Administrative tech.png  administrative techs level 17 and 23) on provinces with -90%  Development cost.png  Development Cost.

At -20%  Development cost modifier  Development Cost Modifier it will cost 4  All power costs.png  monarch points per point of development. Meaning that  Development cost modifier  Development Cost Modifier is only useful in increments of 20% on provinces with -90%  Development cost.png  Development Cost, meaning that a -5%, -10% or -15%  Development cost modifier  Development Cost Modifier by itself will have no effect on these provinces.

At -81%  Development cost modifier  Development Cost Modifier it will cost 0  All power costs.png  monarch points per point of development. Meaning that if it was somehow possible to stack enough  Development cost modifier  Development Cost Modifier it would be possible to develop every province with -90%  Development cost.png  Development Cost for free (until their development is high enough that they no longer get -90%  Development cost.png  Development Cost).

     * Focus on Development cost modifier Development Cost Modifier for high development provinces whose Development cost.png Development Cost is so high that a small additive reduction won't be as effective.
     * Since you get 0.2% crownland per manual development most of the time, this means that at -90% Development cost.png it will cost just 125 All power costs.png to get 5% more crownland or 1250 for 50% more crownland.

   EU4 Beginner Tutorial #3 - Diplomacy. A complete beginner tutorial with MordredViking looking at how diplhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/omacy works and how you can utilize it to achieve the goals you have set for yourself.
   The diplomacy interface, as the player nation, viewing France

   Diplomacy in https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/EU4 is the system that involves all relations and actions with other nations. Relatihttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ons can be increased through alliances, coalitions, commhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/on wars, common rivalries, decisions, events and having a diplomat improve relations. Relations are decreased by declaring war, beinhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/g rivals, sending insults, having a differhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ent religion, breakhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ing/dishonoring an alliance, events and dehttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/cisions. Diplomacy is a bilateral systhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/em and will affect relations on both sides https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/of an agreement.

   Reasons for a nation's opinion of another are displayed in tooltips wherever opinion is shown. The total is capped at +200/−200.

   Diplomacy is conducted by dhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/iplomats, and the diplomatic options available to diplomats depends on a country's technology and https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ideas. Diplomatic options are split in seven categories: alliance, influence, relations, dynastic, covert, economy and access. Three additional categories are available to any nation that qualifies for them:
     * The emperor of the Holy Roman Empire has an extra category: Emperor actions.
     * The Papal controhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ller also has an extra category: Papal actions.
     * The leading 8 powers of the world have an extra category: Great Power actions.

   The declare war and sue for peace diplomatic options are found outshttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ide of these categories.

/eu4.paradoxwikis.com/an class="mw-headline" id="Diplomats">Diplomats[edit | edit source]

   Ambox outdated info.png
   Please help with verifying or updating this section. It was last verified for version 1.24.

   A Diplomat.png diplomat is required to perform most diplomatic actions. Sohttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/me actions - improving relations, annexing a vassal, building up a spy network and counterespionage - will occupy a diplomat indefinitely or until completion of the task, unless the diplomat is manuallyhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ recalled. Actions that will occupy a diplomat for a perihttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/od of time will display a diplomat icon ( Diplomat.png ) on their button. Other actions are immediate.

   When inhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/itiating a mission, a diplomat takes one day to reach thehttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ target country and begin its mission. After completing a mission, a diplomat will be unavailable while he travels back home, the time which scales based on the distance between one's capital and that of the target country. The precise travel speed of diplomats is 20 distance per day.

  Gaininghttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ diplomats[edit | edit source]

   Each country has 2 Diplomat.png diplomats by default. Additional diplomats mahttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/y be gained through the following triggers, ideas and policies:

Diplomatic relations cahttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/p[edit | edit source]

   Ambox outdated info.png
   Please help with verifying or updating this section. It was last verified for version 1.24.

   The number of other countries a nation can have diplomatic agreements with is limited. Each relation over the cap costs 1 Diplomatic power.png diplomatic monarch point per month. The limit only counts for thhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/e number of different countries with whom an agreement has been closed, not the number of agreements. Having multiple agreements with a single nation https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/only counts as one diplomatic relation.

   Agreements that count towards the cap include:
     * Alliance.png Alliances
     * Royalmarriage.png Royal marriages (except those subject types that do not count toward the cap)https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/
     * Guarantees, but not the guarantees created frohttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/m forcing the release of nations in peace deals
     * Having a Icon vassal.png vassal or Personal union.png junior personal union partner
     * Receiving military access
     * Supporting independence
     * Having a client state

   Agreements that do not count toward the cap include:
     * Granting military access
     * Receiving or granting fleet basing rights
     * Receiving or granting loans
     * Coalition.png Coalitions/eu4.paradoxwikis.com/a>
     * Federations
     * Embargoes
     * Warning other nations
     * Givhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ing subsidies
     * Having a Subject colony icon.png colonial subject.
     * War reparations
     * Transferring trade power (including enforced 'transfer trade' as part of a peace agreement)
     * Having vassals who are members of the empire as the https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/Holy Roman Emperor, if Revoke the Privilegia has been passed.
     * Receiving condhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/itional military access (e.g. within the HRE due to being in a war with the Emperor, or with someone else who has access)
     * Daimyo https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/subjects of the Shogunate government type.
     * Eyalets and corehttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ Eyalets, unless there is also a royal marriage.

Diplomatic reputation[edit | edit sourcehttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/]

   Ambox outdated info.png
   Please help with verifying or updating this section. It was last verified for version 1.24.

   A nation's Diplomatic reputation.png diplomatic reputation represents its overall diplomatic ability andhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ credibility. Diplomatic reputation is visible in the diplomacy window of the country screen.

  Effects[edit | edit source]

   /eu4.paradoxwikis.com/p>Diplomatic reputation positively affects both subject relations and relations with sovereign nations.

   With subject nations, each point of diplomatic reputation gives:
     * +5% chance to inherit lesser partner in a Personal union
     * +1 Diplomatic power.png diplomatic power used per month while annexing vassals or junior partners
     * −3% to thehttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ Liberty desire.png liberty desire https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/of all subject nations

   With other countries, each pointhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ of diplomatic reputation gives the following bonuses when accepting diplomatic proposals:

             Action                        Bonus
   Offer Alliance              https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/5
   Offensive Call to Arms      5
   Royal Marriage              5
   Offer Vassalization         3
   Transfer Trade Power        3
   Ask for Military Access     3
   Ask for fleet basing rights 3
   Request to share maps       5
   Demand unlawful territory   3
   Grant free city status      3

   Increasing diplomatic reputation also improves:
     * the country's score in elections for the Holy Roman Emperor.
     * /eu4.paradoxwikis.com/g alt="Res Publica.png" src="images/thumb/b/b5/Res_Publica.png/28px-Res_Publica.png" dehttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/coding="async" loading="lazy" width="28" height="28" data-file-width="42" data-file-height="42" /> the chance that the country's candidate for the heir of an elective monarchy will gain points while being supported.

Diplhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/omatic actions[edit | edit source]

  War[edit | edit souhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/rce]

          Main article: Warfare

   Declaring war initiates a military conquest against the target country. A casus belli can be selected and the allies of both sides are shown in the declare war screen. Winning battles, achieving the wargoal, and occupying provinces accumulates War score.png war score for both parties, by which peace terms may be agreed upon. At war a country can offer a peace deal (sue for peace) or an unconditional surrender.

  Alliance actions[edit | edihttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/t source]

    Form coalition against[edit | edit source]

          Main article: Alliance#Coalition

   A Coalition.png coalition is an alliance of nations whhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/o have bonded together against a common enemy because of that enemy's very high Ae impact.png aggressive expansion. Coalitions members will automatically be offehttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/nsively and defensively called to arms in any direct war between a coalition member and the coalition target.

    Offer alliance[edit | edit source]

          Main article: Alliance

   An Alliance.png alliance is a military agreemenhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/t of mutual support in wars between two nations. The strength of an alliance is based on trust and favors with the alliance partnerhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/.

    Supporhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/t independence[edit | edit source]

If the target nation declahttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/res a war of independence, all nations supporting its independence will automatically ally the targehttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/t nation and join the war against the former overlord of the now (temporarily) independent nation. The Liberty desire.png liberty desire of the subject is not relevant, but AI subjects dhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/on't accept independence support if they have a Loyal attitude loyal attitude towards their overlord.     Offer condottieri[edit | edit sourchttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/e]

   Mare https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/Nostrum.png Available only with the Mare Nostrum DLhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/C enabled.

          Main article: Condottieri

    Trade leaguehttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/[edit | edit source]

   [28px-Mare_Nostrum.png] Available only with the Mare Nostrum DLC enabled.

          Main article: Trade league

   Trade leagues are a group of small countries banded together to boost trade and providehttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ defensive protection to each other. Only single province countries can join a trade league. A trade league must be lead by a Merchant republic or Veche republic.

          + Medina (384)

     * Is Muslim

    Enforce peace[edit | edit source]

   /eu4.paradoxwikis.com/v class="thumb tright">

   This screen is shown after clicking on enforce peace in the diplomacy tab. The game shows "Invahttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/lid target" until the player choose the country they want to side with by clicking on the flag of the country below the word Enemies. This is necessary even if there is only one countryhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/!

   After choosing a country to side with, its flag and name are shown on the left side and the tooltip for the bar shows the reasons which the country has to accept the enfhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/orce peace.

   The enforce peace action demands that the leading attacker in a war make a white peace with the leading defender. After clicking the Enforce peace action, the enforce peace screen is opened in which the enforcer has to select in which war they want to enforce peace by clicking on the flag of the defender in that war(even if there is only one war). Refusal will bring the enforcing nation into the war on the side of the defender. The following conditions must be met in order to enforce peace:
     * The enforcer must not have a truce with the leading attackehttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/r.
     * The enforcer must have at least +100 relations with thhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/e leading defender (if the enforcer is the emperor of the HRE and the defender is an HRE member, only +0 relations are necessary).
     * The attacker must have −25% War score.png warscore or better.
     * The enforcer must be able to declare war on the attacker (e.g. not in a regency and not being allied to the attacker and not having a https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/transfer trade power relationship with the attacker)

   If the defender is a colonial nation of the enforcer, only the last two conditions must be fulfilled and the enforcer becomes the https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/warleader if the attacker refuses the demand.

   Enforce peace is a useful method for entering wars without triggering any automatic defensive call to arms from the opponent. For example, European powers outside the Imperial authority.png Holy Roman Empire can use enforce peace on empire members to enter wars against them without having to fight the Emperor. Enforce peace can also turn the tides against a rival's offensive war.

    Offer vassalizathttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ion[edit | edit source]

          Main article: Vassal#Offer vassalization (diplomatic)

   Vassalization makes the target nation a subject nation of the country that ohttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ffered it. Vassals are automatically called to their overlord's wars and pay a portion of their Vassal income.png tax income.

    Break vassalizatihttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/on[edit | edit source]

   Breaking vassalization cancels a subject nation's vassalage and makes them independent. This action costs Prestige.png −25 prestige and −200 relations penalty with the former vassal, and results in a truce of 5 years with the former overlord. Vassalization cannot be cancelled when a truce exists with the target.

    Designate march[edit | edit source]

          Main article: March

   Designating a vassal as a March icon.png march grants it substantial military bonuses. Marches do not pay Vassal income.png tax incohttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/me to their overlord, and cannot be diplomatically annexed or peacefully released.

    Revoke march[edit | edit source]

          Main article: March

   Revoking a march changes it to normal Icon vassal.png vassal status, allowing for it to be annexed. This action costs Icon stahttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/bility.png −1 stability and results in a −50 relations penalty with the subject.

    Annex vassal[edit | edit source]

          Main article: Vassal#Annexation

   Diplomatic annexation incorporates a client state or Icon vassal.png vassal into the overlord's domain, resulting in direct control of the former subject's territory and military. This action occupies a Diplomat.phttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ng diplomat for its duration and costs Diplomatic power.png diplomatic power.

    Integrate[edit | edit source]

          Main article: Personal Union#Integration

   Diplomatic integration incorporates a junior parter of a Personal union.png personal union into the senior partner's realm. Like diplomatic annexation of vassals and client states, completion results in control of the junior partner's territory and military, but also gains control of the junior partner's Icon vassal.png vassals and Subject colony icon.png colonial nations. Diplomatic integration of a junior partner in a personal union follows nearly the same principles for requirements, cost, speed, and effects as diplomatic annexation of a vassal.

    Proclaim guarantee[edit | edit source]

   Guaranteed.png Guaranteeing a nation calls the guarantor to war if the target nation is directly attacked by another nation. The guaranhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/tor will not be called to war if the guaranteed nation is cahttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/lled into another war as an ally, unless they are called in as a co-belligerent. The relation uses a Diplomatic upkeep.png diplomatic relations slot and lasts until revoked or a call to arms from the target is declined. A call to arms from a guarantee functions identically to a defensive call to arms in an alliance and carries the shttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ame penalties if declined. Guarantees can be revoked at will, which gives the former guarahttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ntor a truce on the formerly guaranteed country. It is only possible to guarantee countries that are significantly weaker than the guarantor - protection from a weaker nation will not be taken seriously.

    Send warning[edit | edit source]

   Sending a warning to a target country results in a defensive call to arms if the target attacks one of the warner's neighbors (bordering by https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/land). Rejecting this call to arms only incurs a penalty thttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/o trust with relevant nations. The list of neighbors for any nation can be found in its diplomacy tab by filtering its relation list to neighbors only. A country cannot warn another couhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ntry it is already warned by, or that is not significantly weaker. A warning lasts for 20 years and can be issued again once it expires.

    Threaten war/eu4.paradoxwikis.com/pan class="mw-editsection-bracket">[edit | edit source]

   [28px-The_Cossacks.png] Available only with the The Cossacks DLC enabled.

   Threaten war is a diplomatic action which lets a nation demand a province that it or its subjects https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/have a claim or core on. If the demand is accepted,https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ the province is transferred to the demanding nation. If the demand is not accepted a war is declared with the Casus belli.png Conquest casus belli for said province. https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/War cannot be threatened over a country's Capital.png capital (it cannot be targeted at an OPM) or if a https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/truce exists with the target country, and nor can a subject nation (other than Tributaries) threaten war. Successfully demanding a province will cause the threatening country to gain Ae impact.https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/png aggressive expansion as if the prohttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/vince had be conquered in a peace deal and the target nation to lose −10 https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/Prestige.png prestige. This also creates a 5-year truce between the two
   nations. A country will relinquish a province if the relative strength of the demanding country's alliance outweighs the relative worth of the province and the alliances of the thhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/reatened nation. The AI is more willing to give up provinces that the demanding country has a core on, and much less willing to give up provinces if that country has recently demanded another provincehttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/.

   Factors that influence the AI's willingness to giving up a province are:

                             Factor                                                                                  Effect
   Base value:                                                −20
   Province is not a core of the threatening nation:          −20
   Relative strength of alliances:                            −100 to +100 https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/
   Relative worth of province to target's entire development: −1 to −200
   Recently gave in to threat:                                Basehttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ of −120, increasing by +1 per month after truce enhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ded

   Notably, the truce created by this action does not include the subjects of either side, nor do thhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ey need to be at peace themselves if they are allowed to start their own https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/wars. A claim of a colonial nation against another can thus be used to threaten war before, after or even during a colonial war, as long as the province is not occupied.
   https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/

Improve relations[edit | edit source]

   Improve relations.png Improving relations sends a diplomat to the target country to improve relations over tihttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/me. Relations can be improved up to +200/eu4.paradoxwikis.com/b> for subjects and up to +100 for all other nations. Improved relations decay by −3 on the first https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/day of each year if there is no diplomat currently improvinhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/g relations with the target country. The rate at which relations imphttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/rove is highest when relations are 0, and decreases as the difference increases. This rate can be further improved by the improve relations modifier. Any bonus to the improve relahttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/tions modifier also affects how fast any accumulated aggressive expansion will decay.

   When sending a diplomat to improve relations for the first time or when the improved relations value has decayed to 0 doubly improved opinion is gained on the first tick. The rest of the relations improvements take place at the end of each month.

      Scornful insult[edit | edit source]

   Dharma.png Available only with the Dharma DLC enabled.

   A scornful insult will double the loss of opinion – the opinion modifier “Insulted” is replaced by the opinion modifier “Scornfully Insulted”, worth Opinion.png −100 opinion – at costs of Prestige.png 5 prestige (only possible with a positive prestige). Scornfully insulting a rival gains Power Projection.png +10 power projection that stacks upon the potential gain from regular insult. Rivals of the target country get the opinion modifier “Scornfully Insulted Enemy” towards the insulter for 10 years, worth Opinion.png +25 opinion with a yearly decay of https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/��2.5.

  Dynastic actions[edit | edit source]

    Royal marriage[edit | edit source]

   /eu4.paradoxwikis.com/d>For the dynastic effects of royal marriage, see Ruler#Royal marriage
          For information on personal unions, see personal union

   Countries ruled by monarchs may arhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/range Royalmarriage.png royal marriages with others. This improves relations by +25 while in effect. Attacking a country with whom a nation has a royal marriage results in −1 Icon stability.png stability and +1 War exhaustion.png war exhaustion. Note that this penalty will not occur except through a standard declaration of war; to circumvent it, the player may find it useful to Threaten War over a province that the target will refuse to cede.

   Upon the death of a /eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ alt="Catholicism" src="images/thumb/3/39/Catholic.png/28px-Catholic.png" decoding="async" loading="lazy" width="28" height="28" data-file-width="64" data-file-height="64" />Christian monarch with no heir, a ruler from the dynasty of a more prestigious country that shares a royal marriage may rise to the throne. If the countries already share a dynasty, a Personal union.png personal union may result instead. Personal union partners function militarily like vassals. They do not pay a portion of their tax income but may be inherited. Higher Prestige.png prestige increases chances of gaining the crown of a royal marriage partner for a country's dynasty,https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ either independently or as a personal union.

   Royal marriages are normally unavailable to /eu4.paradoxwikis.com/g alt="Government theocracy.png" src="images/thumb/8/81/Government_theocracy.png/28px-Government_theocracy.png" decoding="async" loading="lazy"https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ width="28" height="28" data-file-width="47" data-file-height="47" />theocracies and https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ Government republic.png republics. There are multiple reforms for each that enable them. For theocracies: Somalian Theocracy, Dutch Archbishopric, A Dynashttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/tic Theocracy, and Lords of the Sea. For republics: Dutch Republic, Italianhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ Signoria, and Dynastic Rule. Christians may only marry other Christians. All non-Christians may marry each other, but personal unions will only occur for Christian nations.

   The factors that influence a nation's acceptance of a royal marriage proposal are:

                Factor                                         Effect
   Attitude towards proposer        Friendly attitude Friendly: +40
                                    Protective attitude Protective: +40
                                    Threatened attitude Threatened: +10
                                    Neutral attitude Neutral: −20
                                    Domineering attitude Domineering: −980
                                    Hostile attitude Hostile: −1000
                                    Outraged attitude Outraged: −1000
                                    Rivalry attitude Rivalry: −1000https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/
   Nation opinion about proposer    Positive: +0.25 per point
                                    Negative: −0.25 per point
   Same culture group               +20
   Same religion                    +5
   Neighbors                        +5
   Proposer's diplomatic reputation +5 per point
   Distance between borders         −0.1 per distance between borders^†

   †: Distance between borders can only be seen in debug mode.

    Break royal ties[edit | edit source]

   Breaking royal ties ends a royal marriage. This results in −1 stability and −10 prestige. Furthermore, the relation with the target country is decreasehttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/d by −75. The stability cost may be negated by completing Diplomatic idea group.png Diplomatic ideas, being the Curia Controller, or rivaling the target counthttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ry. The death of the ruler who proposed the marriage will also end a royal marriage without penalty.

    Claim throne[edit | edit source]

          For information on improving chances of obtaining a personal union, see Personal Union

   Claiming a throne gives the "claim on throne" CB, a military means of forcing a personal union.

   The requirements to claim a throne are as follows:
     * Target has a Royalmarriage.png royal marriage
     * Target shares the same dynasty as claimant
     * Target has a weak claim heir or no heir
     * Claimant has more Prestige.png prestige than target

   Claiming the throne of a country results in the following diplomatic effects:
     * −50 relations with other royal marriage partners
     * −100 relations with the target country
     * −20 Prestige.png prestige.
     * −25https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ Trust with the target.
     * Claimant gains Casus belli.png "Claim on Throne" casus belli against the target. The War score.png war score cost to enforce a Personal union.png personal union is 84% regardless of the target's size.
     * If the target country dies without an heir, and a succession war ensues, the claiment of the thone will have priority to be the dehttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/fender in the war over those who do not have claim on https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/the throne [usualy settled by highest dev].

   If there are multiple claimants to the throne then the country with the highest dev will be the defender.

   Note that while some allies may be willing to join a conquest war, they will not join a claim on throne war or succession war, due to opposition to a successful personal union. The gained casus belli lasts until thhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/e target country produces an heir with a strong claim or a new heir rises to the thhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/rone or the royal marriage is cancelled by claimant. Claimee cancelling RM, or claimant dying, while retaining dynasty, does not appear to invalidate it. Thus, when declaring war using this CB, the aggressor will take a Icon stability.png -1 stability hit for the royal marriage.

   The claim throne diplomatic action is only pohttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ssible for Christian nations as no other religious group allows personal unions. While the Government republic.png Dhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/utch republic, oligarchic republic, Italian Signoria, andhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ elective monarchy can have royal marriages, their thrones cannot be claimed as they do not have heirs.

    Support heir[edit | edit source]https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/

   https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/Res Publica.png Available only with the Res Publica DLC enabled.

   Supporting an heir is an action that can be initiated on nations with an elective monarchy (which can only be gaihttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ned by event for Flag of Poland Poland and the Flag of Commonwealth Commonwealth, or by using a custom nation). Any nation that is in the same religious group as the country with elective monarchy can support an heir.

   In an elective monarchy, each nation that has supported its heir in the current election cycle has a possible heir to the throne with an associathttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ed amount of support. A diplomat must be sent in order to support a nation's own heir in an elective monarchy,

   The probability of increasing the heir's support every month by 1 is as follows:https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/

  Covert actions[edit | edit source]

   /eu4.paradoxwikis.com/dd>
          Main article: Espionage

   Diplomats can be send to other nations to build up a spy network, or to practice counterespionage and increase the chance of catching spies sent by the target nation. When https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/a spy network has grown enough, espionage actions can be undertaken, which do not require sending a diplomat. Most of the espionage actions require certain ideas from the espionage idea group in order https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/to become available. Actions that do not need this grouhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/p are fabricate claim, support rebels and justify trade conflict. Completing the espionage group will give access to various powerful actions. One example is the vetting idea, the firhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/st of the idea group, which grants a discount to technology cost depending on the difference in technology level between the home country of the spies and the target country, as well as the size of the spy network there. Covert actions are described in more detail on the
   Espionage page.

    Steer trade power[edit | edit source]

   Rule Britannia.png Available only with the Rule Britannia DLC enabled.

   Ask a target non-subject nation to use their merchants to steer trade toward the proposing nation's trade capital. While a transfer of trade power is active, the two nations involved cannot declare war on each other, but unlike transfer trade power, there https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/is no relations bonus. This effectively hijacks trade power in as many nodes as the target has merchants, where their merchants can be placed for the maximum benefit of the proposer. Technically, no trade power is transferred, so the values for each nation in each trade node remain the samehttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/, and if both share the same home node, then the target will still collect withhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ their trade power, effectively wasting the value of the diplomatic agreement. The agreement does not count toward either country's diplomatic relations limit.

Embargoing a rival grants power projection. Embargoing a non-rival gives a penalty to trade efficiency, but can give a net gain in trade power share (and hence income) if the other country is very dominant in an important node.

    Offer knowledge sharing[edit | edit source]

   Rule Britannia.png Available only with the Rhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ule Britannia DLC enabled.

   Gives https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/the other country +1 monthly progress in its capital area towards the oldest Institutions.png institutionhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ the sending country has embraced that the other one hasn't embraced. This costs Gold Icon.png 10% of the receiving country's monthly income and lasts for 10 https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/years, or until all the sending country's institutions arhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/e present everywhere in the receiving country's capital state. It cannot be offered to a country with loans or which would suffer a deficit post acceptance.

   For the player to be offered knowledge sharing by the AI, the player doesn't need to be allied nor have positive opinion with the target who has already embraced the required institution, but needs (i) to be within colonial range, (ii) have no loans, (iii) have a comfortable monthly profit remaining after covering the cost of Gold Icon.png 10% of income for the arrangement, and (iv) not be in any knowledge sharing agreement already. /eu4.paradoxwikis.com/p>

   This means there should be sufficient tax income, phttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/roduction, trade and gold (excluding war reparations or other flexible non-recurring items) to cover expenses for the duration of the agreement.

    Send gift[edit | edit source]

   Allows a nation to send money to improvehttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ relations with a country, up to a maximum of +25. The gift amount can be adjusted in increments of Gold Icon.pnghttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ 25 ducats. The effect of the gift is:

   [MATH: <semantics> <mrow class="MJX-TeXAtom-ORD"> <mstyle displaystyle="true" scriptlevel="0"> <mrow clashttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/s="MJX-TeXAtom-ORD"> <mtext>relation bonus</mtext> https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/</mrow> <mo>=</mo> <mrow class="MJX-TeXAtom-ORD"> <mfrac> <mrow> <mn>2.4</mn> <mo>⋅</mo> <mrow class="MJX-TeXAtom-ORD"> <mtext>ducats gifted</mtext> </mrow> </mrow> <mtext>monthly income of target country</mtext> </mfrac> </mrow> </mstyle> </mrow> <annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{\displaystyle {\text{relation bonus}}={\frac {2.4\cdot {\text{ducats gifted}}}https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/{\text{monthly income of target country}}}}</annotation> </semantics> :MATH]
   {\displaystyle {\text{relation bonus}}={\frac {2.4\cdot {\text{ducats gifted}}}{\text{monthly income of target country}}}}

   The final value is rounded down to the nearest integer. The relation bonus will last for 5 years. Additional gifts sent during this time will have no effect unless it would increase relations more than previous gifts did.

    Loan offer[edit | edit source]

   Allows a nation to loan out money to other countries for interest. When the loan is due to be repaid, the loan-taker can instead choose to keep the ducats. This will give thehttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ loan-giver a casus belli. AI rulers will always dhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ecline unless they have one of the correct personalities.

    Give subsidies[ehttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/dit | edit source]

   Transfer a specified amount of money each month to the target country for a certain duration. The sender may transfer between Gold Icon.png 0.1 ducats and +50% of its monthly income to the target country each month, adjustable in increments of https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/1% of its monthly income. The duration of the subsidhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/y can be set between 10 and 400 years, adjustable in increments of 10 years.

   Maintaining subsidies will improve the target country's relations with the subsidiser each mhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/onth, up to a maximum of +1https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/5 per year. The accumulated relation bonus is completely removed when the subsidy is cancelled or expires. Since there is otherwise no penalty for terminating a subsidy early, it is generally good practice to set a long subsidy duration unless diplomat time is severely constrained. The relation bonus is

   [MATH: <semantics> <mrow class="MJX-TeXAtom-ORD"https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/> <mstyle displaystyle="true" scriptlevel="0"> <mrow class="MJX-TeXAtom-ORD"> <mtext>yearly relations increase</mtext> </mrow> <mo>=</mo> <mrow class="MJX-TeXAtom-ORD"> <mfrac> <mrow> <mn>12</mn> <mo>⋅</mo> <mrow class="MJX-TeXAtom-ORD"> <mtext>monthly subsidy</mthttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ext> </mrow> </mrow> <mtext>https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/target countrys total monthly income</mtext> </mfrac> </mrow> </mstyle> </mrow> <annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{\displaystyle {\text{yearly relations increase}}={\frac {12\cdot {\text{monthly subsidy}}}{\text{target countrys total monthly income}}}}</annotation> </semantics> :MATH]
   {\displaystyle {\text{yearly relations increase}}={\frac {12\cdot {\text{monthly subsidy}}}{\text{target countrys total monthly income}}}}

   All monthly income mentioned in this section refers to the monthly income as reported in the ledger. Be aware that the target country's total monthly income will therefore include thishttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ monthly subsidy once the ledger is updated after the establishment of the subsidy. This imposes significant diminishing returns on the relation benefits of a large subsidy, and encourages one to maintain smaller subsidies over a longer time frame instead.

   Example: Country A has a monthly income of 10 ducats, and country B provides it with a monthly subsidy of 5 ducats. The reported yearly relations boost will start at +6 per year (B's subsidy is 1/2 of A's income), then immediately drop to +4 per year after the first month (the subsidy is now 1/3 their income).

   Subsidies do not consume a diplomatic relations slot. This makes them a valuable tool for blandishing future targets of diplomatic vassalization or annexation.

   Subsidizing a nation at war with a rival grants Power Projection.png power projection.

    Sell province[edit | edit source]

   A province can be sold to an another nation for a price of 0 to 2,000 ducats at a cost of Prestige.png −10 prestige. Both the buyer and seller must be at peace, and neither can be rivals of the other party. Only one provinchttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/e can change hands in a single transaction. The AI wilhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/l only offer to sell isolated provinces, particularly if it is unable to core them. When the sell province button is clicked, the province to be sold can be chosen together with the price that will be asked for it.

   Factors that influence an AI nation's willingness to buy a province:

                                                    Factor                                                                          Effect
   Province is priced above current treasury of buyer                                                        /eu4.paradoxwikis.com/span class="effect-red">−1000
   Buyer hashttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ no core or claim on province that is of a different culture group  −1000
   Buyer has no core or claim on province that is of a different religious group                             −1000
   Buyer has no core or claihttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/m on province that is part of the Holy Roman Empire −1000
   Buyer has no core on province and is currently overextended by any amount                                 −1000
   Buyer would lose Free City status                                                                         −50
   Price                                                                                                     −1 for every 1% above above 50% of buyer's treasury
   Province is adjacent to buyer                                                                             +10
   Province has the same culture as buyer                                                                    +10
   Province has the same religion as buyer                                                                   +10
   Price                                                                                                     −100 to +100 based on development of target province

   A province can always be bought as long as the price is affordable if:
     * Buyer is a subject and seller has a core on the province
     * Buyer has core on province
     * Buyer is at peace
     * Seller is at peace
     * Buyer is not at war with the seller

   Additionally, it is not possible to sell a province to a colonial subject if the province is https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/not in, bordering, or bordering a province which borders its own colonial region. If the province is particularly undesirable to the buyer, then its base value and associated price modifier will both be halved.

   Selling provinces to a vassal is one method of saving administrative power by letting the vassal core the province. It is useful for avoiding overextension in the short term, and exchanges immediate Administrative power.png administrative coring costs for Diplomatic power.png diplomatic annexation costs later. The The Cossacks.png DLC enables giving provinces to vassals directly via the subject inthttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/eractions interface, making selling provinces to them unnecessary.

   As AI nations place a very high priority on core creation, one can delay their research progress in administrative technologies by selling them provinces with a high Administrative power.png cohttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ring cost. This can be particularly useful if the next administrative technology would otherwise unlock a troublesome idea group (e.g. AI Portugal's first idea group is always exploration).

    Sell ships[edit | edit source]

   Navies can be sold to other nations for a price of 0 to 1000 ducats. If the target nation accepts the proposal, the fleet in question will transfer its allegiance to the buyer. In order to be able to sell ships to a nation, both sides have to be at peace and cannot be rivals of each other. After pressing the button, the fleet that is to be sold can be chosen together with the asking price. When offered to buy https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/a fleet, the AI will want to hold on to a certain ratio of ships (for ehttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/xample, most countries on the Atlantic coast don't want to buy galleys) and will never go above their naval force limit. In order to be able to sell ships, the buyer has to have a fleet within supply range of the target natiohttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/n. Fleets outside of the receiving country's supply range are not availabhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/le to sell. The mouse-over on the YES/NO bar will give the factors for their decision (shown below), and if
   the fleet being offered is too large, it specifies how many less they desire, allowing the player to exit diplomacy andhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ structure a fleet that meets the target countries desired profile.

   https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/The factors that influence an AI nation's willingness to buy ships:

               Factor                                          Effect
   Attitude towards proposer      Friendly attithttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ude Friendly: +10
                                  Threatened attitude Threatened: −20
                                  Loyal attitude Loyal: +10
                                  Neutral attitude Neutral: −10
   Price                          +50 to −200 depending on treasury of buyer and value of the ships
   Buyer wants x fewer ship types −10 per ship of undesired type
   Diplomatic reputation          +1 per positive point, −1 per negative point

   The AI will at times purchase obsolete ships. This makes it possible to get friends, allies, and subjects, as well as other non-rival countries to pay for upgrading the player nation's vessels when new models become available through advances in diplomatic technology. An aggressive nation may have trouble finding willing buyers and could potentially arm subsequent targets/victims, albeit with obsolete weapons.

   Tradecharter Regional Scepticism −X this applies to provinces in the subcontinents Western Europe, Eastern Europe, Levant and Persia. The value differs. Observed values hhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ave been −50 and −70

   The base cost for charter company depends on the colonial range:
