  Access actions[edit | edit source]

   Ambox outdated info.png
   Please help with verifying or updating this section. It was last verified for version 1.24.

    Ask for military access[edit | edit source]

   Request military acceshttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/s from the target country, allowing the requester's land armies to pass through its territories. Acceptance will raise the requester's opinion of the host country by +10https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/, while rejection will decrease it by −10. Declaring war on a country that is granting the aggressor military access causes a major https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/�5 hit to stability.

   AI nations will only grant military access if they have more positive than negative reashttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ons for doing so. The relevant factors are

                Factor                                         Effect
   At war with neighboring rival   +150
   At war with rival               +50
   Has alliance                    +50https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/
   Requester army strength         +100 max
   Attitude towards requester      Friendly attitude Friendly: +20
                                   Defensive attitude Defensive: +20https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/
                                   Protective attitude Protective: +20
                                   Threatened attitude Threatened: +20
                                   Neutral attitude https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/Neutral: 0
                                   Unknown attitude Unknown: 0
                                   Hostile attitude Hostile: −100
                                   Rivalry attitude Rivalry: −100
   Requester diplomatic reputation Positive: +3 per point
                                   Negative: −3 per point
   Nation opinion about requester  Positive: +0.2 per point
                                   Negative: −0.5 per point
   Trust                           0.5 per point

   "At war with rival" only applies while at war with a rival that is not a neighbor. "At war with neighboring rival" replaces it when at war with a neighboring rival.

   Military access is shared for all participants in a war. For example, if France and Brittany are in a war against Burgundy and Fhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/rance requests military access from Savoy, then Brittany will also have milhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/itary access to Savoy. Similarly Burgundy, and all of its war allies, would also gain military access to Savoy.

   Subject nations always give military access to their overlord. All participants in a war automatically grant military access to their allies, as well as being able to march into their enemies' territory. An army in non-allied land when war ihttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/s declared, or in territory without military access when war ends, will be exiled.

    Offer military access[ehttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/dit | edit source/eu4.paradoxwikis.com/an class="mw-editsection-bracket">]

   Offer military access to the target country, allowing their land armies to pass through the requester's territory. Acceptance will raise the target country's opinion of the requester by +10. AI nations are typically uninterested in obtaining https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/military access unless they are the country's ally or subject, or the country is a large and sprawling empire. They will also seek access if they need to travel through a nation to fight in a war. Countries automatically gain military access to countries that grant military access to someone they are at war or allied with.

   A country can't revoke acchttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ess to someone if they, or someone they are at war with, still has troops inside the country's borders.

    Ask for fleet basing rights[edit | edit source]

   Acquiring fleet basing rights from a nation will give the following benefits:
     * Naval supply range will now extend from the ports of that nation.
     * The requester may dock and repair ships in the ports of that nation.
     * The requester may dihttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/sembark ground troops in that nation by docking loaded transports at its ports. These land troops will not be exiled, and may move into any adjacent province that they would normally be able to enter.

   The cost of purchasing fleeting basing rights is as follows:
     * The base cost is Gold Icon.png 0.1 ducats per month per port, with a minimum of Gold Icon.png 0.5 ducats and maximum of 2.0 ducats. This fee is based on the amount of permanent ports.
     * Non-city colony ports are usable https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/and count toward the fee.
     * Ports that reside in https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/a province which are terra incognita to the receiving country also count toward the fee.
     * Occupied ports only charge a fee if they can be docked at.
     * The fee can be seen in the economy window under Harbor Fees.

   Fleet basing rights no longer extend colonial range as in past versions of the game. They can sthttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ill be used to great advantage by distant fleets however. With El Dorado.png El Dorado active, they are no longer useful to explorers since they no longer take attrition while exploring. Only nations that have diplomatic technology level 2 or higher can grant fleet basing rights.

   The following factors will influence an AI nation's decision to grant fleet basing rights:

                              Factor                                                                                                                                Effect
   Nation is allied to requester                                +50
   Nation opinion of requester                                  Positive: +0.2 per point
                                                                Negative: −0.5 per point
   Attitude towards requester                                   Friendly attitude Friendly: +20
                                                                Defensive attitude Defensive: +20
                                                                /eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ alt="Protective attitude" src="images/a/aa/Attitude_protective.png" decoding="async" loading="lazy" width="24" height="24" data-file-width="24" data-file-height="24" /> Protective: +20
                                                                Unknown attitude Unknown: 0
                                                                Neutral attitude Neutral: −20
                                                                Threatened attitude Threatened: −30
                                                                Hostile attitude Hostile: −1000
                                                                Outraged attitude Outraged: −1000
                                                                Rivalry attitude Rivalry: −1000
   Trust                                                        +0.5 per positive point
   Requeshttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ter diplomatic reputation Positive: +3 per point
                                                                Negative: −3 per point
   Requester is embargoing nation                               −1000
   Asked nation is embargoing requester                         −1000

   Once fleet basing rights have been obtained, AI nations will generally not revoke them unless there is a drastic change in relationship.

  Favors[edit | edit source]

          See also: Diplomatic feedback

   Ambox outdated info.png
   Please help https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/with verifying or updating this section. It was last verified for version 1.31.

   [300px-Trust_and_Favors.png]
   Shows trust and favors in the diplomatic feedback screen.

   Favors are a diplomahttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/tic currency that measures the extent to which an AI country owes another country their support, although having a country owe favors is not a guarantee of their support.

Earning favors[edit | edit source/eu4.paradoxwikis.com/pan class="mw-editsection-bracket">]

   Favors are gained from three sources:
   https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/
     * By participating in an ally's war - The higher the country's participation, the more favors will be owed. Base favors earned this way is 20, modified by the war contribution relative to the power of the contributing ally (nations expect strong allies to do more work). Participants will earn fewer favors if they receive land in a peace deal neghttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/otiated by their side's by the war leader.
     * By giving ahttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/n ally land in peace deals - The more land is given to an ally, the more favors a country will gain from that ally. The exact amount of favors gained is scaled to the warscore cost of the provinces and the war participationhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ of the ally. It is reduced if the ally was promised land when https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/they were called to arms. (In this circumstance, if the ally receives less land than it feels it deserves based on its war participation, the peace deal can cause the ally to lose trust with the war leader instead of the war leaderhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ gaining favors from the ally.)
     * Over timhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/e while allied - The rate depends on the relative strength of the two countries; the stronger one nation is compared to the other, the faster it will accumulate favors. /eu4.paradoxwikis.com/>Using the "Curry Favors" diplomatic action - Generates favors every month based on Opinion, Diplomatic https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/Reputation and relative military strength.

Spending favors[edit/eu4.paradoxwikis.com/pan class="mw-editsection-divider"> | edit source]

   Favors can be spent in the following ways:
     * Call to Arms - The main purpose of favors is to call allies into offensive wars. Allies https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/have to either be promised land or 10 favors have to be spent in order to invite them into an offensive war. However, if an ally does not first have net positive reasons to accept the call, then no favors can be spent to invite them.
     * https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/Prepare for war - Ten favors can be spenhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/t to tell a country to prepare for war. For one year they will raise maintenance on their armies and avoid declaring offensive wars. In addition they gain a +20 modifier to accept when being called into a war.
     * Trade Favors for https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/Trust - Favors can also be spent in order to increase https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/an ally's trust at a rate of 10 favors for 5 trust.

   Players with the Leviathan expansion can also spend favors in the following ways:
   https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/Leviathan.png Available only with the Leviathan DLC enabled.
     * Trade Favors for Ducats - Spend 10 favors to receive 6 months of the lowest of the requesting country's and the target country's income. After being used, this action is disabled for 5 years.
     * Trade Favors for Soldiers - Spend 10 favors for 6 months of the lowest of the requesting country's and https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/the target country's manpower. After being used, this action is disabled for 5 years.
     * Trade Favors for Sailors - Spend 10 favors for 6 months of the lowest of the requesting country's and the target country's sailors. Afhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ter being used, this action is disabled for 5 years.
     * Reduce Opinion - Spend 10 favors to reduce the target country's opinion of a third country by 100. After being used, this action is disabled for 15 years.
     * Ask to Return Core - Spend 3 favor per devehttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/lopment to force another country to cede any province it owns and which you or your subject hashttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ a core on.
     * Break Alliance with X - Spend 50 favors to force an allied country to break an alliance with a third country. This also blocks them from reforming the broken alliance for ten years.
     * Request Relative as Heir -https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ Spend 90 favors to give an heirless country an heir of your dynasty. Both the acting and target countries must be monarchihttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/es. However, it generates 20 aggressive expansion with every country of the same religion. (It generates aggressive expansion with countries of your own religion, if the religion of your own nation and the target nation differ.) This diplomatic action is disabled if the difficulty is set to "Hard" or "Very hard".

Papal actions[edit | edit source]

          Main article: Papacy

   https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/

   Some diplomatic actions require control of the Curia and are also discussed on the papacy page. One of the diplomatic actions, call for cruhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/sade, allows the curia controller to call a crusade on a heathen nation. This will give every Christian nation bonuses if they are fighting in a war against the crusade target. The other achttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/tion, excommunication, will grant every neighbor of the excommunicated ruler of a nation a free casus belli.

Great Power actions[edit | edit source]

          Main article: Great power

   The top 8 high-scoring nations receive the Grehttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/at Power status. For being a great power, you will unlock the following actions:
     * Take on Foreign Debt – Pay off all the loans of the target independent non-great power country. Gives +10 /eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ alt="Icon diplomacy relations.png" src="images/e/e6/Icon_diplomacy_relations.png" decoding="async" loading="lazy" width="24" height="24" data-file-width="24" data-file-height="24" /> relations bonus for every standard size loan of the target yohttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/u clear, capped at +200, decaying https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/-2/year. Also grants +5 trust and +2 favours (if The Cossacks.png The Cossacks is enabled). Requires enough money to pay off target’s loans.
     * Influence Nation – Pay 1 year of target income(minimum cost Gold Icon.png 60https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/) to increase relations and grant +1 All power costs.png monarch points in their weakest category for 10 years in a target non-great power nation. This raises their opinion of the grehttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/at power by +25 for the 10https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ years, also gives +5 trust. Going to war with them cancels this bonus.
     * Intervene in War – If there is an ongoing war between three or more great powerhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/s but an imbalance in the number of great powers involved on each side, you can make it your buhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/siness to intervene. For example, if great power England is singlehandedly fightihttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ng the great powers of France and Spain, you as a great power Commonwealth can intervene on England's side to balance out the number of great powers involved.
     * Break Alliance – This will force a nation to break its alliance with another. https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/They will accept if the target nation is sufficiently afraid of the player and yohttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/u will gain a 10-year one-way truce with the nation you forced this upon. It is useful for stripping the war target of pesky roadblocks, because there won't be a truce between the great power and the former ally. The former ally gets a "Forced ally to break alliance" CB against the grhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/eat power for 10 years. Both the target country and thhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/e former ally get a -50 Icon diplomacy relations.png relations modifier with the great power. The target country's trust towards the great power will be reduced by 5.

   The Flag of Germany German "Concert of Europe" mission strengthens these actions to give further benfits.

Losing Great Power status[edit | edit source]

   Ambox outdated info.png
   Please help with verifying or updating this section. It was last verified for version 1.35.
   https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/

   If a country falls behind on the Great Power ranking to below #8, it will be given a 5-year grace period to reclaim Great Power status. During that period, said country will still have access to Great Power diplomatic options. If the position is not regained in the grace period, thttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/he country will completely lose Great Power status. If a nation becomes a subject in any way, they automatically lose and are disqualified from Great Power status, though half their development will go to their new overlordhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/'s Great Power points.

Hegemony[edit | edit source]

   Ambox outdated info.png
   Please help with verifying or updating this section. https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/It was last verified for version 1.35.
   Emperor Ahttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/vailable only with the Emperor DLC enabled.

   A Great power.png great power that fulfills certain conditions can declare itself to be the economic, naval or military hegemon. Being a hegemon grants great rewards, but antagonizes allhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ other countries. Hegemons are listed at the bottom of the great power list.

Becoming Hegemon[edit | edit source]

   A Great power.pnghttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ great power can declare themselves to be a Economic, Naval or Military Hegemon if it fulfills the conditions that are listed in the table below. If there is already a hegemon of that type, the hegemon must first be made to lose the hegemony before another country can become the same type of hegemon. Becoming a hegemon immediately grants the base effects.

   A country that is already a hegemon of one type can't become another hegemon.

Hegemon power[edit | edit source]

   Hegemon power scales from 0% to 100%. As long as a hegemon fulfills the hegemony requirements they will gain 0.5% hegemon power per month. If they don't fulfill all requirements anymore, they will lose 0.5% hegemhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/on power per month. The scaling effects that are listed in the table below, increase with the hegemon power. At 0https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/% hegemon power these effects are not active and at 100% they ahttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/re in full effect.

   At 100% hegemon power the additional effect https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/from the last column will be activated.

    Other bonuses and penalties[edit | edit source]

     * Hegemons gain a +100%/eu4.paradoxwikis.com/b> bonus to Icon score.png score generation rate.
     * Hegemons gain Power Projection.png +25 Power projection
     * Countries allied to a hegemon gain Power Projection.png −20 Power projection
     * Every country except for the hegemon's subject nations gains the Opinion.png opinion modifier "Hegemon" −50 towards a hegemon
     * Every country that is not a hegemon gains the Contain Hegemon casus belli against a hegemon
     * Hegemons can't ally other hegemons and existing alliances with other hegemons are automatically broken when a country becomes a hegemon

Losing Hegemony[edit | edit source]

   A country can lose its hegemon status by losing great power status (5 yhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ears after falling below 8th place in the great power lishttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/t) or by losing a war. Even a war in which the hegemon is not the war leader or ghttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/iving any concessions to a secondary participant counts for that.

   Losing a hegemony gives the "Lost Hegemony" modifier for 20 years giving All power costs.png +10%/eu4.paradoxwikis.com/b> to all power costs. During that time the country can't become a hegemohttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/n again.

Select rival[edit | /eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ href="https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/index.php?title=Diplomacy&action=ehttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/dit&section=85" title="Edit section: Select rival">edit https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/source]

   The rival mechanic was added with patch 1.6.

Rivals are countries thhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/at a nation expects to come into conflict with in the future. Rivals are usually https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/very comparable in military and diplomatic power and have interests in the same regions and https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/thus will often clash with each other. Rivals may be only selechttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ted from countries that are comparable in power. When in the rival sehttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/lection screen, the nations that are availhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/able as rivals and their corresponding opinion of the country and their relative army and navy strength can be seen. A country can have up to 3 rivals^[1] at the same time. If a rival becomes too weak or too strong it will cease being a validhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ rival. When selecting possible rivals, the game will take the https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/relative army strength into higher account than the relative navy strength.https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/
Relative development and technology levels are also taken into accord. Nations must be relatively near to be eligible rivals, with more powerful countries able to have rivals at greater distance. Setting a nation as a rival will greatly decrease the amount of diplomacy that can be exchanged between the two nations. Rivals rarely accept diplomatic requests from their nemeses. In order to be rivals both countries must have each other discovered. Selecting a rival has the following benefits:
     * A nation is more likely to sign alliances with the enemies of their rivals.
     * +25% Prestige.png prestige from defeating a rival in battle.^[2]
     * No Trade efficiency.png trade https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/efficiency penalty from embargoing the rival.
     * +25% spy network build rate against the rival.^[3]
     * −33% /eu4.paradoxwikis.com/mg alt="Diplomatic power.png" src="images/thumb/d/da/Diplomatic_power.png/24px-Diplomatic_power.png" decoding="ahttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/sync" loading="lazy" width="24" height="24" data-file-width="28"https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ data-file-height="28" /> Diplomatic Power cost for demanding uhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/njustified provinces from the rival in peace deals.^[4]

Having a rival and taking actions against it grants power projection. Not having enough rivals gihttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ves a penalty to power projection.

Changing a rival is possible after 5 years^[5] for Diplomatic power.png 100 diplomatic power^[6]. The cost to change a rival may be reduced by 50%https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ with the ‘Flexible Rivalries’ ability during the Age of Absolutism.png ‘Age of Absolutism’ and by 20% with the North Western Native idea 1: Raid Warfare.

   AI nations have distance penalty cut by 50% and given a lower treshold thhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/an the player as to when existing rivahttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ls become too small or too big.

Historical Rivals[edit | edit sourhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ce]

   Ambox outdated info.png
   Please help with verifying or updating this section. It was last verified for versihttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/on 1.30.

          Main article: Relations#Historical_friends_and_rivals

   Historical rivals are pre-set by the scenario's starting conditions, and do not change over time (except by events). Historical rivalry not only afhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/fects relations by giving −25 malus, but historical rivals will almost always rival each other and if that's no longer possible, they will never make an alliance. If https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/historical rival country is a vassal or lesser partner in personal union, it will have Liberty desire.png +50% liberty desire modifier. For example: Denmark and Sweden after The Scandinavian Constitution event.

Release subject[edit | edit source]

   This releases a country as a Icon vassal.png vassal. The released country gets all of theirhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ core provinces that are owned by the releasing country, except for the releasing country's capital if applicable; the releasing country does not need to have cores on any of the provinces. Nations can only be released if at least one owned province is both a core ofhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ the nation and has a culture of the same group as the nation's primary culture. This action can not be done while at war.

   This is far more useful of an action than it looks like at first:
   /eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ul>

     Annex one or two provinces with cores of an extinct, but formerly large nation, and release that nation as a vassal. Then, you can slowly retake all their former land with the Reconquest CB, at no diplohttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/matic point cost and only 25% of the Aggressive Expansion penalty.

     You should also do this if the nation is merely near death, but cannot be diplomatically vassalized for whatever reason. It causes more AE than forced vassalization, but the difference will not be significant if thhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/e country is small, and you will immediately have a vassal with low liberty desire and a good opinion of you, instead of large penalties from forced vassalization and aggressive expansion.

Disasters

   From Europa Universalis 4 Wiki
   Jump to navigation Jump to search

   This article is timeless and should be accurate for any version of the game.

   Disasters are a system introduced in Patch 1.9 that replaced the previous MTTH event-based system used to simulate national disasters.

   Disasters can be found under the ‘Stability and Expansion’ tab. The tab lists disasters that may happen if the country's situation matches the start conditions, or the disaster that is currently in progress. Once the start conditions are met, various conditions cause the disaster's progress to tick up by a certain amount each month from 0 to 100 until it reaches 100, at which point the disaster begins with an initial event. Progress on a disaster falls, or may stop altogether and be reset, when any of the prerequisites are not fulfilled. It is also possible for progress to be "on hold" where the disaster's prerequisites are fulfilled, but none of the monthly progress conditions are fulfilled.

   While in a disaster, the country suffers a detrimental modifier, and special events happen on a monthly tick (not every month will have an event). The action required to end the disaster varies: usually it includes reversing whatever condition caused it to start (which is made more difficult by the disaster modifier), and often includes defeating rebels and stabilizing the country. Ending the disaster triggers an end event and removes the detrimental modifier.

   For most disasters, the nation cannot suffer the same disaster again (the main exception being estate disasters). It is also only possible to be in one disaster at a time; progress on other disasters will halt when one begins.^[1]

   Currently the following disasters are possible:^[2]
   [ ]

   Too much religious differences in our country is causing a lot of intolerance and bigotry.

   Revolution icon

Economy

   From Europa Universalis 4 Wiki
   Jump to navigation Jump to search

   Please help with verifyihttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ng or updating older sections of this article.
   At least some were last verified for version 1.24.
   Economy interface

   Economics in EU4 revolves around the earning and expenditure of Gold Icon.png ducats, the game's international currency. The national and international economy underpin almost every function of a country, and oftenhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ fuels international diplomacy. Understanding and developing a country's economy yields better national finances, allowing the country thttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/o boost its standing in the world and further grow at a faster pace.

   The Economy panel in the Country interface displays a summary of the player's finances and provides a few ihttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/mportant actions relating to it (such as Loans and Reduce Inflation).
   [ ]

Overview[edit | edit source]

   Ambox outdated info.png
   Please help with verifying or updating this section. It was last verified for version 1.24.

   The total amount of https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ Gold Icon.png ducats in a country's treasury is updated at thhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/e beginning of every month. The amount by which this changes is the total Income.png income minus the Expenses.png expenditure forhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ the previous month. The various factors which affect these amounts are listed below. In addition, various Msg event.png events may add or take away from the treasury.

   Aside from the continuing incomes and ehttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/xpenses mentioned below, Gold Icon.png ducats may also be gained or spent as one-time earnings or payments in the following ways:

   Earnings:
     * Treasure fleets
     * https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/Estate interactions
     * Receiving gifts and loans from other countries through Diplomatic power.png diplomacy
     * Siphon income from a junior partner in a personal union
     * /eu4.paradoxwikis.com/a href="https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/Development#Exploiting_development#Exploiting_development" title="Development">Exploiting Develohttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/pment from provinces

   Expenditures:
     * Constructing buildings
     * Estathttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/e interactions
     * Hiring and salary costs for /eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ alt="Advisor.png" src="images/thumb/6/6a/Advisor.png/28px-Advisor.png" decoding="async" loading="lazy" width="28" height="28" data-file-width="48" data-file-height="48" />advisors
     * Recruitment costs for Infantryhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/.png land and https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ Heavy ship.png naval units
     * Providing gifts, subsidies, and loans to other countries through Diplomatic power.png diplomacy
     * https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/Supporting rebels in another country through espionage
     * Paying another country to share knowledge
     * Embracing institutions

Income[edit | edit source]

   Ambox outdated info.png
   Please help with verifying or updating this section. It was last verified for version 1.24.
   The "Income" column lists regular shttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/treams of income, and effect by modifiers plus efficiency https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/(in grey, middle column).

   Income.png Income is the sum of all money gained monthly. Unlike in EU3, all income is liquid and does not need to be minted. The continuhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ous sources of income that a country has is listed in the "Inchttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ome" column, which is on the left side of the Economy panel (see right). This panel lists both the total amount from each source and that source's bonus (if any). Hovering over the sourhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ce or bonus shows a tooltip with detailed information, such as modifiers or a breakdown of inhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/come by province.

   The maximum amount of Gold Icon.png ducats a country can have in its treasury is 1 million. However, this number is considered to be difficult to reach without using console commands or mods.

Taxation[/eu4.paradoxwikis.com/span>edit | edit source]

          Main article: Tax

   /eu4.paradoxwikis.com/mg alt="Tax income.png" src="images/thumb/1/19/Yearly_tax_income.png/28px-Yearly_tax_income.png" decoding="async" loading="lazy" width="28" height="28" data-file-width="48" data-file-height="48" />Tax comes directly from the population of a province, and produces a relatively dependable baseline income. Each province has a Tax Base Iconhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/.png base tax (which may be increased by spending Administrative power.png administrative power), and a Local tax modifier.png tax income efficiency. The yearly province tax amount is the multiple of the two amounts. There is also a Global tax modifier.png National Tax Income, thttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/hat is calculated at a countrywide level. Various tax modifiers exist that may change this amount.

Production/eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ class="mw-editsection-bracket">[edit | edit source]

          Main article: Production

   Production.png Production is a measure of the amount of income generated in a province by local producers of its trade good. Unlike in EU3, production income is added directly to the state's income each month. This amount depends on the good's prices, the province's base production, and the Production efficiency.png production efficiency (among other modifiers).

Trade[https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/edit | edit source]

          Main article: Trade

   The https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/"Trade trade value produced by each province flows into the trade network, where it is eventually collected by capitals and Merchants.png merchants and converted into Gold Icon.png ducats. Careful management of trade can make it the most powerful source of income by far, which makes control of trade-important provinces instrumental for a long-term increase of a nhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ation's economical power.

Gold[edit | edit source]

   Gold Gold Gold is a special "trade" good. Gold dohttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/es not produce any Trade value.png trade value; instead, it is converted directly into ducats. Gold production income is 40 Gold Icon.png ducats per year per unit produced, with the exception of unreformed New World natives, who only receive 1 Gold Icon.png ducat per year per unit produced. Income from gold causes Inflation reduction.png inflation per year equal to half its proportion of the country's income; at 100% income the country's inflation would increase bhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/y 0.50% per year.

Treasure fleet[edit | edit source]

   El Dorado.png Golden Century.png Available only with the El Dorado DLC or the Golden Century DLC enabled.

   Subject colony icon.png Colonial nations with gold provincehttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/s will not receive the income of gold for themselves, but instead wihttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ll store it in a ‘Treasure Fleet Counter’ that counts up towards a certain sum depending on the size of the colony’s gold mines. Once the counter is full, the colony will send a trehttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/asure fleet. The treasure fleet travels downstream along the trahttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/de routes, passing each node between the colonial nation and its overlord's trade capital. If there are prihttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/vateers present in these nodes, they will steal a share of thhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/e gold corresponding to their power in the node. At the end of the journey, any money that remains is given to the overlord nation. Both the overlord nation and nations privateering suffer Inflation reduction.png inflation similar to that gained from gold mines.

   The incomhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/e of treasure fleets may be increased by:

   Nations who do not have their trade capital downstream of their colonies’ trade nodes will be unable to receive treasure fleets. In these cases, the colonial nation will simply keep the gold for themselves, paying just the usual amount in tariffs.

Tariffs[edit | edit source]

          Main article: Tariffs

   Subject colony icon.png Colonial nations are required to transfer a part of their tothttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/al income, called Global tariffs.png tariffs, to their overlord. At their formation, this ahttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/mount is 10% of their income. The tariffs can be set fhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/or each colonial nation by the overlord in the Subjects interface or may change through Msg event.png events. Higher tariffs increase the level of Liberty desire in the colonial nation.
   https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/

Vassals[edit | edit source]

          Main article: Income from vassals

   Icon vassal.png Vassals are required to pay a Vassal income.png fee to their overlords. The basis for calculating this fee is the Tax income.png tax income of the vassal. The amount that must be paid is modified by the ‘vassals tax effihttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ciency’ of the overlord, which is influenced by the overlord's Legitimacy.png legitimacy, among other factors. Apart from the fee, vassals may be requehttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/sted to give all of their trade power to their overlord. While this action will increase their liberty desire by 30 %, this may significantly bohttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ost the overlord's trade income, especially if he has better trade efficiency.

Harbor fees[edit | edit source]

   Signing a fleet basing agreement with another country will cost an amount equal to 0.1 Gold Icon.png ducats^[1] per month for every port belonging to the other country with a minimum of 0.5 Gold Icon.png ducats and maximum of 2.0 Gold Icon.png ducats per month.

   The AI never asks to access ports of the player, and thehttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ player can never offer it (there is a -1000 "strategic interests" modifier). Whether the province is cored or not has no effect on the cost of fleet basing rights.

Subsidies[edit | edit source]

          Main article: Diplomacy § Give subsidies

   Chttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ountries that have a strategic interest in another country may grant subsidies to that country, which is given in the form of a certain amount of the benefactor's Income.png monthly income ehttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ach month for a certain number of years.

Spoils of war[edit | edit source]

   The Spoils of War section includes income gained from military and wartime actions. This includes:
     * Looting and blockading: Looting occurs when a province (either occupied or https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/besieged) has hostile units stationed in it, as long as the province has loot left. A province with a port is blockaded by any hostile fleet stationed in the sea province where the port is located.
     * Privateering: A country can send their Light ship.png light ships on missions to Privateer in certain sea zones, aiding pirate nations in exchange for a portion of their earnings.

   Income from razing and coastal raiding is not accounted for.

War Reparations[edit | edit source]

   A country has the option to demand 10% of an enemy's income for 10 years as part of a peace deal.

Condottieri[edit | edit source]

   Mare Nostrum.png Available only with the Mare Nostrum DLC enabled.

   It is possible to offer a country Condottieri, which are armies rented out for money. Note that, in the event https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/that the contractor is a player-controlled country, thhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/e army will stay under the control of the AI.

Knowledge Sharing[edithttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ | edit source]

   Rule Brhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/itannia.png Available only with the Rule Britannia DLC enabled.

          Main article: Diplomacy § Knowledge Shhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/aring

   A country may offer other countries progress in institutions they haven't yet embrachttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ed. This costs Gold Icon.png https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/10% of their monthly income, which they pay direct to the country that's sharing. Only one knowledge sharing agreement may be made at a time.

Expenses[edit | edit source]

   Ambox outdated info.png
   Please help with verifying or updating this section. It was last verified for version 1.28.
   The "Expenses" column showing major payments and maintenances.

   A country's Expenses.png expenses, i.e., its monthly continuous payments, is similarly listed in the Expenses column on the right side of the Economy panel. This column lists two types of expenses:
     * Automatic expenses: These https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/are expenses which are automatically deducted from the treasury. They cannot be modified from the Economy panel, simply viewed (except for Interest.png Interest, which may be changed through the Loans interface).
     * Adjustable expenses: These expenshttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/es are shown with sliders, to adjust the amount being spent monthly on them. Changinhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/g these expenses using the sliders will have an impact on the action being done or the asset being maintained.

Advisors[edit | edit source]

          Main article: Advishttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/or cost

   Advisor.png Advisors have a base monthly salary equal to the square of their skill level, increased by 0.5% per game year since 1444. Hovering over this in the Expenses column shows a tooltip that lists other modifiers, incluhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ding Inflation.

State maintenance[edit | edit source]

          Main article: State maintenance

   Icon states.png States require continuous monetary upkeep, depending on the development of the provinces, the distance to the capital and further modifiers.

Interest/eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ class="mw-editsection-bracket">[edit | edit source]

          Main article: Loans

   Interest.png Interesthttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ must be paid on loans. The default interest rate is 4%, which may be changed by modifiers. Further information is given in the Loans section below.

Diplomatic expenses[edit | edit source]

   Diplomatic expenses.

   Hovering over Diplomatic Expenses shows a tooltip with a more detailed breakdown of a country's diplomatic expenses (see right). These are as follows:
     * Our Cities Looted and Our Ports Blockaded: The enemy's income from looting and blockading provinces is taken from the treasury and is listed here only when it applies.
     * Subsidies: Gold Icon.png Ducats sent monthly to other countries as subsidies, if any.
     * Vassal fee: If the country is a Icon vassal.png vassal, the amount of Vassal income.png vassal fees sent to their overlord.
     * Outgoing tariffs: If the country is a Subject colony icon.png colonial nation, the amount of Gold Icon.png ducats paid to their overlord as Global tariffs.png tariffs.
     * War reparations: Amount paid to winners of previous wars (usually 10% of income for 10 years). See war reparations for more details.
     * Support loyalists: Amount spent to junior partners in Personal union.png personal unions to reduce their Liberty desire.png Liberty desire.
     * Send officers: Amount sent to March icon.png marches to reduce their liberty desire and provide a bonus to thttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/heir armies.
     * Knowledge sharing: Amount sent to subjects to spread institutions. (Requires Rule Brihttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/tannia.png Rule Britannia DLC).
     * Condottieri fees: Amount paid to other countries ahttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/s rent for Condottieri (requires Mare Nostrum.png Mare Nostrum DLC).

Fort maintenance[edit | edit source]

          Main article: Forts

   This shows the amount spent monthly to maintain the Fort level.png forts present in a country. The amount spent on each fort depends on its fort level. Forts can be mothballed while at peace to reduce their Fort maintenance modifier.png maintenance by a -50% modifier. Doing so will inhibits the forts upkeep of Army tradition.png army tradition and remove the defenders https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/making it easy to conquer in a war. Further modifiers are granthttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ed by ideas and policies among others.

Colonial maintenhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ance[edit | edit source]

          Main article: Colonial maintenance

   Colonies require a monthly maintenanchttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/e while they grow until they become full cities. The cost per year is:

   [MATH: <semantics> <mrow class="MJX-TeXAtom-ORD"> <mstyle displaystyle="true" scriptlevel="0"> <mrow class="MJX-TeXAtom-ORD"> <mtext>cost per year</mtext> </mrow> <mo>=</mo> <mrow> <mo>(</mo> <mrow> <mn>24</mn> https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ <mo>+</mo> <mrow class="MJX-TeXAtom-https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ORD"> <mfrac> <mtext>total development</mtext> <mn>4</mn> </mfrac> </mrow> </mrow>https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ <mo>)</mo> </mrow> </mstyle> </mrow> <annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{\displaystyle {\text{cost per year}}=\left(24+{\frac {\text{total development}}{4}}\right)}</annotation> </semantics> :MATH]
   {\displaystyle {\text{cost per year}}=\left(24+{\frac {\text{total development}}{4}}\right)}

   So, the cost per month is roughly:

   [MATH: <semantics> https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ <mrow class="MJX-TeXAtom-ORD"> <mstyle displaystyle="true" scriptlevel="0"> <mrow class="MJX-TeXAtom-ORD"> <mtext>cost per month</mtext> </mrow> <mo>=</mo> <mrow> <mo>(</mo> <mrow> <mn>2</mn> <mo>+</mo> <mrow> <mo>(</mo> <mrow> <mrohttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/w class="MJX-TeXAtom-ORD"> <mtext>total development</mtext> </mrow> <mo>⋅</mo> <mn>0.02</mn> https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ </mrow> <mo>)</mo> </mrow> </mrow> <mo>)</mo> </mrow> </mstyle> </mrow> <annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{\displaystyle {\text{cost per month}}=\left(2+\left({\thttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ext{total development}}\cdot 0.02\right)\right)}</annotation> </semantics> :MATH]
   {\displaystyle {\text{cost per month}}=\left(2+\left({\text{total development}}\cdot 0.02\right)\right)}

   Thus, a 5 Development.png development province will cost about 2.10 Gold Icon.png ducats per month to colonize, while a 6 development province will cost 2.12 Gold Icon.png ducats per month. The cost is further increased quadratically for each colony over the number of Colonists.png colohttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/nists the country has. Colonial maintenance can be reduced, but at the cost of colonial growth. Provincial modifiers to colony growth are applied separately to this change. So, a tropical colony will shrink by -110 settlers with zero maintenance due to the additional -10 settlers provincial modifier. https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/Colonial maintenance also does not affect growth from colonist agents.

   Colonists.png Colonists cannot be sent while a country is bankrupt.

Missionary maintenance[edit | edit source/eu4.paradoxwikis.com/an class="mw-editsection-bracket">]

          Main article: Missionary maintenance

   The costs of an active Missionaries.png missionary depends on the founding and the development and local autonomy of the province which he is converting.

https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/Root out corruption[edit | edit source]

          Main article: Corruption

   A country can lower Corruption.png corruption by spending up to 0.05 Gold Icon.png ducats per effective Development.png development per month under the Root Out Corruptionhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ slider, for a maximum of -1% every year. Effective development is affected by Autonomy.png autonomy. The total cost of rooting out corruption is calculated using the formula:
   cost of rooting out corruption = corruption cost multiplier × effective development

   where effective development is determined by the formula:
   effective development = total national development − Σ(total province development × local autonomy)
     * Corruption cost multiplier is the amount spent per effective developmenhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/t. This is the amount that is controlled by the slider. It can be changed from 0 Gold Icon.png ducats per month to 0.05 Gold Icon.png ducats per month.
     * Local autonhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/omy is used in decimal form in the above calculations.

Example[edit | edit source]

   Total province development and local autonomy for each of the three provinces for Andhra

   For the three-province country Andhra (see right), the maximum cost to root out corruption can be calculated as follows:
     * Total national development: Kosta + Velanadu + Konaseema = 11 + 15 + 11 = 37
     * Sum of effective development changes by each province: Σ(province development × local autonomy)
          + Kosta: 11 × 0.25 = 2.75
          + Velanadu: 15 × 0.25 = 3.75
          + Konaseema: 11 × 0 = 0
     * effective development change = 2.75 + 3.75 + 0 = 6.5
     * effective development = total national development − effective development change = 37 − 6.5 = 30.5

   So, the final cost will be:
   total cost of rooting out corruption = 0.05 × 30.5 = 1.52 ducats/month

   The calculations above mean that higher Autonomy.png local autonomy will decrease the cost of lowering corruption.
   https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/

Army maintenance[edit | edit source]

          Main article: Army maintenance

   At full Land maintenance modifier.png army https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/maintenance, each fielded regiment has a monthly maintenance cost equal to 2% of its Global regiment cost.png recruitment price. All modifiers to maintenance are added together and applied to this. Reducing army maintenance using the slider affects Reinforce speed.png reinforcement rates and Land morale.pnghttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ morale, to 0% reinforcement rate and a -100% modifier to morale at minimal funding. Condottieri reinforcements and maintenance costs are applied even when maintenance slider is at zero.

   Maintenance costs increase over time as a country advances in Technology.png technology.

   Maintenance costs will reduce when a regiment suffers casualties, but will increase due to an added cost for reinforcement. Maintenance costs will also increase when a country exceeds its Land forcelimit.png force limit.

Fleet maintenance[edit | edit source]

          Main article: Navy maintenance

   Naval maintenance modifier.png Fleet maintenance works the same as army maintenance but with certain exceptions:
     * First, naval maintenance increases at discrete steps rather than continuously. It is increased by 10% at Diplomatic tech.png Diplomatic technology levels 3, 5, 9, 15, 19, 22, 25, 27, 29, https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/and 31 (to a total of +100%).

     * Second, each vessel type has its own maintenance modifier.

     * Third, vessels do not cost increased maintenance to /eu4.paradoxwikis.com/mg alt="Global ship repair.png" src="images/thumb/5/5d/Global_ship_repair.png/28px-Global_ship_repair.png" decoding="ashttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ync" loading="lazy" width="28" height="28" data-file-width="48" data-file-height="4https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/8" />repair, but also do not cost reduced maintenance if damaged.

   Further differences, including those on how modifiers are applied, are listed on the Navy page.

   Similar to army maintenance, reducing navy maintenance using the slider gives negative modifiers to Global ship repair.png ship repair and Naval https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/morale.png Naval Morale, up to -100%. In addition, Ship trade power.png Light Ship Trade Power is reduced by up to -75%.

   Mothballhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ing allows naval units to be left unusable in a country's docks for lower maintenance, while giving ships 5% hull damage per month of being mothballed until 25% health remains.

Bank loans[edit | edit sourhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ce]

   The size of the loans are determined by your country's development as per the formula below, while the number of loans are a function of the interest (that is, the maximum number of loans are limited to when your total interest equals your monthlhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/y income (the point where one goes bankrupt)

   Taking ahttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ loan grants an amount of money equal to result of the following formula:
   loan size = floor(0.5 × Development.png total development) × (1 + Trade efficiency.png trade efficiency from dihttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/plomatic technology)

   And the amount of loans that you can take depends on your monthly income (before expehttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/nses) divided by your monthly interest per loan and rounded:
   amount of loanhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/s = monthly income / (loan size * (Interest Per Annum / 100) / 12)

   A loan may be taken at any time, although each loan taken increases inflation by 0.1.^[1] A loan may be paid back in fulhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/l, plus the total remaining interest owed, at any time durinhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/g the loan period. If a loan expires and the borrower cannot (or chooses not to) pay the principal, the loan will be extended for an additional 5 years at the current interest rate, and inflation will increase by an additional 0.1.

   Debt Restructure: Given the same increase https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/in inflation whenever a loan is renewed automatically, it may be goohttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/d to "restructure" your debt every now and then. That is, over time as your development increases your loan sizes increase, however when the old loan renews it gives the same inflation but for a smaller original loan amount. Therefore rather borrow doing a new larger loan to repay the old one before it expires. This allows you more debt capacity as you mayhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ recall the size of the loan (based on development) is determinedhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ separately from the number of loans (based on interest vs income).

   Determining total loans outstanding by others: There is no ledger to view this, however, as a Great Power one can hover over the great power action "Take on Foreign Debt" to see the target nation's total outstanding loan balance. Alternativelyhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/, if one is not a great power with access to this menu option, there is a rough short-hand that is fairly accurate to help estimate this value. In the Ledger under "Country", "Score Comparison" hover your mouse over the "Adhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/m. Rating". Loans will be shown in a red negative number, where each −0.02 is roughly equal to one outstanding loan. Hence, −0.08 would roughly be equal to 4 loans. To determine the value of each loan view the country development under the ledger and divide the development by 2. Hence, a 500 total development country would roughly be able to borrow 250 ducats per loan. Another method would be to use the "Declare War" on the target county's ally. One of the reasons for not
   joining in the war would be "loans outstanding" and a total debt value would be shown.

Loans from countries[edit | edit source]

   Countries that have a strategic interest in another country's wars may grant loans to that country. Rulers with the Indulgent trait will accept loans from hhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/uman players if needed.

Interest[edit | edit source]

   The interest rate of loans from countries is set by the country granting the loan.

CB for cancelling loan[edit | edit source]

   If the borrower refuse tohttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ pay the principal when a loan expires, the lender gets ahttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ 12-month CB "Cancelled Loan" against the borrower.

Loans from estates[edit | edit source]

   The estate privileges Indebted to the Bourgeoisie and Indebted to the Jains provide five loans at 1% interest. Repaying the loans automatically removes the privilege.

Debase currency[edit | edit source]

   Ambox outdated info.png
   Please help with verifying or updating this section. It was last verified for version 1.29.

   Debasing currency gives the https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/player a loan's amount of money at the cost of 2 Corruption.png corruption. It cannot be done if corruption is already over 90. This is useful if the player wahttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/nts to repay it over time at their pace (not receiving even more inflation forhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ re-newing loans); however, it is a lot more costly than a regular loan to be repaid using only "Root Out Corruption", plus the negative modifiers for having corruption. But the value to root it out can be reduced significantly ihttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/f the player is ahead of time on diplomatic and/or administrhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ative technology, and if its ruler has the Incorruptible trait, giving a "negative" interest if the player is willing to wait for it to decay naturally, with the only penalty the negative effects from corruption. The cost for rooting https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/out corruption depends on the autonomy
   modified development while the loan size depends on the unmodified development. With a high average autonomy (over 60%) debasing currency gives more money than it cost to root out the corruption.

Bankruptcyhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ strategy[edit | edit source]

   It is possible to go bankrupt inadvertently while still economically healthy (interest well below income) due to having many loans that are smaller than the current loan amount. To avoid this, debt restructuring is recommended, where you take out a few lhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/arger loans to pay off older, smaller ones. Since the inflation gain from renewing loans is https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/fixed per loan, not by loan size, this will also reduce the rate at which you gain inflation from renewing loans and thus the amount of administrative power you spend on reducing inflation.

   Deliberately going bankrupt, though dangerous, can be a powerful tool for restoring the economy if managed carefully. Try to have truces lasting at least 5 years with as many dangeroushttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ neighbors as possible, so they can't attack during bankruptcy. Before https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/declaring bankruptcy, spend all monarch points on developing provinces or boosting stability (to at least +1 – less will be wasted, the best is to boost stability to 3 beforhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/e declaring as bankruptcy reduces it by 3), as they will all be lost othttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/herwise. Ensure that no provinces are in the process of being cored. Colonies should be abandoned unless very close to completion (no provinces can be colonized during bankruptcyhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/). If planning bankruptcy, you should plan it at least 5 yearshttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ in advance and not build or upgrade any buildings in that 5 years, as they will be
   destroyed.

   Rebels are more difficult to fight while bankrupt due to the penalties to army morale, but can be beaten with enough numbers (just feed a series of small stacks one day apart into the same bathttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/tle – the small morale boost from fresh new troops will help win these costly bathttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/tles). Get stability back up to at least 1 (to avoid instability events) as soon as possible and also consider spending military points to raise legitimacy or republican tradition.

Inflation[edit | edit source]

   Ambox outdated info.png
   Please help with verifying or updating this section. It was last verified for version 1.24.

   In economics, inflation is an increase in the money supply which contributes to ahttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/n increase in the price of goods over time. In gameplay terms, inflation makes all expenses cost more. Low levels of inflation (around 10%), though not ideal, are reasonable. https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ Around 20% or higher, this could signify an economic catastrophe, and measures must be tahttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ken to avoid total collapse. However, as soon as inflation is 5+%, it's possible to get bad events because of the high inflation incurring stability drops or increased local autonomy.

   Contrary to real life, inflation in game does not mean constantly increasing prices, but rather a flat increase of the country's expenses. Some expenses, such as Advisor cost, behave more realistically, with a constant increase in their cost, but they are not called "inflation" in the game, or reflect how it works. In real life, certain incomes would increase with inflation as well. This reflects that the in game "ducats" have a constant value over the course of centuries and serve as an absolute indicator of value. The in-game inflation simply represents the inflation over the time between collecting income and spending it, therefore representing that the income has lost value while it was sitting in the country's treasury.

   Inflation applies as an additive modifier equal to its value to the following:
   Inflation effects
     * Construction cost
     * Fort maintenance
     * Mercenary cost
     * Infantry cost
     * Cavalry cost
     * Artillery cost
     * Heavy ship cost
     * Light ship cost
     * Galley cost
     * Transport cost
     * State maintenance
     * Advisor costs
     * https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/Institution embracement cost
     * Trade company investment cost
     * Center of trade upgrade cost
     * Missionary maintenance cost
     * Flhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/agship cost
     * Great project upgrade cost
     * Colonial type change cost modifier
     * Colonial subject type upgrade cost modifier
     * Colony cost modifier

   For Russia, it also applies its value divided by 100 to monthly modernization.

Gaining inflation[edit | edit source]

   Inflation is increased by the following:https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/
     * Each loan taken or extended increases infhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/lation by +0.10.
     * Income from gold increases inflation by 0.50 per year times the proportion of ihttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ncome from gold relative to 100% of total income. Accordhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ingly, assuming one has a Master of Mint, ensure that income from gold is less than 20% of total income so as not to increase inflation. Flag of Kilwa Kilwa idea 5: Gold of Sofala and Flag of Zimbabwe Zimbabwe idea 3: Gold Deposihttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ts decrease this amount by −20%.
     * Lump sums of monetary compensation claimed in a peace treaty (but not reparations) cause a one-time increase of inflation.
     * Selling provinces or ships to other nations
     * Receiving gifts from other nations
     * (Requires El Dorado.png El Dorado DLC) Receiving or plundering treasure fleets
     * Various events can increase inflation.

   These are all situations where the country's money supply is expanded. In economics, an expansion in the supply of money without corresponding economic growth causes https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/a decrease in its value, i.e. inflation. Before the middle of the 20th centhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ury, and certainly during the period of EU4, currency was only considered money to the extent that it was either made of or backed by gold (and silver, which is represented by gold in the game), which is why gold income (a direct injection of pure money) causes inflation.

   Estates^[1] are factions within the nation that influence domestic politics. Estates apply modifiers at the national level and may grant one-time bonuses or bonuses to specific provinces. They have two basic attributes: influence and loyalty; which depend on the amount of land they hold, event choices and several other factors.

   The influence and loyalty levels of an estate determine their power within the country and how they "react" to the player's actions with them. These can be seen in the nationwide bonuses or penalties provided by the estate, outcome effects of certain interactions provided through the estathttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/es, as well as their rebellion strength if worse comes to worst. Estates which grow too powerful can bring a disaster upon the nation. This may come into https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/effect by the estate seizing control of the country or breaking it apart.

   Estates can be granted privileges, which grant additional bonusehttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/s, but come with a price. Privileges can shape your nation in the early stages, but will likely become a burden while your country centralhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/izes its power and grows its administration. You can influence your estates by granting and revoking privileges, and by ceding them lands or confiscating themhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/.

   The lands that are not owned by any of your estates is your crownland. Having more crownland means having a more direct control https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/on your lands, but reducing the power of estates. Having less crownland means your estates will like you more and will be more impactful, but you will hhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ave a lesser control on your lands and your subjects.

   There are a total of 13 estates, though most nations have access to 3 estates. The exact number may chahttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/nge during the campaign and depends on location, government and religion. Conquered provinces will change the distribution of lands in your realms. It is possible to https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/add more estates to the game and change conquest behavior via modding.

   Each state begins with its own distribution of lands, and for somehttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ its own already active privileges, which can be changed during the game.

Estate modifiers[edit | edit source]

   Ambox outdated info.png
   Please help with verifying or updating this section. It was last verified for version 1.31.

   Note: Most of the values mentioned here are fully moddable.^[2]
     * Loyalty /eu4.paradoxwikis.com/img alt="Estate loyalty" src="images/a/a6/Estates_loyalty.png" decoding="ashttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ync" loading="lazy" width="24" height="24" data-file-width="24" data-file-height="24" /> is a measure of how willing the estate is to aid in the nation's government. It is a modifier that trends slowly towards a base value, the loyalty equilibrium, which is 30 per default and can be increased by the share of lands it controls and changed with privileges, governmenhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/t reforms and loyalty modifiers from other sources. The speed ofhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ decay depends on how far from the equilibrium it is (further = faster). Loyalty scales from 0 to 100, and is separated into three tiers: disloyal (0–29), neutral (30–59), and loyal (60−100). Loyalty determines what effects the estate confers. When disloyal, an estate confers only penalties; when neutral, it confers a single bonus; and when loyal it confers one or more
       additional bonuses. The strength of the effects is determined by the estate's influence.https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ Loyalty is affected by various national factors, events, decisions and territorial grants and revocations.
     * (Estate) influence Estate influence is a measure of how much power the estate has over the nation's government and scales from 0 to 100. Influence determines the strength of the national effects conferred by the estate's loyalty through four levels: 0−19 / 20−39 / 40−59 / 60−100. These levels modify the effects by a factor of 0.25 / 0.50 / 0.75 / 1. Moreover, if an estate's influence is 100 and its loyalty is below 50, the nation is at risk of the estate seizing power in a coup, in the form of a disaster. Each estate has a base level of influence, and is affected by privileges, various national factors, events, decisions, and the land share of the estate. Influence does not increase or decrease over time. If an estate's influence drops to 0, it will grant no nationwide effects but will still appear in the Estates interface.
     * Territory Estate territory https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/. Even though your estates have a certain share of the reahttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/lm land, no province is explicitly owned by an estate. An estate territory is thus represented only by the share of the realm land it holds. See the crownland sectionhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ below for ways to increase and reduce the land shares of the estates ahttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/nd the crown
     * Influence (calculation) is based on how much an estate controls the development in the country. Influence of an estate increases by 0.5 for every 1% of the land it chttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ontrols, up to a maximum of 40. The Dhimmi and Tribes esthttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ates have modifiers that lower this factor (0.25 for each 1% for the Dhimmi, and 0.2 for each 1% for the tribes).
     * Loyalty equilibrium (calculation) is based ohttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/n territorial grant/revocation. Loyalty equilibrihttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/um of an estate increases by 0.2 for every 1% of land it controls.
     * Privileges are a set of actions that can be taken towards estates, typically either giving something to the ehttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/state or requesting something from it. Interactions affect the estates' loyalty and influence in various ways, and almost all of them reduce Maximum absolutism maxhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/imum absolutism.
     * (Estate) Disasters occur after an estate gains high influence levels (100). The estate disaster will begin ticking if the associated estate has less than 50% Estate loyalty loyalty and the nation is not at war. Unless lowered, this will eventually trigger its associated disaster. During an active estate disaster all other estates will lose influence and loyalty.

Crownland[edit | edit source]

   Ambox outdated info.png
   Please help with verifying or updating this section. It was last verified for version 1.31.

   The land of a realm which has access to estates is divided among all the estates, and the crownland, which represents the land you directly control. These lands are not represented by specific provinces in game (and neither are the lands of the other estates).

   The share of crownland in the realm is linked to a series of bonuses which provide better benefits the higher this share is (as your realm becomes more centralized).

   Most nations start the campaign with a base value of 30% crownland. The Papal States are one of the few exceptions, instead starting with 50%. Nations such as those listed above whttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/hich do not use estate mechanics receive no crownland modifiers, https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/positive or negative.

  Changing crownland[edihttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/t | edit source]

  The game offers several ways to increase or decrease the amount of crownland:

    Seize land[edit | edit source]

  The Seize Land estate interaction can be used everyhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ 5 years and provides an instant 5% boost to crownland. The button is only available whehttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/n a nation is not at war, has no active revolts and no https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/rebel-controlled provinces. All estates lose 20% loyalty and a share of controlled land in proportion to the existing amount of land thathttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ they have (so that the ratio of land between estates doesn't change). If any estate's loyalty drops below 30% due to this, rebels will spahttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/wn. The amount of rebel stacks is
  [MATH: <semantics> <mrow class="MJX-TeXAtom-ORD"> <mstylehttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ displaystyle="false" scriptlevel="0"> <mn>1</mn> https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ <mo>+</mo> <mrow class="MJX-TeXAtom-ORD"> <mfrac> <mtext>number of owned areas</mtext> <mn>10</mn> </mfrac> </mrow> </mstyle> </mrow> <annotation encoding="applicatihttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/on/x-tex">{\textstyle 1+{\frac {\text{number of owned areas}}{10}}}</anhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/notation> </semantics> :MATH]
  {\textstyle 1+{\frac {\text{nhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/umber of owned areas}}{10}}} . The type of rebels depends on the disloyal estate. If there are multiple disloyal estates, the type of each rebel stack is randomly chosen between the rebel types of each disloyal estate. The rebelshttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ will spawn in provinces which have the highest supply limit of all ownhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ed provinces in their area and which have a land connection to the capital or are in a state. All provinces in the area in which rebels spawn get National unrest.png +10 local unrest.

  Some privileges exempt an estate from Seize Land. An exempt estate will neither lose land nor loyalty.

    Sale of titles[ehttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/dit | edit source]

   The Sale of Titles estate interaction can be used every 5 years to sell 10% of the crownland to the estates. The button is only available when a nation has no active revolts and no rebel-controlled provinces and the crownland share is at least 10%. All estates gain https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/10% loyalty and the sold crownland is distributed to the estates in proportion to the existing amount of land that they have (so that the ratio of land between estates doesn't change). The country gains Gold Icon.png ducats equal to X years of inhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/come multiplied by the sum of the land shares which all estates had befhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ore the button was pressed. X is 2.5 during the Age of Discovery.png Age of Discovery, 2.0 in the Age of Reformation.png Age of Reformation, 1.5 in the Age of Absolutism.png Age of Absolutism and 1.0 in the Age of Revolutions.png Age of Revolutions.
     * The "Ottoman Siyasah Tax System" government reform, available for the Flag of Ottomans Ottomans, makes it so that X is always 2.5.
     * The "Grant Land to the Monasteries" government reform, available for Orthodoxyhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ Orthodox nations, also increases https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ Patriarch authority.png patriarch authority by 5% when selling tithttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/les.
     * The common government reform "Superiority of the State", unlocked by completing Court idea group.png Court ideas, "Divihttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ded Aristocracy" available for Flag of Persia Persihttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/a and "Enforced Autocracy", available for Flag of Russia Russia, allows the nation to sell titles to a specific estate.
     * The Flag of Italy Italian "Unify Regional Economies" mission makes it so that selling Titles grants Administrative power.png +25 administrathttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ive power.

    Developing provinces[edit | edit source]

   In most circumstances, each Development.png development click increases the crownland by 0.2%.

   If one or more estates have zero (or near-zero) land, the amount of crownland gahttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ined per development click may be significantly lower than 0.2%, because what actually happens with each development click is each estate loses max(0, 0.2% × estate influence / total estate influenhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ce) land to the crown.^[3] When all estates have a significant amount of land, the overall gain in crownland is 0.2% (as above). However, if one or more estates have zero (or near-zero) land, then the floor at zero bites, and thttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/he amount of crownland gained per development click will be reduced – perhaps shttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ignificantly.

   Some privileges exempt an estate from losing crownland from developing provinces:

    Gaining new provinces[edit | edit source]

   Gaining new development through conquest or integration of subjects moves the land share of each estate towards an equilibrium which is determined by the relative influence of the estate compared to the other estates. The crown is considered to have an influence of 60 + Absolutism.png absolutism in percent. How fast the land share moves towards this equilibrium depends on the amount of newly acquired development compared to the total development of the country.

    Privileges[edit | edit source]

   Some privileges reduce the crownland by 5% or 10% when they are granted. This land share is added to the land of the estate which is granted the privilege. Revoking the privilege does not restore the crownland.

    Estate Statutory Rights[edit | edit source]

   The event Estate Statutory Rights has the option to grant the privilege of the same name to an estate. This privilege increases the crownland by 30% when granted, but it increases the Minimum autonomy.png minimum autonomy in fully cored state provinces by 25%. It can only be revoked after 20 years.

    Events and mission[edit | edit source]

   Several events change crownland or estate land shares. The Flag of Austria Austrian mission Balance the Estates and the Flag of Burgundy Burgundian mission Appease the Estates give Crownland.png +5% crownland.

  Crownland equilibrium[edit | edit source]

   Ambox outdated info.png
   Please help with verifying or updating thhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/is section. It was last verified for version 1.31.

   Every nation thahttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/t has at least one estate has an equilibrium for crownland. This equhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ilibrium for crownland is calculated by the estates' collective influence and the nation's current Absolutism.png absolutism. Each time the nation's total develhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/opment changes by conquest or annexation, each estate receiveshttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ or loses crownland in order to approach their personal equilibrium, and this in turn reflects the crown's equilibrium as a result. The larger the relative change in development, the larger the relative drift towards each party's equilibrium.

   The crown's equilibrium of crownland is essentially what remains after each estate's equilibrium is calculated. The formula for how much a specific estate's share of land changes after a change in development is as follows:
