   The tabs are, from top to bottom:

Manpowhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/er Icon.png Land units[edit | edit source/eu4.paradoxwikis.com/an class="mw-editsection-bracket">]

   https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/
   Macrobuilder view (tab 01 - Land units)

   This tab allows recruitment of land units.
     * Units shown are the oneshttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ chosen in the https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/"Tab military tab.
     * Units are displayed with stats and Gold Icon.png ducat cost (and for special units, how manyhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ are available).
     * At the bottom are displayed the Land forcelimit.png land force limit, and number of units currently owned and in production phttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/er unit type.
     * Hovering shows the number of regiments owned of that unit type and its Land maintenance modifier.png maintenance cost.
     * Choosing a unit will color-code the provinces (green / red according to whether those troops can be raised there) and display Gold Icon.png ducat cost and Time Icon.png time to build. Clicking on a green province will begin construction.
     * Provinces with unit construction in progress display pehttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/rcentage progress and number of units in the queue.
     * The second tab shows a list of Posshttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ible mercenaries.png mercenary https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/companies.
     * The third tab details currently defined army templates.
          + Selecting one highlights valid provinces with cost and time, and then clicking on a provhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ince begins construction of the template, setting that province as a rally point.
          + Only contiguous provinces will be used for unit construction, and only up to the limit set by the template.
          + Right-clicking deletes a temphttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/late.

Heavy ship.png Naval units[edit | https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/edit source]

   Macrobuilder view (tab 02 - Naval units)

   This tab allows recruitment of naval units.
     * Units shown are the latest available (see Diplomatic tech.png diplomatic technology for unit unlocks).
     * Units are displayed with stats, Gold Icon.png ducat and Sailors.png sailors cost.
     * At the bottom are displayed the Naval forcelimit.png naval force limit and amount of units in production/queue per unit type.https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/
     * Hovering shows amount of current unit type and it's Naval maintenance modifier.png naval maintenance.
     * Choosing a unit will color-codhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/e the provinces (green / red) and display Gold Icon.png ducat cost and Time Icon.png time to build. Clicking a green province then begins construction.
     * Provinces with unit construction in progress display percentage progress and amount of units in queue.
     * The section at the bottom details currently definhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ed army templates.
          + Selecting one highlights valid provinces with cost and time, and then clicking on a province begins construction of the template, setting that province as a rally point.
          + Only contiguous (bhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/y land) provinces will be used for unit construction, and only up to the limit set by the template.
          + Right-clicking deletes a template.
     * If Levhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/iathan.png Leviathan is active, the "Drafting Transports" Template will be found here, https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/for nations whose Government allows it.

https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ Core creation.png Province coring[edit | edit source]

   Macrobuilder view (tab 03 - Province coring)

   This tab allows coring of the uncored provinces in the nation.
     * Provinces are displayed with Development.png development, Overextension.png overextension and https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ Administrative power.png administrative power cost. Provinces in-progress of coring will show progress bar.
     * Hovering shows the province's percentage contribution (its weight) https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/to the current overextension level along with a break-down of thehttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ cost and time modifiers.

   Territorial cores are not shown unless they belong to state provinces.

Missionaries.png Religious conversion[edit | edit source]

   Macrobuilder view (tab 04 - Religious conversion)

   This tab allows conversion of provinces with non-state religion.
     * Provinces are displayed with current religion and Time Icon.png time to convert. Provinces in-progress of conversion will show progress bar.
     * Hovering shows current religion bohttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/nuses and expanded tooltip for Missionaries.png missionary strength.
     * Prospect provinces are colored green and display Missionaries.png missionary strength and Time Icon.png time to convert. Hovering shows expanded https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/tooltip.
     * Provinces in mid-progress display percentage progress.

Autonomy.png Local autonomy[edit | edit source]

   Macrobuilder view (tab 05 - Local autonomy)

   This tab allows decreasing/increasing of local autonomy in provinces.
     * Provinces are displayed with most likely rebel type to spawn, Local autonomy.png local autonomy and color-coded National unrest.png unrest levels (white / red).
     * Hovering shows effects and Time Icon.png duration (date) of desired action (an expanded tooltip as well).
     * Prospect provinces are colored /eu4.paradoxwikis.com/pan class="effect-green">green and display Local autonomy.png local autonohttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/my and color-coded National unrest.png unrest levels (white / red). Hovering shows expanded tooltip.
     * Provinces acted upon will be colored red for the duration of the action taken ( Time Icon.png 30 years).

Culture conversion cost.png Culture conversion[edit | edit source]

   Macrobuihttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/lder view (tab 06 - Culture conversion)

   This tab allows conversion of a province's culture. At the top there is a button to chose Culture icon.png culture to convert into (advanced culture chttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/onversion requires The Cossacks.png /eu4.paradoxwikis.com/a> DLC; without it, only primary culture is available). Selecting a culture will display only the provinces that can be converted into that culture.
     * Provinces are displayed with current culture color-coded for acceptance (grhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/een / yellow / red). Hovering over the culture shows current culture effects on province (from acceptance level).
     * A gold star indicates primary culture; https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/a silver star, accepted cultures; a bronze star, cultures in the primary culture group.
     * The next column shows Diplomatic power.png diplomatic power cost or, if already converting, a progress bar.
     * A button allows starting the conversion process. Hovering over it gives an expanded tooltip icnluding Time Icon.png time to convert.

   Macrobuilder view (tab 07 - Buildings)

   This tab ahttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/llows construction of buildings in provinces.
   /eu4.paradoxwikis.com/>

     Buildings are displayed with Gold Icon.png https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ ducat cost and upgrade path. Grayed-out buildings are not unlocked as of yet.

     Hovering shows effects of building and Time Icon.png time to build (also [28px-Fort_maintenance.png] fort maintenance for Fort https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/level.png forts). Grayed-out buildings display required technology to unlock.

     Choosing a building will color-code owned and subject provinces:
   /eu4.paradoxwikis.com/li>green: building can be built
     * yellow stripes: building can't be built because the province is busy (e.g. a missionary)
     * teal: building can upgrade another building that's already present
     * blue: building already present
     * red stripes: not enough money

     Choosing a building also displays remaining building slots, Gold Icon.png ducat cost, and, if relevant, effects on Global tradehttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ power.png trade power, Income.png income, State maintenance.png state maintenance, Manpower Icon.png manpower, Sailors.png sailors, Land forcelimit.png /eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ alt="Naval forcelimit.png" src="images/thumb/9/98/Naval_forcelhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/imit.png/28px-Naval_forcelimit.png" decoding="async" loading="lazy" width="28" height="28" data-file-width="48" data-file-height="48" /> force limits, and Trade https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/value.png trade value. Hovering shows Time Icon.png time to build and an expanded tooltip.

     Provinces in mid-progress display percentage progress.

Diplomatic power.png Diplomacy[edit | edit source]

   Macrohttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/builder view (tab 10 - diplomacy, showing the improve relations tab)
   Macrobuilder view (tab 10 - diplomacy, showing the alliance actions tab)
   Mandate of Heaven.png Available only with the Mandate of Heaven DLC enabled.

   This tab gives an overview of diplomatic actions that are available to the player. This tab has eight subhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/sidiary tabs, corresponding to seven of the categories of diplomatic actions plus improve relations.
     * Improve relations.png Improve Relations: This tab allows you to send diplomats to automatically improve relations with certain categories of country. Diplomats assigned https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/this way will choose a country to improve relations with and carry on until reaching +100 improved relations modifier, or in the case of the improve with Outraged Countries option, it only goes until the target country hashttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ positive opinion of the player, then the diplomat will switch to another if possible. If all counthttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ries in a category are already at maximum, the diplomat will sit idle. The buttons for any empty categories are greyed out.
          + Neighbouring Countries are any countries that share a land or sea border.
          + Own Subject Countries includes tributahttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ries but not trade league members.
          + Outraged Countries are countries whose opinion of you is impacted by Ae impact.png aggressive expansionhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ and have -50 or below aggressive expansion opinion.
          + Allies does not include subjects, guaranteed countries, or trade league members.
          + Threatening Countries includes any country that poseshttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ a threat.
     * The other tabs are Alliance.png Ahttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/lliance actions, Influence actions, Dynastic acthttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ions, Economy actions, Papal actions, Emperor actions, and Great Power actions. Each tab gives a list of possible actions; selecting one gives a list of countries, with Yes / No and acceptance numbers if applicable, and ineligible countrhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ies greyed out. Clicking a country enters diplomacy with that country with the appropriate option selected.

   The following interactions are not available here:
     * Offer Condottieri (alliance)
     * Enforce Peace (influence)
     * Threaten War (influence)
     * Send an Insult (relations)
     * Support Heir (dynastic)
     * All covert actions and access actions /eu4.paradoxwikis.com/li>Loan Offer (economic)
     * Sell Province (economihttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/c)
     * Sell Ships (economic)
     * Intervene in War (Great Power)
     * Break Alliance (Great Power)

     * Click on the save button when done.
     * To use a saved template click on it and choose an area to build in (the units will be built simultaneously in the surrounding provinces).

Missions

   From Europa Universalis 4 Wiki
   Jump to navigation Jump to search

   Please help with verifying or updating older sections of this article.
   At least some were last verified for version 1.34.

   Missions are tasks formatted as a "tree", with each completed task allowing the completion of another task in addition to a reward. There are many generic missions available to all nations, with others being available depending upon nation, culture, religion, or region.

   Missions are assigned whenever certain triggers happen, usually when starting the game or forming another nation. Whenever such a trigger happens the game checks the files for all missions the nations currently fulfills the conditions for and makes them available in the missions tab.

   Furthermore, Mission trees in the files are seperated into multiple sections, with every section occupying a dedicated slot in the mission tree (divided in rows and columns and assigend via coordinates with x being rows and y being columns). Each section may have its own conditions to be available to a nation. Thus a single nation may have missions from multiple files and not always all missions from a single file.

   If a nation qualifies for multiple sections that apply the same slot in the tree, the missions take priority equal to their order (alphabetical) in the files. Missions that are lower down have higher priority and will replace missions from further up. This is why "generic missions" are called "00_Generic_missions" in the files; they will always be at the very top and can thus even be replaced by other generic missions.

Non- specific missions[edit | edit source]

   By default if nothing else applies, nations get access to the generic missions. These tables list all the different sections from all files, as long as the sections conditions arent related to tags.

Generic missions[edit | edit source]

   For Trees that have the "generic = yes" tag. They will be replaced by any other applicable missions that occupy the same slot.

            Mission tree                               Missions count                                            Conditions                           DLC      Notes

     * Technology is in Chinese group

     * Capital is in North/South America or in the RNW
     * Technology group is High American

   Northwestern natives missions 5
     * Government is Native Tribe
     * Primary culture is Athabascan, Chinook, Haida or Salish

   Northeastern natives missions 6
     * One of the following:
          + Primary culture is Chiwere or Osage
          + Culture is in the Central Algonquian, Eastern Algonquian or Iroquoian group
     * Is not Flag of Cherokee Cherokee or Flag of Tuscarora Tuscarora.

   Plains natives missions       5
     * One of the following:
          + Primary culture is Chipewyan, Kiowa or Shoshone
          + Culture is in the Caddoan, Plains Algonquian, or Siuan group
     * Primary culture is not caddo, chiwere or osage

   California natives missions   5
     * Government is Native Tribe
     * Primary culture is Yokuts

   Southwestern natives missions 6
     * Culture is in the Apachean or Sonoran group
     * Primary culture is not Kiowa or Shoshone

Nation specific missions[edit | edit source]

   Mission count is determined by calculating the maximum amount of missions the respective nation can have in a single campaign, the number in brackets shows the total amount of missions the nation can have by adding all the branches together.

Monarch power

   From Europa Universalis 4 Wiki
   Jump to navigation Jump to search

   Please help with verifying or updating#20303B;">

   Please help with verifying or updating older sections of this article.
   At least some were last verified for version 1.28.
   Wiki letter w.png
   Please help improve this article or section by expanding it with: a section about ‘all power cohttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/sts’ modifier.

   Monarch power is a measurhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/e of a ruler's influence and ability to govern their country with the help of advisors. It is a central mechanic in Europa Universalis IV, influencing how effective a country is at technological improvements, diplomatic relations, and infrastructure investments.

   There are three types of monarch power:
     * Administrative power.png Administrative power represents the internal organization and development of a country.
     * Diplomatic power.png Diplomatic power represents the external influencehttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ of a country, including diplomacy, naval power, trade, exploration or colonization.
     * Military power.png Military power represents innovations and leadership for armies.

   [ ]

All power costs modifier[edit | ehttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/dit source]

   Ambox outdated info.png
   Please help withttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/h verifying or updating this section. It was last verified for version 1.34.

   This modifier changes the cost for every transaction involving monarch power. If your net All Power Costs Modifier is +15% All power costs.png , then a province that would normally cost 100 Administrative power.png Administrative Power to make a Core Icon.png core would cost 115. However, this doesn't affect scripted amounts of points lost through negative events. Disasters like The Fall of Majapahit and The Cambodian Dark Age and some estate privileges increase this modifier. Ways to decrease All Power Costs Allhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ power costs.png are Innovativeness( −0.1% All power costs.png per 1 Innovativeness.png up to −10% All power costs.png on 100 Innovativeness.png ), −10% All power costs.png All Powers Costhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ for activating Golden Era and by picking the All power costs.png administrative idea in custom nation designer up to −10% All power costs.png All Powers Cost. There are ahttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/lso two government reforms for
   rephttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ublics and some missions and events which reduce this modifier.

Generating monarch power[edit | edit source]

   Ambox outdated info.png
   Please help with verifying or updating this section. It was last verified for version 1.28.https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/

   Monarch power is generated at the beginning of each month. There are four sources of monarch power: ruler, country, advisors, and power projection. Based on these factors, the monarch power gain ofhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ each type can range from 2 to 20 (up to +6 from ruler, +5 from advisor, +2 from national focus, +1 from power projection, +1 from estate, +1 from alcheringa cult “The Rainbow Serpent” or from some sikh gurus, +1 from a custom nation national idea and +3 base https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/value) a month.

   By default a country can only store an amount of monarch power of each type equal to 999, increased by unembraced Institutions and by Corruption.

Generic Sources[edit | edit source]

   By default a cohttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/untry will generate 3 of every monarch power every month. This can be in- or decreased by various factors.
   Monthly administrative power.png Traditions Ideas Bonuses Policies
   +1                               —
     * PLC idea 5: Refinement of Golden Liberty

   —                                —
   Monthly diplomatic powehttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/r.png Traditions Ideashttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ Bonuses Policieshttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/
   In patch 1.37 no https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ideas and policies have the modifier “monthly diplomatic power”
   Monthly military power.png Traditions Ideas Bonuses Policies
   +1                         —
     * Egyptian idea 2: Training Missions in Egypt

   —                          —

   Some missions grant monthly monarch power:

   Administrative:

   Requires Domination DLC: The Prussian mission "Renovate Berlin" adds a modifier "Palace of Berlin" granting +1 monthly administrative power until an enemy sieges or conquers the province Berlin (50).

   The Aragonese mission "The War of the Remences" grants the modifier "Internal Reforms" fhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/or 20 years giving +1 monthly administrative power.

   The French mission "Condorcet's Grandes Écoles" grants the modifier "“Funded the Reforms of Condorcet”https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/" giving +1 monthly administrative power for the rest of the game.

   The French mission "Burgundian Succession" if completed by owning thehttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ required provinces grants "Reintegration of the Burgundian Lands” fhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/or 20 years giving +1 monthly administrative power.

   The French mission "Protector of Catholicism" grants the modifier "Catholic Head of State" until the ruler's death giving +1 monthly administrative power.

   The Lubeckian mission "Safeguard the Salt Road" grants the modifier "Lower Saxohttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/n Drittel" for 15 years giving +1 monthly administrative power.

   The Manchurian mission "Factionhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/al Stability" grants the modifier "Five Trusted Companions" for 20 years giving +1 monthly administrative power.

   The Venetian mission "Unify Italy" grants the modifier "Italian Unification" for 20 years giving +1 monthly administrative power.

   Diplomatic:

   The Mughal mission "Western Allies" if completed with a Diplomat advisor, grants the modifier "Friends in https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/High Places" for 5 years giving +1 monthly diplomatic power.

   The Venetian mission "The Francocracy" grants the modifier "Conquest of Constantinople" for 15https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ years giving +1 monthly diplomatic power.

   Military:

   The Byzantine mission "Beyond the Alps" if completed before the age of reformation has passed grants the modifier "Caesarean Conquestshttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/" for the rest of the game granting +1 monthly military power.

   The Finnish mission "Defend Independence"https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ grants the modifier "End of the Great Thunder" until ruler's death giving +1 monthly military power.

   The Frenchhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ mission "Push the Imperial Line" grants the modifier "Victory in Ghttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ermany" for 25 years giving +1 monthly military power.

   The Timurid mission "Fresh Blood" grants the modifier "Fresh Blood" for 15 years giving +1 monthly military power.

   Government reforms and interactions can also grant monthly monarch power:

   For Zoroastrians, the Monarchy tier 1 government reform "Asha Monarchy, the Monarchy/Theocracy/Republic tier 4 government reform "Embrace the Concept of Free Will," and the Theocracy tier 1 government reform "Zoroastrian Theocracy" enables the "Three Royal Fires" mechanic.
     * "Adur Farnbag" interaction grants +1 monthly administrative power.
     * "Adur Burzhen Mirh" interaction grants +1 monthly diplomatic power.
     * "Adur Gushnasphttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/" interaction grants +1 monthly military power.
       Additionally, having 100 Asha Vahishta grants an additional +1 monthly power to the above interactions.
       Each interaction reduces Asha Vahishta by 50 and resets progress in that interaction to zero, and lasts for 10 years.
       The Monarchy government reform "System of Councils" enables the "System of Councihttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ls" mechanic.

     * "Call the Royal Council" grants +1 monthly administrative power.
     * "Call the Council of State" grants +1 monthly diplomatic power.
     * "Call the Council of War" grants +1 monthly military power.

   Each interaction costs 50 Council Consensus and lasts for 10 years.

   The Monarchy tier 2 government reform "Nob#39; Electorate">Nobles' Electorate" a noble regency grants +1 monthly power to each category.

   The Monarchy tier 6 government reform "Justicia de Aragón" gives +1 monthhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ly administrative power.

   Native tribes can enact the reform "Land Tradition" granting +1 monthly administrative power.

Advisors[edit | edit source]

   A country can have an advisor for each power type. Each advisor starts by providing 1–3 monarch points each month. An advisor's maintenance cost starts at 1 ducat a month for a +1 point advisor at the game's starting date. The cost increases quadratically with advisor skill level, and slowly inflates by 0.5% per game year. It is also modified by inflation.
   Cradle of Civilization.png Available only with the Cradle of Civilization DLC enabled.

   Advisors can be promoted for 5 yehttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ars' of their salary to increase their monarch point generation by +1 up to a max of 5 monarch points.

Power projection[edit | edit source]

   Having at least 50 Power Projection.png power projection provides an extra +1 points a month for all monarch power types.

Increasing monarch power[edit | edit source]

   There are no percentage modifiers to monarch power, though there are effects that modify the cost of specific acthttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ions that require monarch power. The most flexible of https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/these are advisor choices; a rich country could temporarily hire an appropriate advisor to get a discount on an immediate purchase.

   Monarch power gains are much more independent of the size of a country than other resources such as monetary income and size of military, but large countries often require expending more power on additional provinces and military maneuvers. However, there are a few ways of increasing a country's monarch power, particularly if the country has some other resource to spare:
     * Hiring more skilled advisors increases monarch power production at the cost of Gold Icon.png ducats.
     * Many rhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/andom events have an option to gain or lose monarch power. Often (but not always) this is offset with a corresponding loss or gain of some other resource.
     * Republics can re-elect leaders to gain skill in each category at the cost of Repuhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/blican tradition.png republican tradition, or elect https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/a different ruler for a different distribution of skills. With the tier 2 reform "Political Dynasties", one can elect a ruler with random skills that are worse than a monarch on average, but may be better than a normal starting republican ruler (requires Dharma.png Dharma DLC). Other types of government can try to manipulate the heir mechanics through random events, or in the extreme case, arranging for the death of https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/an unwanted ruler or heir in combat.
     * Increasing and maintaining Power Projection.png phttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ower projection of at least 50 by maintaining and acting aggressively towards rivals provides a bonus, at the cost of long-running and often bloody feuds.
     * Most estates can be granted privileges that increase monarch point generation at the cost of −5% loyalty equilibrium and −10% crownland. Clergy estates or their equivalent grant +1 administrative points, Burghers or their equivalent grant +1 diplomahttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/tic points, and Nobles or their equivalent grant +1 military points.
     * Great powers gain a diplomatic option called Influence Nation that allows them to payhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ one year's worth of income to grant +1 monarch power to a target independent non-great power nation in their weakest category for 10 years.
     * Monarchies can abdicate (in favour of a better heir) at the cost of https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ Prestige.png 50 prestige and 20 Legitimahttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/cy.png legitimacy. /eu4.paradoxwikis.com/li>Monarchies can dishinerit a bad heir at the cost of Prestige.png 50 prestige/eu4.paradoxwikis.com/li>

   The Cossacks.png Available only with the The Cossacks DLC enabled.
     * Steppe nomads can gain monarch power by razing non-core provinces, reducing its development. This gives +25 power modified by military technology of the appropriate category for each point of development lost.

   Cradle of Civilization.png Available only with the Cradhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/le of Civilization DLC enabled.
     * Promoting your advisors https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/increases monarch power production at the cost of Gold Icon.png ducats.

   Some situations cahttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/n cause a monthly loss of monarch points:
     * Too many diplomatic relationships: having treaties with more countries than a nation's diplomatic relations cap will result in a monthly loss of diplomatic power, equal to the numbers of relations above the limit. The number of diplomatic relation slots can be increased through selecting idea groups, nahttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/tional ideas, or other modifiers.
     * In the same way, having too manhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/y military leaders will also result in a monthly loss of military power, equal to the number of leaders above the limihttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/t. The number of military leaders without upkeep can be increased by ideas, traditions, and https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/policies, by embracing Feudalism, by increasing and maintaining power projection of at least 25, by increasing government rank to Empire and other factors.

National focus[edithttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ | edihttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/t source]

   Countries can set a national focus on any of the three mohttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/narch power types. The chosen monarch power type receives +2 per month (added to the base gain), while othhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/er two monarch power types decrease by −1 each month. A focus does not change the overhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/all amount of monarch power generated per month, it merely redisthttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ributes it. How often the national focus can be removed or changed dehttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/pends on the country's Government rank: Duchy = 25 years, Kingdom = 20 yearhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/s, Empire = 15 years.

   This allows a country to catch up faster if behind in a specific technology (especially with Military tech.png Military technology, which has a huge impahttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ct) or to fill out ideas more quickly. Always be aware ofhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ the country's ruler though, because they still https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/play an important role. For example, the current ruler may have very good administrative skhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ill, whereas the heir may be unbalanced and only have 1 or even 0 administrative skill. Due to this, and particularly since changing the national focus takes a long time, planning ahead is essential.

Monarch power cap[edit |https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ edit source]

   The amount of each type of monarch power that a country can have at a given time is limited by a cap. This cap is the same for all power types ( Adhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ministrative power.png Ahttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/dministrative, Diplomatic power.png Diplomatic and [Military_power.png] Military). The default valhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ue for this cap is 999 power; however, not having embraced Institutions.png Institutions will increase the cap's value, to 999 × (100% + current tech penalty from institutions). Embracing an institution causes the cap to decrease, but never lohttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/wer than the largest monarch power stockpile. As that stockpile is spent, the cap will decrehttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ase until it reaches the result of the formula above. Thus, https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/accrued monarch power is never lost; the cap prevents only new monarch power generation (including from events and interactions).

   From Europa Universalis 4 Wiki

       Combat sequence[edit | edit source]

       Ambox outdated info.png

   Please help with verifhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ying or updating this section. It was last verified for version 1.30.
       The conclusion to a naval engagement
       Like land warfare, naval combat occurs when opposing fleets confront each other in the same sea province. Also like land battles, these sea battles can go on for many days, so they should be considered not as a single enghttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/agement, but as two fleets maneuvering to gain wind, standing off and skirmishing . A sea battle will last until one side is routed or annihilated. Patch 1.16 also introduced the concept of a nhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/aval combat width, and much like its land cousin it is the total number of ships that can engage the enemy at any one time.
       Engagement[edit | edit source]
       While there is an ongoing naval battle, fleet's ship will try to populate its engagement width until the limit is reached, in the following order:

    1. Heavy ships
    2. Galleys
    3. Light ships
    4. Transports

   Any ships already disengaged will be ignored, and galleys gain priority over heavy ships when battling in inland seas.

   Importanhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/tly, any ships in excess of the engagement width are placed in reserve (until they replace those destroyed or disengaged) where they suffer morale damage although not in the fight. Therefore be sure to rather time adding smaller fresh and high morale reinforcements during each phase of the battle than merely throwing one full stack at the enemy.

Phases[edit | edit source]

   Combat is divided into a series of 3-day phases where the phases alternate between fire and shock, with the fire phase happening first. Therefore each 6 days (after a full cycle of fire and shock) it may be best to try and reinforce the engagement width line with fresh reinforcements as others have been lost or disengaged during these two phases. Staying in reserve in the backline causes severe morale reductions, even while not fighting. So timing reinforcements to match the phases is generally better than depending on ships in reserve.

Target selection[edit | edit source]

   Targeting, and specifically combined targeting, is why the "cannon:hull strength" ratio together with the relative combat width is so important in determining the outcome of a naval battle.

   In combat each ship in the fronhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/t line (all ships up to the engagement width) will try to find a target and make an attack. Every enemy ship has a base chance of 10 to be picked as a target, further modified by:
     * +0 to +5 random chance
     * +5 if same type (hence heavies are more likely to target other heavies, and galleys to target other galleys)
     * x0.1 if morale at 0 or less
     * x2 if hull strength is less than 50% (hence their appeal is doubled, resulting in many ships focusing fire or "ganging up" on the same weaker targets)

   The enemy ship with the highest score https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/is selected as a target. If the previous target is about to die, a new one will be targeted. This group focus on the weaker onhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/es below 50% to push them to zero is why a battle can so quickly turn; normally as one runs out of reinforcements or ships in reserve and those still remaining in the fight have their morale collapse en masse.

   Note that unless a ship disengages it may remain in the combat width line-up at near zero value, inhibiting a fresher high-strength ship to replace it in the combat width. This makes increases in disengagement chances very valuable.

   The successful outcome of this combined targeting can be enhanced by your maximizing the number of cannons to target (from sending in higher quality ships - whether heavies or galleys, and from having a disproportionately higher engagement width than the enemy) as Cannons/Target Hull is the key factor in both the Final Damage and Morale Loss calculations.

Die roll[edit | edit source]

   At the beginning of each phase, each side rolls a die. The result is used to determine the morale damage and hull damage inflicted by that side during each of the three days of that phase. Some ideas and the wooden wall naval doctrines give a bonus to the die roll when fighting off an owned coast.

   Naval combat bonus off owned coast Traditions Ideas Bonuses Policies
   +1                                 —
     * Barbary Corsair idea 3: Vengeful Refugees
     * Eora idea 5: The Sacred Shore
     * Malayan idea 4: Chart the Isles
     * Norse idea 2: Norse Seamen

Hull damage[edit | edit source]

   Base damage is calculated according to the following formula:

   [MATH: <semantics> <mrow class="MJX-TeXAtom-ORD"> <mstyle displaystyle="true" scriptlevel="0"> <mi>B</mi> <mi>a</mi> <mi>s</mi> <mi>e</mi> <mi>H</mi> <mi>u</mi> <mi>l</mi> <mi>l</mi> <mi>D</mi> <mi>a</mi> <mi>m</mi> <mi>a</mi> <mi>g</mi> <mi>e</mi> <mo>=</mo> <mn>0.025</mn> <mo>+</mo> <mn>0.025</mn> <mo>⋅</mo> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mn>2</mn> <mo>+</mo> <mi>D</mi> <mi>i</mi> <mi>c</mi> <mi>e</mi> <mo>+</mo> <mi>C</mi> <mi>o</mi> <mi>m</mi> <mi>b</mi> <mi>a</mi> <mi>t</mi> <mi>M</mi> <mi>o</mi> <mi>d</mi> <mi>i</mi> <mi>f</mi> <mi>i</mi> <mi>e</mi> <mi>r</mi> <mi>s</mi> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> </mstyle> </mrow> <annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{\displaystyle BaseHullDamage=0.025+0.025\cdot (2+Dice+CombatModifiers)}</annotation> </semantics> :MATH]
   {\displaystyle BaseHullDamage=0.025+0.025\cdot (2+Dice+CombatModifiers)} ,

   where Combat Modifiers include the Artillery Fire Modifier, Naval Doctrine Bonus (England) and Admiral pip value difference (between 0 to 6) for that phase of the battle. Ship Combat Ability and Admiral Combat Ability are modifiers applied in the Final Damage formula.

   The amount of cannons of the attacking vessel affects the hull damage dealt and the hull strength (hull size) of the defender decides how long it can stand the cannon fire.

   The Artillery Fire Modifier gives a bonus or penalty to damage dealt depending on if attacker or defender has a technological advantage (with reference not to its Diplomatic Tech, but rather to its Military Tech, and therefore to the relative difference between each side's artillery damage modifiers). For example, jumping from tech 21 to tech 22 relative to your enemy in fact means a cumulative artillery fire difference of +2 (+4.4 vs. +2.4), which doubles this modifier.
     * Attacking unit modifier: The attack modifier from the attacking unit's technology, i.e. "Artillery Fire".

   Artillery Fire Modifier = Attacker Artillery Fire - Target Artillery Fire
     * Attacking unit Combat Ability: Any Combat Ability bonuses the attacking unit has.

   {\displaystyle FinalDamage=0.03\cdot BaseHullDamage\cdot ShipStrength\cdot {\frac {Cannons}{TargetHull}}\cdot (1+0.05\cdot ArtilleryFireModifier)\cdot {\frac {1+ShipCombatAbility+CombatAbilityfromAdmiral}{1+TargetShipDurability}}}

   If target ship Morale is 0 or below, Final Damage is multiplied by 10.

   Importantly, note that since Ship Durability is the denominator (and therefore affecting all the factors), one can drastically reduce the damage taken by having any modifiers that increase durability. For example, the 5% from the Corvettes Idea under Quality.

   Galleys fighting in the inland sea have their Final Damage doubled. Which means that in inland seas, instead of fighting 3 galleys, one heavy is effectively fighting 6. Hence it's best to match galleys to galleys in inland seas and try and maximise your engagement width using a high pip manoeuvre admiral. Having a naval reformer advisor to boost morale will help too.

Unit pips[edit | edit source]

          Main article: Naval units

   Each ship has stats in three categories: Icon hull size.png Hull, Icon ship cannons.png Cannon, and Icon ship speed.png Speed.

   Hull is the defensive stat, and cannons the offensive stat. With the exception of Morale, every combat phase the hull/cannon pips are used against each other to calculate the number of hull damage of each combat phase. Therefore, the damage sustained by the hulhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/l is directly proportional to the number of cannons firing at it.

Concluding a battle[edit | edit source]

   A naval battle ends when one side is either:
     * Reduced to 0 morale; or
     * Flees from combat; or
     * Annihilated (stack wiped)

   Upon victory, ships from the defeated fleet may be captured, depending on your chance to "capture enemy ship" (during a battle, hover your cursor over this percentage in the top right of the battle popup). Your capture chance is affected by selecting "ship boarding" as your naval doctrine (providing you a 33% chance of capturing a ship), ideas such as the "reconquista of the sea" of The Knights (15% chance), policies from Naval&Diplomatic (33%), and the relative maneuver skill difference between the admirals of the two fleets. Generally very few or no ships will be captured for leaderless (0 vs. 0 maneuver) battles.

   If the defeated fleet still has ships remaining, it will escape to the nearest friendly port tohttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ repair and recover its morale. Naval battles, like land battles, may cause war exhaustion as well as affect warscore, naval tradition and prestige. Note that warscore gained from naval battles will gehttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/nerally be insignificant compared to those gained by its land counterparts.

   In the event that more than one nation is on the winning side of a battle, the largest fleet on that side will receive any captured ships.

   Several ideas increase the chance of capturing ships after a battle:

Moralhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/e and strength[edit | edit source]

Morale[edit | edit source]https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/

          "Morale of navies" redirects here. For bonuses that increase naval morale, see § Max naval morale above.

   Morale ishttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ an important factor in fighting battles. Each turn of combat a unit will take a Morale hit. Once a fleet's average Morale value has been reduced to zero the fleet will attempt to retreat. Retreat cannot happen until both a fire and a shock phase have completed, so a fleet that has its morale reduced to 0 before that point will be destroyed.

   If a fleet loses a battle while having low enough morale, they will be forced to retreat to a port of the nearest sea province. While retreatinhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/g, it cannot be engaged in combat or be controlled until it reaches the sea province, nor will it repair. The fleet will also move 50% faster, and will recover https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/morale at a normal rate during the retreat.

   After every battle is fought a fleet must spend some time not fighting for its morale to recover.

Morale recovery[edit | edit source]

   Every month when docked at a home port, a shhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ip recovers a 10% of its maximum morale.

   Certain National Ideas, Idea groups and policies will increase naval morale recovery.
   Recover navy morale speed.png Traditions Ideas Bonuses Policies
   +25%                          —

   Each point of navalhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ tradition also increases naval morale recovery by +0.1%.

Unit strength[edit | edit source]

   Unit strength is an importanhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/t factor in fighting sea battles. Naval unit strength affects how long it can stand cannon fire befohttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/re sinking. Each turn of combat a unit will take hull damage reducing its strength.

   Galleys gain a bonus of 100% strength in inland seas^[3] and a bonus of 50% strength in coastal sea tiles which are not in inland seas^[4]. The inland seas are shown below in pale blue, the coastal seas in blue and open seas in dark blue.
   Terrain map.

Ship rhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/epair[edit | edit source]

   Fleets that have suhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/stained damage will automatically repair up to their full strength when dochttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ked in an owned, allied, or in a province with fleet basing rights. There is a 'repair damaged' button that will detach damaged ships and send them to a nearby port to repair, https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/when they are back up to full strength they will rejoin the fleet.

          Main article: Navy#Ship_Repair

Starhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/t patrolling /eu4.paradoxwikis.com/span>[edit | edit source]

   Unihttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/tpanel button enable patrol.png https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ The start patrolling button orders a fleet to loop its current movement order: when it reaches the finahttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/l destination of its current set of movement ordehttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/rs, it will automatically head back to the point where the patrol was started. Patrol routes can include port visits, where the patrol stops until all ships are repaired. While thttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/he same function can be fulfilled by light ships assigned to protecting trade nearby, patrols are not limithttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ed by ship type, trade power, or trade range.
   /eu4.paradoxwikis.com/>Coastal Raiding /eu4.paradoxwikis.com/an class="mw-editsection-bracket">[edit | edit source/eu4.paradoxwikis.com/span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]
   https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ Mare Nostrum.png Golden Century.pnhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/g Lions of the North.png Available only with Mare Nostrum, Golden Century, or Lions of the North DLC enabled.
   https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/

   Coastal Raiding is a naval ability which allows fleetshttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ belonging to nations with the Raid Coasts idea to raid the coasts of other nations for Gold Icon.png loot (ducats) and Sailors.png sailors.

   Historically, this ability reflects the raids carried out by Barbary pirates which were active in the Mediterranean Sea during the mid-16th to early 19th centuries while in the case of the three Pirate Republics, it simulates the Golden Age of Piracy in the Caribbean Sea from the mid-16th to the early 18th century. Flag of So So is a special case, as it represents a resurgence of the Japanese Wokou Pirates that raided the coasts of East Asia intermittently from the 4thttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/h century to the 17th century.

   Raiding can provide a signihttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ficant early-game boost to the income and sailor pools of nations that can do it and can also serve as a way to damage the economy of other nations. An example of this is Flhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ag of So So, which can employ Coastal Raiding against Flag of Ming Ming to pile up devastation and cause Ming to potentially lose the Mandate.png Mandate of Heaven and collapse.

Mechanism[edit | edit source]

   https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/""
   Raiding coasts as Morocco.

   A fleet can raid a https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/coastal province if all of the following is true:
     * The raiding nation “may raid coastshttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/� (see below).
     * The https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/raider must be able to place a fleet in a sea tile adjacent to the province (but doesn't need to be able to blockade the port).
     * The target province fulfills all the following conditions:
          + Is no more than three sea tiles away from a province owned by the raiding nation. This can be increased with the modifier “Coastal raiding range”/eu4.paradoxwikis.com/i> present in the 2nd Piratical idea).
          + Has a Development.png development lower than or equal to the blockading power of the raiding fleet.
          + Is not owned by a country which has a truce with the raiding nation.
          + Is not of the religion of the raiding nation or belongs to a country with the same religion as the raiding nation (unless the contrary is specifiedhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ by the “May raid coasts including coasts of countries with same religion” ability).
          + Is not controlled by a “friend” (subject, overlord, subject of the overlord, ally, subject of ally, in the same trade league, country with above 100 opinion) of the raiding nation.
          + Has not the “Raided Coast” modifier.

   When a coast is raided, the loot provided is the sum of the available loot of the provinces eligible fohttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/r raid, as follows:
     * As much Gold Icon.png ducats as available loot (i.e. Development.png development affected by Available loot.png available loot modifiers).
     * Sailors.png Sailohttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/rs amounting to the Local sailors modifier.png local sailors reserves divided by 4./eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ul>
       After a province has been raided, its loot bar is emptied, the amount of Devastation icon.png devastatihttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/on is increased by 10%, and thttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/he “Raided Coast” modifier is applied for ten years. Each raided province will add a Opinion.png −25 opinion penalty with the raided country (up to a maximum of −100), decaying by +1 per year.
       Raiding efficiency is reduced by the number of guns foreign fleets on Hunt pirates.png pirate hunting patrol have, comhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/pared to the raiding fleet.

    /eu4.paradoxwikis.com/an class="mw-headline" id="Blockading">Blockading[edit | edit source]
       Fleets will automatically blockade a coastal sea province under hostile control while they are statiohttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/nary and have no other orders.
       Blockade power[edit | edit source]
       The blockade power (sail speed in the tooltip) of a fleet is displayed after the Blockade enemy ports.png blockade icon in the fleet panel. It is mainly determined by the Icon ship speed.png tactical movement speed of the fleet's ships.

                [MATH: <semantics> <mrow class="MJX-TeXAtom-ORD"> <mstyle displahttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ystyle="true" scriptlevel="0"> <mrow class="MJX-TeXAtom-ORD"> <mtexhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/t>blockade power</mtext> </mrow> <mo>=</mo> <mrow class="MJX-TeXAtom-ORD"> <mfrac> <mrow> <mo>∑</mo> <mrow class="MJX-TeXAtom-ORD"> <mtext>speed of ship</mtext> </mrow> </mrow> <mn>3</mn> </mfrac> </mrow> <mo>⋅</mo> <mrow class="MJX-TeXAtom-ORD"> <mtehttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/xt>blockade efficiency</mtext> </mrow> </mstyle> </mrow> <annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{\displaystyle {\text{blockade power}}={\frac {\sum {\text{speed of ship}}}{3}}\cdot {\text{blockade efficiency}}}</annotation> </semantics> :MATH]
                {\displaystyle {\text{blockade power}}={\frac {\sum {\text{speed of ship}}}{3}}\cdot {\text{blockade efficiency}}}

       Each point of blockade power will be able to blockade one development point of a province.

               Ship type          Tactical speed Blockade power
       Heavy ship.png Heavy ships 5              5
       Light ship.png Light ships 10             10
       Galley.png Galleys         8              8
       Transport.png Transports   5              5
       Blockades will only take effect if there is enough blockade power to match the full development. If a fleet does not have enohttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ugh blockade power to blockade all adjacent provinces under hostile control, it will assign its blockade power in precedence of:

     * Hostile province under a siege lead by any friendly force
     * Hostile province with the lowest development
     * Hostile rebel province with the lowest development

   The detach blockade button ( Detach blockahttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/de.png ) in the fleet panel will detach a fleet of sufficient size to blockade all enemy ports neighboring the sea province.

Blockade force required[edit/eu4.paradoxwikis.com/n class="mw-editsection-divider"> | edit source]

   In order to properly https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/blockade a province with your fleet (i.e. inflict the effects of a blockade on the province), the blockade power has to be at least the development of the province. The "Coastal Defence" and "Naval Battery" increase the rehttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/quired blockade power according to their modifers. For example, if your coastal province has 20 development and you have a Naval Battery in the province, the enemy fleet will need to have a blockadehttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ power of 40 in order to give the full blockade effects to the province. In essence, the 'Blockade Force Required' modifier increases the threshold for blockade power to fully blockade the province.

   Blockade force required is determined by:
   Blockade force required.png             Conditions              Required Blockade Power
                           +50% Coastal defence.png Coastal defence Multiplied by 1.5
                          +100% Naval battery.png Naval battery     Multiplied by 2

Effects of blockade[edit | edit source]

   A blockade has a number of effects on any neighbouring land provinces occupied by an enemy:
   Local recruitment time.png  +20%                               Locahttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/l recruitment time
   Local shipbuilding time.png +20%                               Local shipbuilding time
   Local devastation           +0.25/eu4.paradoxwikis.com/td>     Monthly devastation
   Local trade power.png       https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/−100% Local trade power
   https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/

   Notably, provinces producing Spices.png Spices get negative monthly devastation that exactly counteracts the positive modifier from blockades.

   Blockading a country's ports also applies the following modifier, scaled by proportion of (core, state) development blockaded:
   Monthly war exhaustion.png +0.10 Monthly war exhaustion

   Being 100% blockaded also gives the following Debuffs :
     * −75% Global trhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ade power.png Global Trade Power
     * −75% Trade steering.png Trade Steering

   /eu4.paradoxwikis.com/>Blockades have the following further effects:
     * Siege: −2 penalty to die rolls in non-blochttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/kaded coastal provinces, except those owned by primitives. (Provinceshttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ without ports, e.g. on the Caspian Sea, don't count.)
     * War score: Blockahttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/des are worth war score scaling with the proportion of development they rephttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/resent and local autonomy. Capital and fortified provinces are worth more. Some casus belli have blochttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/kades as a war goal.
     * Spoils of War: Blockades add Gold Icon.png ducats to the blockader's treasury (listed under "Spoils of https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/War") in proportion to the province's income.
     * Restriction of movement: See § Blocking a straihttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/t below.

Blocking a strait[edit | edit source]

   To block a strait the following requirements must be met:
     * The blockading alliance or a neutral nation have to control (owns or occupied) at least one side of the adjacent provinces
     * The blockading alliance have to control the sea by a naval force (blockade efficiency doesn't matter)

   As a consequence, if a war allhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/iance controls both sides of the strait they can march over regardless of blockades.

   Examples:
     * A war participant controlling both sides of a strait: The Ottomans can cross the strait at Bohttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/sphorus as long as they have control of Constantinople and Kocaeli even when the enemy controls the sea. Same system applies for the second strait between Gelibolu and Biga.
     * A neutral nation controlling a side of a strait: Ulster, controlling Ulaidh, cannot cross the strait across the Irish Sea to Ayrshire in Scotland if Ulster is only at war with England (Scotland is neutral and gives military ahttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ccess to one of the war participants), and England controls the Irish Sehttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/a.
     * However, if Ulster has called in an ally, say Burgundy, and Burgundy is in a separate war with Scotland and controls Ayrshire, then the first requirement is no longer fulfilled, and the Irish nation can cross the strait despite England having control of the Irish Sea.

   Besieging a province of a strait does not fulfil the first requirement; the siege must finish, translating to control.

Naval missions[edit | edit source]

   Ambox outdated info.png
   Please help with verifying or updating this section. It was last verified for version 1.25.

   Fleet missions are grouped together under a collective “Select Mission” button ( Select mission.png ) that allows the player to tell their fleets to;
     * Protect Trade
     * Privateer
     * Hunt Pirates
     * Explore
     * Hunt Enemy Fleets
     * Blockade Enemy Ports
     * Intercept enemy fleets

Protect trade[edit | edit source]

   Protect trade.png

   This mission is available to any fleet that contains light ships. It will add the trade power of the light ships in the fleet to any maritime trade node that the player already has some trade power in, provided that the trade node is within both trade range and supply range.

   The trade power of light ships depends on ship model, and increases as diplomatic technology advances. Furthermore, it scales linearly with the naval maintenance slider, reaching full potential at maximum naval maintenance, but suffering a −75% penalty at minimum naval maintenance. AI nations do not suffer a trade power penalty to light ships from low naval maintenance.

Privateer [edit | edit sourcehttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/]

   https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ Wealth of Nations.png El Dorado.png Mare Nostrum.png Golden Century.png Lions of the North.png Available only with Wealth of Nations, El Dorado, Mare Nostrum, Golden Century or Lihttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ons of the North DLC enabled.
   Privateer.png

   This mission is available to any fleet that contains light ships. The fleet will hoist the Jolly Roger and add the trade power of its light ships to a pirate nation in any selected trade node. Unlike the protect trade mission, existinghttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ trade power is not needed in a trade node to start a privateer mission.

    Effects[edit | edit source]
       The privateer fleet increases the trade power of a pirate nation that acts as a collector in the trade node. This pirate nation will submit /eu4.paradoxwikis.com/b>50%
       of its earnings to the nations that commissioned the privateers contributing to its trade power. The presence of this pirate nation effectively reduces the share of trade value controlled by all non-pirate nations in the node. Income from privateering will be recorded in the economy window ahttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/s spoils of war.
       Any country that would have more thanhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ 20% of the trade power in the node without privateers will receive a casus belli against any nation that has sent privateers to that node.
       Any country that would have more than 10% of the trade power in the node without privahttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/teers will have a −1 opinion modifier per month of any nation that has sent privateershttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ to that node, capped at −100.
       https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/Sending light ships on privateer missions against rivals grants up to 10 power projection monthly per country.
       Activating a privateer mission will force the game to update a nation's power projection on the next game day. This will consequently update, among other things, the trade power in trade nodes and the nation's military force limits. Triggering an update like this can be useful when game stats are temporarily desynchronhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ized due to certain actions, such as sending light ships to protect trade or changing local autonomy levels.)
       Privateers also capture a portion of the ducats carried in treasure fleets passing through the node in which they operate.

Hunt pirates[edit | edit source]

       Mare Nostrum.png El Dorado.png Available only with the Mare Nostrum DLC or the El Dorado DLC enabled.
       Hunt pirates.png
       This mission is available to fleets which contain at leasthttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ one ship that isn't a transport. Fleets containing Heavy ship.png heavyhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ ships or Light ship.png light ships may hunt pirates in any trade node which is not Inland node.png inland; however, fleets containing only Galley.png galleys (as well as fleets which are a mixture of galleys and transports) can only hunt pirates in nodes where all nearby sea provinces are inland seas, e.g. in Basra and Alexandria, but not in Hormuz. This does not necessarily mean that fleets will only hunt in inland sea provinces (where they are more effective): for instance, a fleet hunting pirates in Canton will use the Luzon Strait.
       The total Icon ship cannons.png number of guns of the ships is used to find the efficiency at which they hunt the pirates. The Global trade power.png trade power of pirates is reduced by hunt pirate efficiency. This means that it reduces Privateer efficiency.png privateering efficiency from 0%, when no fleet is hunting pirates, up to 99%, if the total number of guns from the hunting fleet is greater than or equal twice the total number of guns from pirating fleet. It is important to note that the reduction of privateering efficiency will not stop privateering fleets from stealing trade income if that fleet has any bonuses to its privateering efficiency.
       In addition, it is helpful to know that this is also effective at stopping other nations from raiding your coasts.
       Note that pirate fleets and fleets hunting pirates do not actually battle or otherwise damage each other, unless the countries that own the fleets are at war with one another.

       El Dorado.png Available only with the El Dorado DLC enabled.

       Strategy The below is one of many player suggested strateghttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ies for Naval warfare. Bear in mind, due to the dynamhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ic nature of the game, it may unfold differently for other playershttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/.
    Deployment[edit | edit source]
       Decisive wins can https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/be achieved in battle by concentrating all battle ships (heavies and gallehttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ys) in one fleet up to just a little over the engagement width, with a re-enforcehttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ment fleet in the neighbouring tile. Seek battle if one has superior naval assets, and avoidhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ engagement otherwise.
       When ready to attack detach and send only the front line (your best ships and flagship https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/up to the value of your engagement width ahttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/nd a few more) into battle. Then as the phases progress feed reinforcements every few days from your neighbouring reinforcing fleet piece-meal into the battle to replace destroyed or disengaged ships. This will reduce morale losses from having as few ships as possible in the reserve line in the battle. One could call ithttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ the "just-in-time" re-enforcement method.
       Remember to https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/maximise your engagement width by using your highest manoeuvre admiral, prehttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ferably with high shock and fire pips too. You want more ships than the enemy to all be firing at the same time.
       Naval admirals can significantly tilt a battle in one's favor, even more so than generals; without an admiral, stack wiping and sometimes even victory becomes unlikely even with a seemingly overwhelming advantage.
       However, other factors may complicate this. A country may be forced to divide thehttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ir fleet if they have naval objectives other than destruction or suppression ofhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ the enemy navy, such as protecting (multiple) trade nodes, transporting land units byhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ sea, exploring, patrolling for pirates, reconnaissance, blockading and so https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/forth. If the country lacks naval supremacy compared to their enemies, https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/they may be forced to risk losses, support fewer of these objectives at the same time, or leave the sea entirely for the duration of the war.
       However, even if you are weaker than the enemy, tactics may make the difference in a long drawn out war. Smartly engage one enemy stack at a time (using the techniques above) whenever the oddhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/s are materially in your favour to win that specific battle. A sequence of such victories can qhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/uickly add up to war score and help ensure the enemy cannot lanhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/d their troops.
       Be sure to sail your full shttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/tacks into ports where you have coastal forts with terrain penalties for the besiegershttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/. The enemy will be lured into sieging these unfriendly forthttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/s if they don't see your stacks nearby, while having fleets allow you to sail into thttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/hese coastal forts before they can withdraw. Such attacks can lead to quick stack wipes of the enemy and can dramatically turn the war in your favour.
       Bringing an enemy fleet to battle[edit | edit source]
       A country with a naval advantage may wish to bring a reluctant enemy fleet thttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/o battle. This can be accomplished in several ways:
       https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/

     * If the enemy fleet is docked at a port, they cannot be attacked directly. Howevhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/er, the fleet may be ejected by occupying (suhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ccessfully sieging) that province, at which point the leaving fleet will enter into combat with any opposing fleet(s) in the corresponding sea province.
     * A small "bait" fleet may be used to lure the enemy into attacking, whereupon the main fleet can reinforce from a nearby sea province or port. This can also be used thttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/o lure fleets into or out of inland seas, where galleys have a relative advantage.
     * Light ships move fasthttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/er than heavy ships / transports, which move faster than galleyhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/s. A fleet without galleys can easily catch an enemy fleet that containhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/s galleys.
     * Putting your ships into port will https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/usually cause the AI navy to be more aggressive and leave port, sometimes even attempting a full blockade, leaving their navy significantly more vulnerable.
     * After a defeat, an enemy navy will typically retreat to an adjacent port. Having an army already sieging down this port will give you a significant advantage, as the shiphttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/s will be forced to leave port soon after arriving while having low morale andhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ no repairs, allowing for a stackwipe or a victory in which they may lose most of their ships. /eu4.paradoxwikis.com/li>Sometimes a bug will allow the AI to remain permanently in a province even if it is sieged down. The only way to fix this is to retreat several sea tiles from the province and then go into port, or in other words give the ai an illusion of safety.

Organization[https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/edit | edit source]

   The basic unit of naval forces is predictably the ship. Each ship is classed as heavy, light, galley or transport.
   <#Transports#Transports" title="Naval units">transport.

   Ships are grouped into fleets. Each fleet can be led by an admiral or explorer. A fleet travels at the speed of its slowest ship class.

Building ships[edit | edit source]

   Ambox outdated info.png
   Please help with verifying or updating this section. It was last https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/verified for version 1.30.

   Building ships requires an owned, cored and controlled Province icon.png province with a port, Gold Icon.png ducats to pay for the costs of the ship, Time Icon.png time to build the ship and Sailors.png sailors. Ehttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ach province can build one ship at a time, though multiple ships can be queued up in a single province.

   The base cost and building time of a ship depends on its type, and is then ahttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/djusted by any modifiers, in particular those coming from buildings the province might have. Ships start with 50% of maximum Naval morale.png morale when they have been built. Going over the Naval forcelimit.png naval forcelimit will result in higher maintenance cost.

   Unlike land units, ships do not automatically upgrade to new models as technology advances. Fleets are modernised by building new ships, or by manually upgrading existing ships.

  Ship cost[edit | edit source]

   The ducat cost for ships is computed as follows:

          [MATH: <semantics> <mrow class="MJX-TeXAtom-ORD"> <mstyle displaystyle="true" scriptlevel="0"> <mrow class="MJX-TeXAtom-ORD"> <mtext>ship cost</mtext> </mrow> <mo>=</mo> <mrow class="MJX-TeXAtom-ORD"> <mtext>base cost</mtext> </mrow> <mo>⋅</mo> <mrow class="MJX-TeXAthttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/om-ORD"> <mtext>max</mtext> </mrow> <mrow> <mo>(</mo> <mrow> <mn>100</mn> <mi mathvariant="normal">%https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/</mi> <mo>+</mo> <mo>ȡ#x2211;</mo> <mrow class="MJX-TeXAtom-ORD"> <mtext>ship cost modifiers</mtext> </mrow> <mo>,</mo> <mn>20</mn> <mi mathvariahttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/nt="normal">%#x0025;</mi> </mrow> <mo>)</mo> </mrow> </mstyle> </mrow> <annotation encoding="apphttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/lication/x-tex">{\displaystyle {\text{ship cost}}={\tehttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/xt{base cost}}\cdot {\text{max}}\left(100\%+\sum {\text{ship cost modifiers}},20\%\right)}</annotation> </semantics> :MATH]

    Ship cost modifiers[edit | edit source]

   Ship cost can be affected by general and ship type-specific modifiers which are added additively.

      General modifiers[edit | edit source]

   General modifiers reduce the ducat cost of all types of naval units. All modifiers that reduce the cost of new ships also reduce the maintenance of existing ships by a corresponding amount.

  Shipbuilding time[edit | edit source]

  Drafting Transport Ships[edit | edit source]

   Leviathan.png Available only with the Leviathan DLC enabled.

   The government reforms Eastern Plutocracy, Kongsi Federation, Livonian Admiralty and Livonian Plutocracy, allowhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ the cheap drafting of transport ships.
   This adds a new template to the macrobuilder, which will dynamically include enough transports so that after building it, 80% of the force limit whttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ill be made up of transports.
   Building these tranports will only take 50https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/% of the normal time and cost 20% less sailors.
   The monetary cost will be 1 years worth of income, multiplied by the percentage of forcelimit thats being build (80% = 0.8).
   At the least, they will be 20% cheaper than regular thttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ransports (this is relevant for nations with very high yearly income).
   The lowest price the template can reach is 1 ducat per ship (this is relevant for poor nations), unaffected by fhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/urther reductions to ship cost.
   Except for this, reductions to ship cost interact normally with drafting.

Upgrading ships[edit | edit source]

   /eu4.paradoxwikis.com/>When docked in an owned and controlled port, ships can be upgraded individually or at the fleet level. When an upgrade is triggered, the relevant ship(s) are replaced instantly, but reduced to an initial 1% condition to simulate the replacement ship being built virtually from scratch. For each ship, an upgrade costs the same amount of ducats as building a new ship.

   Advantages of upgrading include:
     * The 'construction' process (i.e. repairing the ship from its initial 1% condition) takes only 10 months, which is generally faster than simply building a new ship, especially for heavies.
     * Upgrades bypass the build queue and so are not limited in speed by the availability of coastal provinces for building.
     * The original name of each upgraded ship is maintained.
     * Upgrading is more convenient than manually destroying older ships and building new ones.
     * Upgrading, rather than disbanding and rebuilding, maintains the presence of a fleet where that is desirable, e.g. for deterring attack. (Alternatively one could temporarily go over force limit before disposing of the excess ships.)

   Disadvantages:
     * Repairing from 1% does not benefit from ship construction speed bonuses. (But it does benefit from ship repair bonuses, and repairing is generally faster anyway.)
     * Upgrading destroys the value embodied in the old ship, which could have been partially recouped by selling it to another country. Selling and rebuilding can therefore be more cost effective, where there are countries willing to buy.

  Naval maintenance modifier.png Maintenance[edit | edit source]

   Each ship costs ducats to upkeep every month. By class, the base ship maintenance depends on the type of ship and is proportional to the cost to build the ship along with a defined ship maintenance factor, based on ship type. This cost in turn is then multiplied by global cost modifiers to obtain the total cost per month for that specific ship.

   Naval maintenance can be computed as follows:

          [MATH: <semantics> <mrow class="MJX-TeXAtom-ORD"> <mstyle displaystyle="true" scriptlevel="0"> <msub> <mrow class="MJX-TeXAtom-ORD"> <mtext>naval maintenance</mtext> </mrow> <mrow class="MJX-TeXAtom-ORD"> <mtehttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/xt>ship</mtext> </mrow> </msub> <mo>=</mo> <mrow> <mo>(</mo> <msub> <mrow class="MJX-TeXAtom-ORD"> <mtext>base naval maintenance</mtext> </mrow> <mrow class="MJX-TeXAtom-ORD"> <mtext>ship type</mtext> </mrow> </msub> <mo>)</mo> </mrow> <mo>⋅</mo> <mrow> <mo>(</mo> <mrow> <mn>100</mn> <mi mathvariant="normal">%</mi> <mo>+</mo> <msub> <mrow class="MJX-TeXAtom-ORD"> <mtext>naval maintenance modifier</mtext> </mrow> <mrow class="MJX-TeXAtom-ORD"> <mtext>tech</mtext> </mrow> </msub> </mrow> <mo>)</mo> </mrow> <mo>⋅</mo> <mrow> <mo>(</mo> <mrow> <mn>100</mn> <mi mathvariant="normal">%</mi> <mo>+</mo> <mo>∑</mo> <msub> <mrow class="MJX-TeXAtom-ORD"> <mtext>naval maintenance modifiers</mtext> </mhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/row> <mrow
          class="MJX-TeXAtom-ORD"> <mtext>non-tech</mtext> </mrow> </msub> </mrow> <mo>)</mo> </mrow> <mo>⋅</mo> <mrow> <mo>(</mo> <mrow> <mn>100</mn> <mi mathvariant="normal">%</mi> <mo>+</mo> <mo>∑</mo> <mrow class="MJX-TeXAtom-ORD"> <mtext>build cost modifiers</mtext> </mrow> https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ </mrow> <mo>)</mo> </mrow> </mshttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/tyle> </mrow> <annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{\displaystyle {\text{naval maintenance}}_{\text{ship}}=\left({\text{base naval maintenance}}_{\text{ship type}}\right)\cdot \left(100\%+{\text{naval maintenance modifier}}_{\text{tech}}\right)\cdot \lefhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/t(100\%+\sum {\text{naval maintenance modifiers}}_{\text{non-tehttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ch}}\right)\cdot \left(100\%+\sum {\text{build cost modifiers}}\right)}</annotation> </semantics> :MATH]
          \text{naval maintenance}_\text{ship} = \left(\text{base naval maintenance}_\text{ship type} \right) \cdot \left( 100% + \text{naval maintenance modifier}_\text{tech} \right) \cdot \left( 100% + \sum\text{naval maintenahttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/nce modifiers}_\text{non-tech} \right) \cdot \left( 100% + \https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/sum\text{build cost modifiers} \right)

   Where:

          [MATH: <semantics> <mrow class="MJX-TeXAtom-ORD"> <mstyle displaystyle="true" scriptlevel="0"> <msub> <mrow class="MJX-TeXAtom-ORD"> <mtext>base naval maintenance</mtext> </mrow> <mrow class="MJX-TeXAtom-ORD"> <mtext>ship type</mtext> </mrow> </msub> <mo>=</mo> <mrow> <mo>(</mo> <mrow class="MJX-TeXAtom-ORD"> <mtext>ship cost</mtext> </mrow> <mo>)</mo> </mrow> <mo>⋅</mo> <mrow> <mo>[</mo> <mrow> <mrow class="MJX-TeXAtom-ORD"> <mtext>trunc</mtext> </mrow> <mrow> <mo>(</mo> <mrow> <mrow class="MJX-TeXAtom-ORD"> <mfrac> <mtext>maintenance factor</mtext> <mn>12</mn> </mfrac> </mrow> <mo>,</mo> <mn>3</mn> </mrow> <mo>)</mo> </mrow> </mrow> <mo>]</mo> </mrow> </mstyle> </mrow> <annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{\displaystyle {\text{base naval maintenance}}_{\text{ship type}}=\left({\text{ship cost}}\right)\cdot \left[{\text{trunc}}\left({\frac {\text{maintenance factor}}{12}},3\right)\right]}</annotation>https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ </semantics> :MATH]
          \text{base naval maintenance}_\text{ship type} = \left( \text{ship cost} \right) \cdot \left[ \text{trunc} \left( \frac{\text{maintenance factor}} {12} , 3 \right) \right]

   In this case, the game truncates all digits to the right of the third digit after the decimal point. For example:

          [MATH: <semantics> <mrow class="MJX-TeXAtom-ORD"> <mstyle displaystyle="true" scriptlevel="0"> <mi>trunc</mi> <mo>⁡</mo> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mn>0.0036</mn> <mo>,</mo> <mn>3</mn> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> <mo>=</mo> <mn>0.003</mn> </mstyle> </mrow> <annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{\displaystyle \operatorname {trunc} (0.0036,3)=0.003}</annotation> </semantics> :MATH]
          \operatorname{trunc}(0.0036,3) = 0.003

   The base build costs and ship maintenance factors are given here:

           Ship Class         Base Cost Maintenance Factor monthly maintenance without any modifiers
   Heavy ship.png Heavy ships 50        0.10               0.4
   Light ship.png Light ships 20        0.03               0.04
   Galley.png Galleys         10        0.04               0.03
   Transport.png Transport    12        0.04               0.036

     * Being over naval force limit will multiply the maintenance cost of ships by the force limit proportion. For example, if a country has 10 ships on a force limit of 5, maintenance is doubled.
     * Practichttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ally speaking, for a homogeneous fleet, the marginal maintenance of the first ship built or captured above the naval force limit is about 2* normal. For example, being at 100% of the forhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ce limit will result in the next ship adding about 200% of its normal maintenance, with this multiplier increasing by 2x per multiple of the force limit reached.
     * Light Ships suffer the penalty to their build cost as well, which squares the effect on maintenance cost. For example, being at 150% of the forchttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/e limit with all Light Ships will result in navy maintenance being 225% of normal. In this case, the marginal maintenance is about 3* the force limit proportion squared. For example, being at 150% of the force limit with all Light Ships will result in the next light ship adding about 675% of its normal maintenance.
     * Unlike land units, the tech modihttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/fier to Naval maintenance stacks multiplicatively with other modifiers. Thus, reductions to Naval Maintenance keep their strength better throughout the game than their land counterpart.
     * For a homogeneous fleet, the marginal maintenance of each ship is about twice the force limit proportion. For example, being at 150% of the force limit will result in the next ship adding about 300% of its normal maintenance.
