   Colonies will convert to their owner's religion and culture in certain circumstances, most requiring the involvhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ement of a colonist. See Colonization § Colonial provinces for details.

National conversion[edit | edit source]

   There are several different ways a country may change religion.

By direct action/eu4.paradoxwikis.com/n class="mw-editsection">[edit | edit source]

   Some religions may convert among certain heresies/sects via the Religion panel, at a cost of 100 prestige. This can only be done once evehttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ry 10 years. This is true for Catholic, Protestant and Reformed Christians, Hihttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ndus and Sikhs once Sikhism is unlocked, as well as all Buddhists. Conversion by this method will give +10% /eu4.paradoxwikis.com/mg alt="Missionary strength vs heretics.png" src="images/thumb/0/0f/Missionary_strength_vs_heretics.png/24px-Missihttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/onary_strength_vs_heretics.png" decoding="async" loading="lazy" width="24" height="24" data-file-width="48" data-file-height="48" /> missionary strength against heretics for ten years, making conversion of provinces of the old faith quite rapid. Sikhs can also convert to Sunni or Shia Islam this way. Defenders of the Faith cannot convert religions through this method.

   Conversion is also possible through decisions in some cases, which causes a -4 stability hit (except for Sikh or Sunni/Shia conversion, which only reduces it by 2). With the Star and Crescent DLC, Sunni and Shiite (but not Ibadi) Muslims may convert to the other denomination if both their capital and the majority of their province development follows the other denomination.

   Without Mandate of Heaven.png Mandate of Heaven, Japanese daimyos, but not the Shogun or Japan itself, may convert to Catholicism by decision if the majority of their territories are Catholic, which can happen following https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/certain events in the 16th century. With Mandate of Heaven, the Open outcome for the Ikko - Ikki, Neo-Confucianism, and Spread of Christianity Incidents will unlock a decision to convert to Mahayana, Confucianism, and Catholic respectively.

   Pagan nations that are not Tengri may convert to any non-Pagan faith if they control even just one province of that faith (they do not require a majority of that faith to convert and can immediately accept religious rebel demands to convert); Tengri nations are limited to Vajrayana Buddhism.

   Muslims owning a Sikh province may decide to convert to Sikhism - this decision probably mostly exists to allow Punjab to easily follow its historical religion.

   If using rebels to convert (see the section below) be aware that newly acquired provinces will suffer separatism that will spawn separatists instead of religious rebels if being converted by a missionary on low maintenance. To avoid this make sure the new province only has the player's core on it, or that rebel progress is below 30% (hence 20% or lower) in which case the rebels will change from separatists to religious rebels.

By event[edit | edit source]

   Tengri Tengri pagans with a dominant secondary faith may be prompted to change to it or face a -3 stability hit; they also have event chains that end in conversion to their secondary religion. See: Tengri_events#Religious_Unrest

   Flag of Ming Ming has a event chain to convert to Catholicism Catholicism. See: Ming_events#Chr#Christianity,_a_faith_for_the_Emperor?

   https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/"Flag Kongo has a event chain to convert to Catholicism Catholicism. With Origins.png these events are intertwined with their Mission.png mission tree. See: Kongo_events#Foreigners_arrive_in_Kongo!

   A nation in the British region, typically /eu4.paradoxwikis.com/span style="white-space:nowrap;"> Flag of England England
   , can get an event, based on the wives of Henry VIII, to convert to Anglican.png Anglicanism with the Rule Britannia.png Rule Britannia DLC. See: Anglican_events#The_Church_of_$COUNTRY$

   Scandinavian culture nations have unique events enabling them to become Norse.png Norse. See: Norse_events

   Flag of Dai Viet Dai Viet can convert to Confucianism Confucianism before 1500. See: Confucian_events#Confucian_Heritage

   Non-Confucian nations (except Flag of Ming Ming) can convert to Confucianism Confucianism when becoming the Emperor of china icon.png Emperor of China. See: Emperor of China events#An_Ideology_for_our_Empire

   Countries that have the Indian Sultanate government by default, but are neither Muslim nor were forcefully converted to another religion, will quickly be forced to choose by event between conversion to the appropriate branch of Islam, or facing a large amount of rebels and a stability hit. This generally only is the case if they have been released as a vassal or in a peace deal, which will likely make them Hindu initially, because Indian sultanates rarely convert the local religion, and indeed have no need to due to their large bonus to heathen tolerance. AI will always choose to convert. See: Religious_events#Muslim_coup

     * [More advanced methods] This same method can be used "in reverhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/se" by the player to be converted by another AI heretic nhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ation (hence in the same denominational group). To do this the plhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ayer should get to a 100% war score against the enehttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/my AI by sieging all their provinces. Thenhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/, instead of demanding something from the AI enemy, the player in facts offers to the enemy (as though it has lost the war) that the player itself be converted. Hence, for example, the player being an Animist Ryuku could "offer" to the AI Nahuatl enemy to be force converted into Nahuatl, which is in the same Pagan denominationhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/al group. Be sure that the player's overall country size must be less than 100% war score to be conhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/verted this way by the AI. To do this the player needs to have an Orthodox human ally force convert say a neighbouring AI One Province Minor (OPM) within Catholic Europe with whom the player is at war. To do so both the player and the ally need to fight together in the war with the OPM. Forced conversion by rebels[edit | edit source]

   Nations can support religious zealots in other countries. These rebels convert a province's religion to the one they represent when occupation is ahttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/chieved.

   Supporting religious zealots is only possible if the desired religion is presenhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/t in the target nation and is the likely rebel type in a provinhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ce with unrest above 0. If there are no such provinhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ces in the target nation, one way to achieve it is to sell the target a province of thhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/e correct religion.

   Generally the nation will be ablehttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ to overpower the rebels if left to its own devices, so it is critical to support thhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/em militarily. This can be done by declaring war against the target nation using the "Support Rebels" casus belli.

   A nation that is broken by religious rebels, or that accepts their demands, will convert to the rebels' religionhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ provided that the rebels' religion is the plhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/urality^[13 #91;13] religion in terms of development (the autonomy of the provinces or the number of provinces do not matter). For most countries, giving in to religious rebels is the only way to change between religious groups.

   Starting with version 1.34, rebels of any pagan faith except Nahuatl, Mayan and Inti can convert a tag of any faith to their own throughttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/h enforcing their demands (their demands cannot be accepthttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ed as a non-pagan nation); formerly this was only possible for [28px-Animist.png] Animist rebels.

   To trigger a religious rebel revolt and be forcefully converted by rebels the following steps are suggested:
     * The player https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/must ensure they own at least one province of the targeted religion and that the province has unrest (provinces ihttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/n which there has recently been a revolt will have a -100% modihttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/fier, and will not be suitable).
     * The player should reduce theihttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/r missionary maintenance to zero and then send a missihttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/onary to the targeted province to try and convert it. At zero maintenance the province will never be converted and simply cause additional unrest.
     * This should trigger religious rebels with a ticking progress meter.
          + If using rebels to convert be aware that newly acquired provinces will suffer separatism that will spawnhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ separatists instead of religious rebels if being converted by a missionary onhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ low maintenance. To avoid this make sure the new province only has the player's core on it, or that https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/rebel progress is below 30% (hence 20% or lower) in which case the rebels should change from separatists to religious rebels.
     * In the rebel interaction menu the player can then "provoke rebels" once the progress meter has reached 50%; this will spawn rebels at +50%https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ strength.
     * Once the rebels have spawned they will start converthttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ing provinces unprotected by forts (hence be sure to mothhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ball forts before they spawn).
     * Once the plurality of religion is of the new type the player can then accept their demands and be converted.
     * Be aware that rebels can break a country prematurely if they control more than 50% of the country or have controlled the capital for a while (typically 24 months). However, rebels cannot enforce their demand during war (unless they somehow manage to chttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/onvert 100% of all provinces, or they have controlled the capital for 24 mohttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/nths). So it may be advisable to be at war while these rebels are converting as much of the country as possible. These rebels are fragile though and need to be "protected" while converting.
          + The player should therefore set vassals to "snooze" in their own territories and not allow allies or other armies engaged in war to have access in thehttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ player's country so as to accidentally engage the rebels. /eu4.paradoxwikis.com/i>Also, uneven and untidy borders and strahttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/its blocked by ships may cause rebels to walk through neighbouring countries and be killed there.
     * If they are killed, re-siege one of the newly converted provinces (ones without the -100% recent uprising modifier) to again try and convert it and respawning the rebels.
     * Know that if one is not at war while the rebels are busy moving about one's country it will become a fine balance behttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/tween (i) unsieging rebel-controlled provinces to avoid their phttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/remature enforcement of demands (before the 50% requirement is met) or thttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/riggering "rebels break the country" and (ii) not impeding their progress.
     * Be considerate that they are very likely to re-siege the same provinces or to attack one in order to keep provinces under their control.
     * To check the threshold for when the religious rebels change the state religion when they win, use the "Charts"https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ panel (panel 35) under the Economy Sectiohttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/n in the ledger. In the brackets you see the development of each religion in your country. If the rebelling religion has the plurality of the development, you get the religion when you accept rebel demands or they enforce it onto you.

   With some luck and God's will these rebels may be successful in their quest to convert the majority of the countrhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/y and the player can soon enjoy following the path of this new accepted https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/faith.

Strategy[edit | edit source]

   Strategy The below is one of many player suggested strategies for Religiohttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/n. Bear in mind, due to the dynamic nature of the game, ithttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ may unfold differently for other players.
     * Base missionary strength is very small compared to modifiers, both positive and negative. This means that conversion can be very fast or impossible. Religious ideas are sometimes essentialhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ to make any progressive conversion work./eu4.paradoxwikis.com/li>
     * Setting provinces as states ihttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/s vitally important:
          + Provinces in territories and with an unaccepthttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ed population culture have a missionary strength modifier ofhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ -4% before other modifiershttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/. In contrast, provinces in states can promote culturehttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/s to become acceptable and can further enact "Enforce Religious Unity" for a modifier of /eu4.paradoxwikis.com/an class="effect-green">+1%, a net overall difference of +5% in such accepted culture enforce religious unity provinces.
     * Provinces that do not have the state religion generally suffer from low tolerance and also lower the nation's Religious Unity. With that, nations that are challenged with large numbers of wrong-religion provinces will have to choose between converting them or thttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/olerating them, and with the 1.26 update the main way of tolerating them ahttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/s a large nation is to use the Humanist idea group.
     * Note that only provhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/inces with the the state religion and no separatism can be culthttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ure converted.
     * Several Triggers for Religions give bonuses ohttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/r penalties. You should keep in mind thesehttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ Triggers to optimize your religious conversion. See Triggered modifiers.
     * In high development provinces building a cathedral will add +3% local missionary strength, helping with thhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/e conversion as well as additional tax revenue.
     * For Cahttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/tholic nations intending to convert to Protestant or Reformed, consider drihttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ving relations with the Pope down to enact Declare Statute in Restraint of Appeals and then build them back up to Revoke Restraint of Appeals for a +1% missionary strength that remains to the end of the game.

Stability

   From Europa Universalis 4 Wiki
   Jump to navigation Jump to search

   Please help with verifying or updating older sections of this article.https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/
   At least some were last verified for version 1.25.

   Icon stability.png Stability is a measure of the nation's internal peace. Unstable nations are more likely to face revolts and turmoil, while stable nations enjoy increased prosperity.

   Like many other game mechanics, a player spends monarch power to increase stability, in this case administrative power ( Administrative power.png ). Since these are also thttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/he points that go towards increasing the number of ideas and development, it is less likely that https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/a country will always be at peak stability since a player may plan on investing monarch power in other things.
   [ ]

Effects[edit | edit source]

   Ambox outdated info.png
   Please help with verifying or updating this section. It was last verified for version 1.25.

   Maintaining at least neutral (0) or positive stability reduces the chance of rebellion and increases national income, amongst other minor benefits.

   Increasing stability also grants Abhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/solutism.png +1 Absolutism.

Stability cost[edit | edit source]

   Ambox outdated info.png https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/
   Please help with verifying or updating this section. It was last verified for version 1.25.

   The base price for increasing stability is Administrative power.png 100 administrative power, but overextension and lack of religious unity can increase this cost significantly. Some ideas and advisors decrease this. Thhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ere are also events and other random factors also modifying the price temporarily. Stability https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/cannot go higher than 3; any events that increase stability at this maximum will not increase stability further.

   Main modifiers that affect the cost of raising stability are:
     * +50% increase per point of positive Icon stability.png stability.
     * +50% if another country has sown discontent in the country.
     * https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/+ Overextension.png (Overextension / 2)%. Half of overextension is added to the cost.
     * +(100 https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/�� religious unity)%. The lack of religious unity is added to the cost.
     * +2*(100 − Republican tradition.png republican tradition)%
     * A country will usually have increased Icon stability.png stability cost if suffering a disaster.
     * +25% regency.

   The minimum cost to raise stability is Ahttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/dministrative power.png 10 administrative power.

Subject nation

   From Europa Universalis 4 Wiki
   (Redirected from Subject nations)
   Jump to navigation Jump to search

   Please help with verifying or updating older sections of this article.
   At least some were last verified for version 1.25.
   The subjects interface panel image as of patch 1.18

   Subject nations are semi-autonomous subordinate nations that surrender their economic, diplomatic and/or military power to their overlord in exchange for protection. It is possible to see a subject's nation information by selecting the country icon on the subjects tab. The types of subject nations range from the primarily economic Tradecompany icon.png Trade company to the military-focused March icon.png March. All subjects (except trade companies) have a Liberty desire.png liberty desire that determines their loyalty towards their liege.
   Unless stated otherwise, all subject nations also receive the following "Subject nation" malus:
   Tax income.png       −6 Tax income
   Land forcelimit.png  −3 Land force limit
   Naval forcelimit.png −6 Naval force limit
   [ ]

Subject types[edit | edit source]

Icon vassal.png Vassal[edit | edit source]

          Main article: Vassal

   Vassals are the most basic form of subject nations. While vassals may have control over their own territory and military, they also automatically join any conflict their overlord enters into.
              Subject                                     Vassal
   Subject Nation penalty        Yes
   Diplomatic relation slot      Yes
   Subject tax
     * Gold Icon.png 1 × Vassal income.png income from subject × their Tax income.png tax income
     * If the overlord is a merchant republic:
          + Vassals transfer Global trade power.png 50% of their trade power to the overlord

   Overlord force limit increase Land forcelimit.png 10% of the subject's land force limit
   Liberty desire calculation
     * Calculates based on all (incorporated) vassals, eyalets, marches, pronoias and soyurghals for army, navy and economic size comparison
     * Liberty desire from subjects development Per development:^[1] 0.25
     * If they are a client state:
          + −25%

   Integratable after            10 years
   Integration cost              100%
   Effects on subject
     * Development cost.png +50% development cost
     * If the overlord has enacted the T4 government reform Gov fiqh laws.png Fiqh Laws (available for Flag of Ottomans Ottomans and Flag of Rûm Rûm) and is of same religion:
          + Manpower in true faith provinces +25% Manpower in true faith provinces
          + National sailors modifier.png +25% National sailors modifier
          + Production efficiency.png +15% Production efficiency
     * If the overlord has granted the "Customs Union" Burghers.png Burghers privilege (available for Flag of Germany Germany)
          + Global prov trade power modifier.png +33% Provincial trade power modifier

   Effects on overlord
     * Land forcelimit.png +1 Land force limit

   If the Government republic.png T13 government reform Gov neutral ground.png Neutral Ground Policy (available for Gov pirate republic.png Pirate republics) is enacted, and if the vassal is a Gov pirate republic.png Pirate republic:
     * Manpower Icon.png +4000 Manpower increase
     * Sailors.png +2000 Sailors increase
     * Yearly navy tradition.png +0.25 Yearly navy tradition
     * Naval forcelimit.png +2 Naval force limit

   Independent diplomacy?        No
   Gained via
     * The "X Vassal" peace treaty
     * The "Offer Vassalization" diplomatic action
     * Releasing owned land as a vassal through the diplomacy tab

   Notes

   Vassals cannot declare war (except with the Independence CB against their overlord), but can fabricate claims that either they or their overlord deems as 'vital interest'. Vassals which do not have a truce with their overlord can request a support of independence from other nations. AI vassals don't do that if they have a Loyal attitude loyal attitude towards their overlord (Below Liberty desire.png 50% liberty desire the attitude changes to loyal on the next month tick if the attitude is not Outraged attitude outraged). A vassal can break free through an independence war (AI vassals don't do that if they have a truce or are loyal). Vassals which are not Loyal attitude loyal are also more active diplomatically as to forming their own alliances with other rebellious subjects of their overlord, seeking foreign support for their independence, and setting more provinces as those of interest.

March icon.png March[edit | edit source]

          Main article: March

   A march is a militaristic vassal that cannot be annexed and does not pay taxes to the overlord, but gets significant bonuses to its armed forces.
              Subject                                          March
   Subject Nation penalty        Yes
   Diplomatic relation slot      Yes
   Subject tax
     * If the overlord is a merchant republic:
          + Marches transfer Global trade power.png 50% of their trade power to the overlord

   Overlord force limit increase Land forcelimit.png 20% of the subject's land force limit
   Liberty desire calculation
     * Base: −15%
     * Calculates based on all (incorporated) vassals, eyalets, marches, pronoias and soyurghals for army, navy and economic size comparison
     * Liberty desire from subjects development Per development:^[1] 0.25
     * If they are a client state:
          + −25%

   Integratable after            No
   Integration cost              No
   Effects on subject

   If total development is at most 25% of the development of their overlord:
     * Land forcelimit modifier.png +30% Land force limit
     * Naval forcelimit modifier.png +30% Naval force limit
     * Global manpower modifier.png +25% National manpower modifier
     * Manpower recovery speed.png +20% Manpower recovery speed
     * Defensiveness.png +20% Fort defense
     * Fort maintenance modifier.png −20% Fort maintenance
     * Land maintenance modifier.png −20% Land maintenance modifier
     * Naval maintenance modifier.png −20% Naval maintenance modifier

If the overlord has enacted the T4 government reform  Gov fiqh laws.png  Fiqh Laws (available for  Flag of Ottomans  Ottomans and  Flag of Rûm  Rûm) and is of same religion:

     * Manpower in true faith provinces +25% Manpower in true faith provinces
     * National sailors modifier.png +25% National sailors modifier
     * Production efficiency.png +15% Production efficiency

   Effects on overlord           Land forcelimit.png +1 Land force limit
   Independent diplomacy?        No
   Gained via                    The "Designate March" diplomatic action, used on a regular vassal

   March status can be revoked and the subject turned into a simple vassal, but at the cost of stability and relations loss.

Client state.png Client state[edit | edit source]

          Main article: Client state

   Client states are highly loyal, custom vassals. They are unlocked by either getting Diplomatic tech.png diplomatic technology level 23, using the Mercenary–Influence policy "Client State Act", or having the level 2 monarchy reform "Reform the Pronoiar System" (limited to Flag of Byzantium Byzantium, the Flag of Roman Empire Roman Empire, and custom nations). They can be formed from any province or provinces that the player has control over and is on the same continent as their capital or borders an existing client state or has a land connection to the capital.

   Mechanically, they function like a ordinary vassal but with a permanent Liberty desire in subjects −25% liberty desire bonus.

   Client states cannot be turned into daimyos, eyalets, or incorporated vassals, but they can be designated as March icon.png marches.

   Generally, any province within two tiles by land can be added to a client state, including over straits. The first province that a new client state is given is automatically designated as the capital, and the Culture icon.png culture in that province will become the primary culture of the new client state. The client state will have its creator's state religion. The client state gets a automatic core on its capital but will have to create cores on other provinces manually.

   It is possible to customize the flag, the name, and the map colour of a client state based on a set of flag templates and images when it's created and at any time after then.

Daimyo[edit | edit source]

          Main article: Japan#Daimyo & Shogunate

   Mandate of Heaven.png Available only with the Mandate of Heaven DLC enabled.

   A Daimyo is a unique form of vassalage to the shogun of Japan. A daimyo may ally with and fight other daimyo (typically with the Casus belli.png "Sengoku" CB), but not foreign countries. They also have a special Casus belli.png "War for the Emperor" CB targeting their overlord to take their place as shogun.
   Subject Daimyo
   Subject Nation penalty Yes
   Diplomatic relation slot No
   Subject tax Gold Icon.png 1 × Vassal income.png income from subject × their Tax income.png tax income
   Overlord force limit increase Land forcelimit.png 10% of the subject's land force limit
   Liberty desire calculation
     * Base: +10%
     * Calculates only own value; for army, navy and economic size comparison
     * Liberty desire from subjects development Per development:^[1] 0.25

   Integratable after 10 years
   Integration cost 100%
   Effects on subject
   Effects on overlord For each daimyo at peace:
   Stability cost modifier.png −2%  Stability cost modifier (maximum of −20%)
   Yearly legitimacy.png       +0.1 Yearly legitimacy (maximum of +1)

   For each daimyo with the same level of isolationism as the Shogun:
   Yearly prestige.png +0.1 Yearly prestige

   For each daimyo with a different level of isolationism as the Shogun:
   Yearly prestige.png −0.05 Yearly prestige

   The above isolationism modifiers combined cannot exceed either −1 or +1 yearly prestige.
   Independent diplomacy?
     * Can declare war on other daimyo
     * Can ally other daimyo
     * Can rival other daimyo

   Gained via
     * Every vassal of a nation with the Shogunate tier 1 reform will turn into a daimyo, except client states.

   Notes Should a daimyo conquer the province of Kyoto (1020), it will become the Shogun and the defender and all other daimyo will become its daimyo subjects.

   Outside nations can enforce peace on two warring daimyo without calling the shogun or its vassals to war, effectively providing a way for outside powers to get easy land in Japan.

Incorporated vassal[edit | edit source]

   Winds of Change.png Available only with the Winds of Change DLC enabled.

   An Incorporated vassal has all the same mechanics of a traditional vassal, but its overlord traded a cost in Governing capacity.png governing capacity for a reduced Diplomatic annexation cost –25% diplomatic annexation cost.
              Subject                                                                                           Incorporated vassal
   Subject Nation penalty        Yes
   Diplomatic relation slot      Yes
   Subject tax                   Gold Icon.png 1 × Vassal income.png income from subject × their Tax income.png tax income
   Overlord force limit increase Land forcelimit.png 10% of the subject's land force limit
   Liberty desire calculation
     * Calculates based on all (incorporated) vassals, eyalets, marches, pronoias and soyurghals for army, navy and economic size comparison
     * Liberty desire from subjects development Per development:^[1] 0.25

   Integratable after            10 years
   Integration cost              75%
   Effects on subject            Development cost.png +50% development cost
   Effects on overlord
     * Land forcelimit.png +1 Land force limit
     * Governing capacity.png −100 Governing capacity

   Independent diplomacy?        No
   Gained via                    The "Incorporate Vassal" diplomatic action, used on a regular vassal.
   Notes                         In general only available to Flag of Germany Germany via the Gov crown.png Imperial Descent government reform, but there are several missions that can award Incorporated vassals.

   The following is a list of all missions that reward this subject type:
     * The Government steppe horde.png Tatar and Mongol Mission.png mission "March into Central Asia" if Flag of Kazakh Kazakh was previously released (does not reduce governing capacity)
     * The Flag of Austria Austrian Mission.png mission "A.E.I.O.U." unlocks the ability to create these subjects. (max 5?)
     * The Flag of Bohemia Bohemian Mission.png mission "Consolidate Silesia" if completed diplomatically – for Flag of Silesia Silesia (does not reduce governing capacity)
     * The Flag of Timurids Timurid Mission.png mission "Ambition in Yuan" (on the "Nomad" branch) if the "We shall follow in his footsteps." option is chosen in the "Yuan Campaign" event – for Flag of Yuan Yuan (does not reduce governing capacity)

Personal union.png Personal union[edit | edit source]

          Main article: Personal union

   Junior partners in a personal union share the same ruler and heir as that of the leading country. Unlike vassals, unions do not have to provide their overlord with a percentage of their monthly income, and only get a small Opinion.png +10 relations boost with their overlord.
              Subject            Personal union
   Subject Nation penalty        Yes
   Diplomatic relation slot      Yes
   Subject tax                   No
   Overlord force limit increase No
   Liberty desire calculation
     * Adds overlord prestige below Prestige.png 0 × 1
     * Calculates only own value; for army, navy and economic size comparison
     * Ignores development

   Integratable after            50 years
   Integration cost
     * 100%
     * Alternatively, unions can be inherited:
          + Inheritance automatically annexes the junior partner with no autonomy, but occurs only upon ruler death.
          + The probability of inheritance increases with the senior partner's Diplomatic reputation.png diplomatic reputation and stability and decreases with the junior partner's number of provinces.

   Effects on subject

   If the senior partner has enacted the Government monarchy.png T1 government reform Gov danish archkingdom.png Unified Kalmar Monarchy (available for Flag of Denmark Denmark):
     * The junior partner receives the bonuses of being a March icon.png march

   Effects on overlord

   If the senior partner has enacted the Government monarchy.png T1 government reform Gov danish archkingdom.png Unified Kalmar Monarchy (available for Flag of Denmark Denmark):
     * Manpower Icon.png Manpower increase
     * Sailors.png Sailors increase
     * Global manpower modifier.png National manpower modifier
     * National sailors modifier.png National sailors modifier

   If the junior partner is Flag of England England or Flag of Great Britain Great Britain and the senior partner has completed the Flag of Netherlands Dutch Mission.png mission "Glorious Revolution" diplomatically and chosen the first option in the following event:
     * Has man of war.png Can build Man-of-war ships
     * Allowed man of war fraction.png +10% Man-of-war force limit fraction

   Independent diplomacy?        No
   Gained via
     * Personal unions can occur when a ruler dies without a legal heir. In this case, if a royal marriage partner shares the same dynasty as the deceased ruler, it becomes the senior partner in a union.
     * Additionally, a Casus belli.png "Claim on throne" casus belli can be used on nations with a disputed succession (weak or no heir) of the same dynasty that the player has a royal marriage with.

   Notes
     * Only nations that have one of the Christian denominations as their state religion are able to be the junior partner in personal unions or, under normal circumstances, become the senior partner.
     * When a union forms peacefully, a succession war may erupt between rivals or other valid partners.
     * Junior partners retain all non-PU subjects they had (PU subjects will be transferred to the senior partner). They can also have their own colonial nations.
     * Should the ruler die while the junior has negative opinion, the union will be broken.

   Some nations can get a Casus belli.png "Restoration of Union" CB against countries that they never had a union with in the first place, such as Flag of Austria Austria, which can receive this casus belli against Flag of Bohemia Bohemia and Flag of Hungary Hungary as a mission.

Integrated personal union[edit | edit source]

   Winds of Change.png Available only with the Winds of Change DLC enabled.

   An Integrated personal union has the same mechanics as a traditional Personal union.png personal union, except that it has a reduced Diplomatic annexation cost –25% diplomatic annexation cost.
              Subject            Integrated personal union
   Subject Nation penalty        Yes
   Diplomatic relation slot      No
   Subject tax                   No
   Overlord force limit increase No
   Liberty desire calculation
     * Adds overlord prestige below Prestige.png 0 × 1
     * Calculates only own value; for army, navy and economic size comparison
     * Ignores development

   Integratable after            50 years
   Integration cost              75%
   Effects on subject            None
   Effects on overlord           None
   Independent diplomacy?        No
   Gained via                    Several missions
   Notes
     * In general only available to Flag of Austria Austria via its Mission.png mission "A.E.I.O.U", but there are several missions that can award integrated personal unions.
     * There is a maximum amount of integrated personal unions a nation can have.

   The following is a list of all missions that reward this subject type:
     * The Flag of Austria Austrian Mission.png mission "Royal Hungary" – for Flag of Hungary Hungary
     * The Flag of Austria Austrian Mission.png mission "Crown of Spain" – for Flag of Castile Castile or Flag of Spain Spain

Theodoro personal union[edit | edit source]

   Internally the game has another Personal union.png personal union type, called "Theodoro personal union". In game this is simply called "Personal Union" and functions much like one. However, like an integrated personal union, this type of union has a reduced Diplomatic annexation cost –25% diplomatic annexation cost. The following is a list of all the ways to gain this subject type:
     * Choosing the "The Rus will be part of [Root.GetName]" option of the "Atop the Kremlin" event, triggered by completing the Flag of Theodoro Theodorian Mission.png mission "Palace of the Tsars" on the "Russian Claims" branch, for whatever Russian junior partner that was gained earlier (usually Flag of Muscovy Muscovy).
     * Choosing the "They belong under the Dutch realm." option of the "The Throne of England" event, triggered by completing the Flag of Netherlands Dutch Mission.png mission "Glorious Revolution", for junior partner Flag of England England or Flag of Great Britain Great Britain.

Subject colony icon.png Colonial nation[edit | edit source]

          Main article: Colonial nation

   Colonial nations represent the distant New World colonial territories of Old World countries. They will automatically form once five cored colonial provinces exist inside a single colonial region. Once formed, colonial nations will take control of any province that would otherwise be owned by their overlord in a given colonial region, even if the province is uncored or would otherwise cause extreme Overextension.png overextension.
              Subject                                                                              Colonial nation
   Subject Nation penalty        Yes
   Diplomatic relation slot      No
   Subject tax
     * Colonial nations transfer Global trade power.png 50% of their trade power to the overlord
     * Global tariffs.png Global tariffs × Production.png 50% production income

Tradecompany icon.png Trade company[edit | edit source]

   Wealth of Nations.png Available only with the Wealth of Nations DLC enabled.

          Main article: Trade company

   A trade company is a collection of overseas provinces in a trade company region that exchanges tax and manpower for trade, maritime and production benefits. They are not actually nations, but they are listed in the subjects tab.

   A province in a trade company gets autonomy-reduced Tax income.png tax income, Sailors.png sailors, Manpower Icon.png manpower and Land forcelimit.png land force limit like a territory, but less autonomy impact on Production.png production income, Global trade power.png +100% provincial trade power, and Naval forcelimit.png 0.5 naval force limit. Additionally, Goods produced.png goods produced remains unaffected by cultural intolerance, religious intolerance is ignored (but they get Local missionary strength.png −20% local missionary strength), and the province does not contribute to Religious unity.png religious unity.

   Trade companies may be formed by nations that own at least one province in a territory which is on a different subcontinent from their capital and not in a colonial region. They differ from colonial nations in the Americas and Australia in that they are not separate governments, as all territories remain part of the mother country. Provinces in a trade company must belong to a territory; adding them to a state will automatically remove them from a trade company, which entails the same Goods produced.png −200% goods produced modifier which manually removing one does. Provinces can be added or removed from a trade company at any time, except when the 5-year Goods produced.png goods produced modifier for removal is present.

Strategy[edit | edit source]

   For a tributary overlord, sending manpower to tributary subjects at war can often be the cheapest way to decrease liberty desire and maintain the more valuable tribute income in the form of monarch power. It can thus be helpful to set large tributary countries as "special interest" (right-click on country flag in provincial interface) and receive notification for wars by these tributaries.

   For establishing tributary subjects of AI nation, Threatened attitude threatened attitude gives the most significant +100. (Strangely, Friendly attitude friendly attitude does not give any modifier.) The attitude goes away at high opinion. Thus the optimal opinion with the threatened attitude is around 0. Players should avoid improving relation for too long in that case.

   Liberty desire modifiers from Demand Additional Tribute and Demand Artifacts decay independently, so alternating between them allows liberty desire to drop down more quickly.

Icon core eyalet.png Core eyalets[edit | edit source]

   To annex an eyalet it must first be diplomatically "reined in", which turns them into a core eyalet. A core eyalet can be diplomatically annexed, but can't at all be called into wars. The 10 year cooldown before the subject can be annexed only starts after turning them into a core eyalet.
              Subject                                                    Core eyalet
   Subject Nation penalty        No
   Diplomatic relation slot      No
   Subject tax                   Gold Icon.png 1.5 × Vassal income.png income from subject x their Tax income.png tax income
   Overlord force limit increase
     * Land forcelimit.png 20% of the subject's land force limit
     * Naval forcelimit.png 20% of the subject's naval force limit
     * Global manpower modifier.png 20% of the subject's maximum manpower
     * Sailors.png 20% of the subject's maximum sailors

   Liberty desire calculation
     * Calculates based only on own value for army, navy and economic size comparison
     * Liberty desire from subjects development Per development:^[1] 0.1

   Integratable after            10 years
   Integration cost              75%
   Effects on subject
     * Global manpower modifier.png −5000 National manpower
     * Land forcelimit.png −5 Land force limit

   If the overlord has enacted the T4 government reform Gov fiqh laws.png Fiqh Laws (available for Flag of Ottomans Ottomans and Flag of Rûm Rûm) and is of same religion:
     * Manpower in true faith provinces +25% Manpower in true faith provinces
     * National sailors modifier.png +25% National sailors modifier
     * Production efficiency.png +15% Production efficiency

   Effects on overlord           None
   Independent diplomacy?        Does not join any offensive wars
   Gained via
     * Using the "Rein in Eyalet" diplomatic action on a regular eyalet

   Notes

   Eyalets whose development is close to or surpasses 200 will be exceedingly difficult to rein in. Being at 200 opinion and 100 trust will only give them 60 reasons to be reined in, while every 4 points of development will give them 1 reason to refuse being reined in. Thus an eyalet with 200 development or above will never accept being reined in if their overlord does not stack diplomatic reputation (which gives 4 reasons to be reined in per point). Furthermore, every point of liberty desire will reduce reining in acceptance by the same value. High development eyalets will thus be even harder to rein in. If one wishes to integrate their eyalets, it is advised to not turn their core eyalets which are granted via missions or events back into eyalets.

     * They can only be established via the "Establish Trade Protectorate" diplomatic action on countries with their capital on a different continent.
     * They are only available to nations that have the Thalassocracy, Merchant Committees, Royal Charters, or British Global Trade Policy government reform.
     * The former is available to all nations that complete the "Confirm Thalassocracy" decision, the second one is only availabel to Flag of Venice Venice via their missions, and the latter two are only available to Flag of England England via their missions.

     * Trade protectorates can declare wars on other tributaries/trade protectorates of the same overlord without involving them.
     * The overlord can protect them if they are attacked, but may refuse, which does not break the relationship.
     * Both overlord and protectorate may diplomatically end the relationship at any time, at the cost of Icon stability.png −1 stability ( Prestige.png −1 prestige with full Diplomatic ideas). This does not create a truce. There is no pop-up if the relationship is broken this way.
     * The trade protectorate may also fight an independence war, but the AI will never do this.
     * They are not automatically called into the wars of their overlord. They can however be called to arms like any ally when declaring a war, including with the promise of land.
     * An AI-controlled trade protectorate always answers such calls if their opinion is at least +100, regardless of favours or claims on provinces, and will never accept otherwise.
     * Calling a trade protectorate to arms will reduce their opinion by −100 which decays at a rate of +5 yearly.
     * They can also be called to wars after the war has been declared or if a war was declared onto their overlord, but only with the "Call trade protectorate to war" action under the Influence Actions group.
     * This action is only possible if the protectorate is not at war and has a positive opinion of their overlord, but will be denied by the AI if the opinion isn't at least +50.
     * They receive an opinion malus of −100 and then join all active wars. The opinion malus is reduced to −50 if they are only called into defensive wars.

Pronoia.png Non-hereditary pronoia[edit | edit source]

     * A hereditary pronoia can be turned into a non-hereditary pronoia via the "Revoke rights of inheritance" diplomatic action, which requires less than Liberty desire.png 15% liberty desire.
     * If the overlord has completed the "Control over the Pronoiars" mission and chose the "End their hereditary freedoms." option, pronoias will be non-hereditary from the beginning.
     * If the overlord has completed the "Control over the Pronoiars" mission and chose the "Focus on the inheritance laws." option, integrating a pronoia will increase the overlord's crownland by Crownland.png +1%, unless the overlord already gained crownland in this way within the last 5 years.
     * Note that the liberty desire requirement for inheritance is counted after the ruler dies, so if for example the death of the pronoia's ruler breaks a royal marriage, and that puts their liberty desire above 50%, they won't be annexed.

Liberty desire.png Liberty desire[edit | edit source]

   Ambox outdated info.png
   Please help with verifying or updating this section. It was last verified for version 1.25.

   All subject nations have a liberty desire between 0 and 100, indicating their wish for independence.
     * Below 50 a subject state is loyal: it pays taxes/tariffs to its overlord and takes an active part in all wars.
     * Above 50 liberty desire, a subject becomes disloyal, refusing to pay taxes while being unhelpful in wars by only defending its own territory. Disloyal subjects readily accept support for their independence from foreign nations and make alliances with each other, and may declare an independence war if they have sufficient strength. In rare cases, a disloyal subject may still have a Friendly attitude toward its overlord; this means it will not accept requests to support its independence or alliances from fellow subjects, but does not otherwise alter its behavior.
     * At 100 liberty desire, a state is rebellious, and will, at least in theory, declare its independence at the slightest opportunity.

Relative modifiers[edit | edit source]

   Liberty desire from army is calculated as follows:
     * The relative army size of the subject compared to its overlord. There is +75 liberty desire for having 100% of the overlord's forces, scaling proportionately (e.g. +37.5 at 50%).
          + The combined strength of all (incorporated) vassals, eyalets, marches, pronoias and soyurghals is used for their liberty desire.
          + Daimyos, all three personal union types, all five colonial nations, commercial enterprises, both tributaries, trade protectorates, cultural influenced states, appanages, core eyalets and Mongol brother realms only consider their individual strengths.
          + Additionally, nations allied with or supporting the liberty of a subject nation will have their army strength added to that specific subject. Other subjects will not have their army strength increased, unless their independence is also supported.

   Liberty desire from economy is calculated as follows:
     * The relative economic size of the subject compared to its overlord. There is +75 liberty desire for having 100% of the overlord's forces, scaling proportionately (e.g. +37.5 at 50%).
          + The combined strength of all (incorporated) vassals, eyalets, marches, pronoias and soyurghals is used for their liberty desire.
          + Daimyos, all three personal union typies, all five colonial nations, commercial enterprises, both tributaries, trade protectorates, cultural influenced states, appanages, core eyalets and Mongol brother realms only consider their individual strengths.
          + Additionally, nations allied with or supporting the liberty of a subject nation will have their economic strength added to that specific subject. Other subjects will not have their economic strength increased, unless their independence is also supported.

   Liberty desire from navy is calculated as follows:
     * The relative navy size of the subject compared to its overlord. There is +75 liberty desire for having 100% of the overlord's forces, scaling proportionately (e.g. +37.5 at 50%).
          + Only subjects that are considered "overseas" gain liberty desire from navy strength.
          + The combined strength of all (incorporated) vassals, eyalets, marches, pronoias and soyurghals is used for their liberty desire.
          + Daimyos, all three personal union typies, all five colonial nations, commercial enterprises, both tributaries, trade protectorates, cultural influenced states, appanages, core eyalets and Mongol brother realms only consider their individual strengths.
          + Additionally, nations allied with or supporting the liberty of a subject nation will have their navy strength added to that specific subject. Other subjects will not have their navy strength increased, unless their independence is also supported.

Generic modifiers[edit | edit source]

   Generic modifiers to Liberty desire.png liberty desire are:
     * −50 if the overlord and its subject are Friendly attitude historical friends
     * −50 if the subject was recently defeated in an independence war (decreasing over time)
     * −20 for being Naval hegemon with max power
     * −10 for each use of the Placate Local Rulers.png “Placate Local Rulers” subject interaction (capped at −100 and decreases over time by 1 per year)
     * −5 with a Royalmarriage.png royal marriage
     * −5 for each subject's loan paid back with the Pay off debt.png “Pay Off Debt” subject interaction (capped at −100 and decreases over time by 1 per year)
     * −5 per each Development.png development point improved in a subject's province (capped at −100 and decreases over time by 1 per year)
     * −5 Great project level icon tier 1.png /−10 Great project level icon tier 3.png for holding Great project alhambra.png Alhambra (only with Leviathan.png )
     * −5 Great project level icon tier 1.png /−10 Great project level icon tier 2.png for holding Great project Kyoto.png Imperial City of Kyoto (only with Leviathan.png )
     * −3 per point of Diplomatic reputation.png diplomatic reputation
     * −0.5 per Development.png province development granted in a peace deal or with the Grant Province.png “Grant province” subject interaction (capped at −100 and decreases over time by 0.1 per month)
     * ±0.4 per point of trust below/above 50 (min −20 at 100 trust, max +20 at 0 trust)
     * −0.1 for each point of Opinion.png positive relations (max −20 at +200)
     * +0.2 for each point of Opinion.png negative relations (max +40 at −200)
     * +0.3 per 1% of the subject's development that has the Revolution target.png revolution (this does not apply to client subjects)^[11]
     * +5 for each level the overlord's Diplomatic tech.png diplomatic technology is behind the subject's
     * +10 subject nation is a Government steppe horde.png Steppe nomads
     * +50 for historical Rivalry attitude rivals

     * +2 for cultural influenced states, per each Prestige.png prestige below 0 (up to +200 liberty desire at -100 Prestige.png prestige)

Enhance provinces of subject nations[edit | edit source]

   It is possible for the overlord to construct buildings in the provinces of subjects, and to develop them. Each time the overlord develops a subject's province, their Liberty desire.png liberty desire is reduced by 5%, decaying by +0.1% per month. However, since this increases the subject's development, it also increases base liberty desire by +0.25 for those subject types that have development-based liberty desire (i.e. not personal unions), and can increase their liberty desire based on relative power.

Diplomatic Annexation[edit | edit source]

   Ambox outdated info.png
   Please help with verifying or updating this section. It was last verified for version 1.23.

   Most Subjects can be diplomatically annexed/integrated by their overlord through the Annex vassal / Integrate diplomatic option. Annexation occupies a Diplomat.png diplomat until complete, and results in direct control of the former subject's territory and military.

   The requirements for initiating diplomatic annexation are:
    1. The subject has been a subject for a certain amount of time, depending on type (usually 10 or 50 years).
    2. Subjects opinion of overlord is at least 190.
    3. Liberty desire is less than 50%.
    4. Subject is at peace.
    5. Subject has control of its Capital.png capital.
    6. Subject has at least one core province that can be cored.

   Personal unions have one additional conditions to be integrateable:
    1. Senior partner has more provinces than junior partner.

   Uniquely, the time after which they can be integrated, can be reduced by the "Years for Personal Union Integration" modifier:
   Years for personal union integration.png Traditions Ideas Bonuses Policies
   −10                                      —
     * Angevin idea 4: The Many Thrones of the Plantagenet

   —
     * Infrastructure-Diplomatic: Smooth Integration Act

   Further modifiers:
                                                                       Type                                                                      Years for personal union integration.png
   Tier 1 Government monarchy.png Reform "Unified Kalmar Monarchy" for Flag of Denmark Denmark                                                   −40
   permanent modifier “Hegemons of Western Europe” from the Mission.png Hegemon of Europe mission which is available for Flag of Austria Austria −10
   permanent modifier “Universal Monarchy” from the Mission.png Universal Monarchy mission which is available for Flag of Spain Spain            −10
   holding Great project schonbrunn palace.png Schönbrunn Palace Great project level icon tier 3.png                                             −5
   Tier 1 Government monarchy.png Reform "Burgundian State" for Flag of Burgundy Burgundy                                                        −5

   Annexation progress of subjects appears in the diplomacy interface as a horizontal progress bar next to the vassalage icon Vassalage.png . If the annexation process is cancelled before completion, all progress is lost, including the invested Diplomatic power.png diplomatic power.

   Diplomatic annexation will be paused if:
     * the Subject's Liberty desire.png liberty desire is greater than 50%;
     * the Subject does not have control of its Capital.png capital; or
     * the Subject is at war and any of its provinces are occupied by rebels or an enemy nation.

   For Personal Unions only:
     * Integration will be immediately cancelled at the end of the month, if both countries are no longer members of the same religious group. This can be avoided by force-converting the Junior partner or changing the Senior partner's religion through rebels.

Cost[edit | edit source]

   The full formula for diplomatic annexation cost is:

   {\displaystyle {\text{dip point cost}}={\text{floor}}\left(\sum _{\text{per province}}\left[8\cdot {\text{development}}\cdot (1-{\text{administrative efficiency}})\cdot \left(1+\sum {\text{annexation cost modifiers}}\right)\cdot \left(1+\sum {\text{all power costs modifiers}}\right)\cdot \left(1+\sum {\text{local coring cost modifiers}}\right)\right]\right)}

   Development of provinces the overlord already has cores on is not included. The cost reduction from administrative efficiency is capped at 90% and the final cost per province can not go below 0.1 dip points per development(or 1.25% of the normal cost). The final cost for the whole country is rounded, so it can be 0 in extreme cases.

   The base annexation cost is 8 Diplomatic power.png diplomatic power per stated Development.png development of the Subject and 4 Diplomatic power.png diplomatic power per Development.png development in territories and trade company provinces. Provinces on which the overlord has cores don't cost anything to integrate. Having claims or permanent claims on some provinces of the vassal does not change the integration cost. This cost is decreased by Administrative efficiency.png administrative efficiency, All power costs.png all power cost modifiers and Diplomatic annexation cost diplomatic annexation cost modifiers. Speed of annexation[edit | edit source]

   The overlord invests diplomatic power into the annexation process each month at the following rate:
     * +2 base rate
     * +1 if same religion
     * +1 if in same Culture icon.png culture group
     * ±1 per positive/negative point of Diplomatic reputation.png diplomatic reputation.

   If the total balance of diplomatic power is 0 or negative (hence the balance cannot cover the monthly rate), annexation will pause, but not reverse

   Note that if integrating multiple subjects concurrently, this monthly rate as above will apply to each subject independently (modified for the culture and religion of each), even if it results in a monthly diplomatic power deficit. As long as there is still a positive diplomatic power balance to cover the monthly deficits, progress will continue. Should stockpiled Diplomatic power become zero or less, all integration will pause and only resume when the stockpile is positive again.

Effects[edit | edit source]

   Annexation is completed once the required diplomatic monarch points are spent, and results in the following effects:
     * Control of all the subjects provinces, army, and navy. This may put the overlord over its force limit.
     * Fully Cores on all the subjects core provinces.
     * Control of the subjects former subjects
     * +5 prestige.
     * An event gives the "Annexed Subjects" national modifier for 10 years giving Diplomatic reputation.png  −3 diplomatic reputation. (While the penalty does not stack, the duration of the penalty does so annexing 3 vassals will result in a 30 years penalty). You can avoid getting this penalty via the following:
          + Nobility integration
          + maratha
          + Rajput
          + Reform the league (maya mission), only for mesoamerican tributaries

Military focus[edit | edit source]

   Ambox outdated info.png
   Please help with verifying or updating this section. It was last verified for version 1.30.

   A nation can set its subject's military focus to any of the following, which will determine how they behave in wars. If the subject has more than 50% liberty desire, they will always behave as though set to passive.
     Focus                                         Behaviour
   No focus   The subject will decide its own strategies.
   Supportive The subject will seek to attach to friendly armies.
   Aggressive The subject will be aggressive towards enemies, seeking battles in enemy territory.
     Focus                                                         Behaviour
   Passive   This will make the subject stay with armies in their own territory, and defend there. Unless escaping a larger threat.
   Defensive This will make the subject defend its allies' territory. (Recommended for stronger subjects)
   Siege     This will make the subject use its armies to siege down hostile fortresses and not seek any battles.

Technology

   From Europa Universalis 4 Wiki
   Jump to navigation Jump to search

   Please help with verifying or updating older sections of this article.
   At least some were last verified for /eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ href="https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/Europa_Universalis_4_Wiki:Versioning" https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/title="Europa Universalis 4 Wiki:Versioning">version
   1.30.
   Technology interface

   There are three technology types that line up with the three types of monarch points. Each type is divided into 33 levels of technology which enable new abilitiehttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/s, buildings or units or improve existing skills. Each technology level in the game is associated with a parhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ticular year that corresponds roughly to when that technology historically appeared. (See: Year column in the https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/lists of technologies.)

Types[edit | edit source]

Administrative[edit | edit source]

   Administrative tech.png Administrative technology is the broad group that makes new government types available, increases production efficiency, unlocks national idea slots, and enables thehttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ construction of a wide range of different buildings, most of which are related to issues of stability and income. Higher levels also provide more administrative efficiency for your country, which means less coring costs and less aggressive expansion impacts but also higher liberty desire in colonial nation subjects. Most formable nations require administrative technology level 10 to form.

Diplomatic[edit | edit source]

   Diplomatic tech.png Diplomatic technology is primarily related to interactions with other nations and far off lands. This research area increases trade efficiency, colonization range, diplomatic influence, and naval power. The buildings that diplomatic technology allows are trade and sea related.

Military[edit | edit source]

   Military tech.png Military technology focuses on improving the performance of land forces and provides access to new troop types, increases the morale, maneuver and tactics of armies, and allows construction of buildings associated with warfare, including https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/recruitment centers and fortresses.

   Each country belongs to a technology group, which deterhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/mines the initial starting level of technology and in general terms how much of the map is discovered at the beginning of the game.^[1]https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ Each group has a unique list of land unit types representing the general military strategy of similar countries. To view your technology group open the Military tab which lists all your units and the number of each type. The technology group is wrhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/itten at the top of the unit list.

   Almost all countries in a givehttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/n tech group begin the game either embracing the institution of feudalism or not (exceptions to this rule are listed below). Those that don't therefore start with a 50% penalty to technology cost due to institutions. Those that do embrace it have no such penalty until reaching techs that require Renaissance. All countries in a givehttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/n tech group begin the game with their given tech level, regahttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/rdless of whether or not that country begins with a tech penalty that deviates from the standard institution penalty of their given tech group. For more information, see Institutions.

Cost[edit | edit source]

   Ambox outdated info.png
   Please help with verifying or updating this section. It was last verified for version 1.30.

   The cost for researching a new technology level consists of the base cost, 600 monarch points,^[2] multiplied by the current multiplied by the current institution penalty and all modifiers, plus 100%.

  Institution penalty[edit | edit source]

          Main article: Institutions

   There are eight world-changing ideas that spread throughout the world over the course of history. Societies that haven't embraced these ideas will have a harder time keeping up in technology as the rest of the world, especially Europe where these ideas usually originate, outpaces them. Each technology has specific institution requirements, which will increase tech cost by +15%, +30% or +50% when not fulfilled, and give a corresponding bonus to the maximum number of stockpiled monarch points. These penalties accumulate as additional institutions appear; at the extreme, a country that still hasn't embraced any institution in 1821 will have a +400% penalty to technology cost.

  General modifiers[edit | edit source]

   General modifiers reduce the cost of all technology types.

    Increase over time[edit | edit source]

   Technology cost increases over time.^https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/[3] This increase is linear and only depen#91;3&]
   This increase is linear and only depends on the historic discovery date of the current technology of a country. This means if the historic discovery date of the current technolohttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/gy is 1444 the increase to discover the next technology is 0% and if the historic discovery date of the current technology is 1821 the increase is 30%.^[4&#https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/93;

    Neighbor https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/bonus[edit | edit source]

   A counthttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ry will get a -5%^[5] (up to a maximum of https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/-75%^[6]) to technology cost for each level in a technology type it is behind the most advanced nation either bordering the countryhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ with a land connection to its own capital or in the same technology group as the country. This means that a Chinese or Indian nation will see a benefit merely from bordering a Western nation when the border connects via https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/land to its capital, but a less-advanced Western nation will not https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/be helped more by expanding to the borders of a highly advanced one (as it gains the bonus through technology group).

    Espionage bonus[edit | edit source]

   /eu4.paradoxwikis.com/e class="metadata plainlinks ambox mbox-small-left ambox-notice" style="">
   The Cossacks.png Available only with the The Cossacks DLC enabled.

   Once you have Study Technology (Dihttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/plomacy 9), the cost of a technology is reduced if you havehttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ a spy network in a nation that has that technology. The reduction scales with the size of the spy network. At 100 spy network the reduction is −5% per technology that the other country is ahead. The maximum reduction is −30%.

Ahead of thttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ime penalty and bonus[edit | edit source]

   Ambox outdated info.png
   Please help with verifying or updating this section. It was last verified for version 1.30.

   A country is ahead of time in a technology type if the game year is earlier than the historic discovery date of the current technology.

   If a nation has a technology that is ahead of time, the technology cost for the next technology of this type is increased by 10%^[8] per yehttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ar ahead. Please note that this penalty is calculated with respect tohttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ the historical date of the current technology, not the one being researched.

   While a nation has a technology that is ahead of time, it will also receive a bonus depending on the technology type:
     * Administrative technologies will grant a Production efficiency.png +20% production efficiency bonus and Corruption.png -0.05 corruption^[#cite_note-9">[9]
     * Diplomatic technologies will grant a Trade efficiency.png +20% trade efficiency bonus and Corruption.png -0.05 corruption^[10]https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/
     * Military technologies do not grant any additional bonus^[11]

   Trade nodes
   Historical centers of trade and other provincial trade power modifiers in 1444.

   Trade and production of trahttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/de goods are two of the three main sources of income/eu4.paradoxwikis.com/a> for a country, the third being taxes. Every province produces trade goods, which give production income to their owner directly. The trade value of the goods then enters a system of trade nodes, where it is steered and eventually collected by merchants as trade income.

Summary[edit | edit source]

   The trade system in game canhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ be summarized as follows:
     * Trade nodes across the world are connected to form a global network of trade. Each node hosts the trade activity of a group of geographically associated provinces. Money in this global trade network can flow between trade nodes in unidirectional trade routes as well as terminate at end nodes. These connections between trade nodes are fixed and cannot be altered during the course of play.
     * Trade value represents the monthly sum of locally produced and incoming trade goods in a trade node. Trade value is generated from the https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/quantity and price of produced trade goods in each province. All provinhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ces pool their trade value into the total trade value of their associated trade node. The trade tab provides an aggregate trade value in a node while the trade map mode displays a tooltip listing locally produced goods separately from incoming trade good values.
     * Trade power is a number representing a country's control over trade in a node. The trade power of a counthttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ry as a proportion of the total trade power of all countries present in the node determines what will happen to the trade value in each node. Power is used either to retain trade value within thhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/e node (if the nation is collecting with a merchant or at its home node), or to transfer it forward in the trade network (if the nation is steering from there with a merchant, or it's not its home node and it has no merchant). Trade power is generated by provinces, light ships, and merchants. Certain ideas, events and modifiers can also affect a country's trade power in a node.
     * Merchants can be sent to a trade node to collect a portion of the node's thttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/rade value proportional to the nation's share of trade power in the node, or steer the node's trade value in a particular direction.

Sources of trade value[edit | edit source]

   Ambox outdated info.png
   Please help with verifying or updating this section. It was last verified for version 1.25.

          See also: Trade goods

   The Krakow trade node, showing all sources of local trade value.

   All trade income ultimately originates ashttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ provincial trade value.

Local trade value[edit | edit source]

   The trade value of a province is equal to Local goods produchttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ed local goods produced × the price of the trade good that the province produces. This value can be seen in the province window. Trade value determines production income, but it is not itself affehttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/cted by either production efficiency or local autonomy. See Trade goods § Goods produced for the details of goods produced; for trade purposes, the most noteworthy modifier is that Government republic.png merchant republics and Tradecompany icon.png trade companies give a bonus – in all provinces in the node, not just their own – to goods produhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ced proportional to their share of trade power in a node

   Trade value can be further increased by a local Trade value.png trade value modifier, which is given by certain events:

   for 10 years.

   The trade value of all provinces in the same trade node is added together to determine the local trade value of the node. This can be seen in the node's window, as well as the ledger and the trade tab.

Multiple merchant bonus[edit | edit source]

   Three merchants steering from Krakow to Baltic Sea, each with a merchant bonus. Thishttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ tooltip is on the outgoing node, but not the steering button.

   In addition to steering outgoing trade value through a particular outgoing link (see below), each merchant applihttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/es a boost to the trade value on that link—that is, the steered trade value increases by a percentage as it passes between the two nodes, so that the incoming trade value of the downstream node is larger than the corresponding outgoing trade value of the upstream node. This affects all trade on that link, not just the merchant's country, so multiple merchants can boost trade on the samhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/e link. The total boost is:
   Merchants Boost             Cumulative
   0         0.0%  0.0%
   1         +5.0% +5.0% https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/
   2         +2.5% +7.5%
   3         +1.6% +9.1%
   4         +1.2% +10.3%
   5         +1.0% +1https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/1.3%

   Having more than five merchants will not increase the boost further. The boost is modified by the country's Trade steering.png trade steering: for example, if the first merchant's country has +20% trade steering, the boost from the merchant will be increased to +6.0%. The merchant order follows a scripted order, so the merchant with the highest trade steering will not necessarily be first.

Total trade value[edit | edit source]

   The total trade value in a trade node is the sum of local trade value and incoming trade value from upstream trade nodes minus outgoing trade value. For details of incoming trade value,https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ see § Transferring tra#Transferring_trade">§ Transferring trade below.

Trade nodes and power[edit | https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/edit source]

   Ambox outdated info.png https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/
   Please help with verifying or updating this section. It was last verified for version 1.25.

   Each land province in the world belongs to exactly one trade node. The https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/trade value from a province is added to the node's local trade value. In addition, most nodes have one or more other incoming nodes, and one or more other outgoing nodes. In this wahttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/y all nodes are connected in a global network, with a handful (e.g. California, Lhasa, and Great Lakes) being origin nodes with nothing upstream of them, and three (English Channel, Genoa, and Venice) being end nodes with nothing downstream of them.

Relative trade power: compehttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/tition over trade value[edit | edit source]

   Nations use [wer.png] trade power to compete in manipulating the flow of trade value in several ways. The absolute amount of trade power is unimportant; what is important is the relative proportion of trade power wielded by a country and others it is cooperating withttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/h, compared to all countries it is competing with. https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/

   Each country's trade power is increased by their Global trade power.png global trade power modifier for all uses.

Collecting trade/eu4.paradoxwikis.com/span class="mw-editsection">[edit | edit source]

   Each country has a main trade city. This is the same as the capital at the start of the game, and usually stays that way. In the trade node that this province belongs to, the country https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/gets an extra Global trade power.png +5 trade power and automatically collects trade. With the /eu4.paradoxwikis.com/a href="https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/Wealth_of_Nations" title="Wealth of Nations"> Wealth of Nahttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/tions.png
   Wealth of Nations expansion, the main trade city can be changed at the cost of Diplomatic power.png 200 diplomatic power. If the capital ahttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/nd main trade city are the same, moving the capital also moves the main trade city for free.

   Countries can also collect trade by sending a Merchants.png merchant. In this case, the country's trade power is reduced by −50%, unless the merchant is sent to the country's main trade cithttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/y. This is a multiplicative modifier, applied after all other modifiers.^[1] This penalty can be reduced by:

   When collecting trade in a node, the country is allocated a portion of the node's trade value equal to:

          {\displaystyle {\text{Collected value}}=({\text{Total value remaining in the node}})\times {\frac {\text{Trade power in node}}{\text{Total effective trade power in node from collecting countries}}}}

   The effective trade power in a node only counts the trade power of the countries which collect or which transfer downstream, but it doesn't count the countries which have their trade capital upstream.

   This amount is then multiplied by 1 + the country's Trade efficiency.png trade efficiency:

   And this amount,
   [MATH: <semantics> <mrow class="MJX-TeXAtom-ORD"> <mstyle displaystyle="true" scriptlevel="0"> <mrowhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ class="MJX-TeXAtom-ORD"> <mtext>Earned value</mtext> </mrow> </mstyle> </mrow> <annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{\displaystyle {\text{Earned value}}}</annotation> <https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/semantics> :MATH]
