   Each country collecting trade competes with all other countries collecting trade and all countries transferring trade.

Transferring trade[edit | edit source]

   Trade node window, showing the tooltip for trade forwarded out of the node. The cursor is hovering over the red part of the pie chart.

   A country with trade power in a node who either has a merchant present and set to steer, or is not collecting there buhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/t is collecting in a node somewhere downstream (no matter how many hops away), is transferring. There are two stages to transferring trade:
    1. The total value of the transfer: Countries aggregate their trade power (whether they have a merchant present or not) to increase the total share of trade value that leaves the node (outgoing trade value); that is, competing against those who are collecting in the node and hence "retaining trade".
    2. The direction of the transfer: Of those countries transferring with merchants (and only them) their relative trade power determines the share of outgoing trade value that flows into one particular outgoing node.

Pulling trade value forward[edit | edit source]

   All countries transferring trade pool their trade power to pull trade out of the node. The amount of outgoing trade value is equal to

          [MATH: <semantics> <mrow class="MJX-TeXAtom-ORD"> <mstyle displaystyle="true" scriptlevel="0"> <mrow class="MJX-TeXAtom-ORD"> <mtext>Outgoing trade value</mtext> </mrow> <mo>=</mo> <mrow class="MJX-TeXAtom-ORD"> <mtext>Total trade value in node</mtext> </mrow> <mo>×</mo> <mrow class=https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/"MJX-TeXAtom-ORD"> <mfrac> <mrow> <mo>∑</mo> <mrow class="MJX-TeXAtom-ORD"> <mtext>Trade power of countries thttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ransferring</mtext> </mrow> </mrow> <mrow> <mo>∑</mo> <mrow class="MJX-TeXAtom-ORD"> <mtext>Trade power of counthttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ries transferring</mtext> </mrow> https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ <mo>+</mo> <mo>∑</mo> <mrow class="MJX-TeXAtom-ORD"> <mtext>Trade power of countries collecting</mtext> </mrow> </mrow> </mfrac> </mrow> </mstyle> https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/</mrow> <annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{\displaystyle {\text{Outgoing trade value}}={\text{Total trade value in node}}\times {\frac {\sum {\text{Trade power
          of countries transferring}}}{\sum {\text{Trade power of countries transferring}}+\sum {\text{Trade power of countries collecting}}}}}</annotation> </semantics> :MATH]
          {\displaystyle {\text{Outgoing trade value}}={\text{Total trade value in node}}\times {\frac {\sum {\text{Trade power of countries transferring}}}{\sum {\text{Trade power of countries transferring}}+\sum {\text{Trade power of countries collecting}}}}}

   or, equivalently,

          [MATH: <semantics> <mrow class="MJX-TeXAtom-ORD"> <mstyle displaystyle="true" scriptlevel="0"> <mrow class="MJX-TeXAtom-ORD"> <mtext>Outgoing trade value</mtext> </mrow> <mo>=</mo> <mrow class="MJX-TeXAtom-ORD"> <mtext>Total trade value in node</mtext> </mrow> <mo>−</mo> <mo>∑</mo> <mrow class="MJX-TeXAtom-ORD"> <mtext>Trade value collected by each country</mtext> </mrow> </mstyle> </mrow> <annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{\displaystyle {\text{Outgoing trade value}}={\text{Total trade value in node}}-\sum {\text{Trade value collected by each country}}}</annotation> </semantics> :MATH]
          {\displaystyle {\text{Outgoing trade value}}={\text{Total trade value in node}}-\sum {\text{Trade value collected by each country}}}

   At this stage, all countries transferring trade cooperate with each other, and compete with those collecting.

Steering trade[edit | edit source]

   Each country transferring with a Merchants.png merchant present selects an outgoing node to steer trade to (the player does this from the trade map mode). All countries steering in a particular direction cooperate with each other, and chttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ompete with those steering in other directions as well as those collecting,https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ whereas they neither compete nor cooperate at this stage with countries transferring but not steering. The amount of trade value steered towards a particular node is

          [MATH: <semantics> <mrow class="MJX-TeXAtom-ORD"> <mstyle displaystyle="true" scriptlevel="0"> <mrow class="MJX-TeXAtom-ORD"> <mtext>Steered trade value</mtext> </mrow> <mo>=</mo> <mrow class="MJX-TeXAtom-ORD"> <mtext>Outgoing trade value</mtext> </mrow> <mo>×</mo> <mrow class="MJX-TeXAtom-ORD"> <mfrac> <mrow> <mo>∑</mo> <mrow class="MJX-TeXAtom-ORD"> <mtext>Modified trade power of countries steering to this node</mtext> </mrow> </mrow> <mrow> <mo>∑</mo> <mrohttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/w class="MJX-TeXAtom-ORD"> <mtext>Modified trade power of all countries steering</mtext> </mrow> </mrow> </mfrac> </mrow> </mstyle> </mrow> <annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{\displaystyle {\text{Steered trade value}}={\text{Outgoing trade value}}\times {\frac {\sum {\text{Modified trade power of countries steering to this node}}}{\sum {\text{Modified trade power of all countries steering}}}}}</annotation> </semantics> :MATH]
          {\displaystyle {\text{Steered trade value}}={\text{Outgoing trade value}}\times {\frac {\sum {\text{Modified trade power of countries steering to this node}}}{\sum {\text{Modified trade power of all countries steering}}}}}

   Trade node window and trade map mode. The tooltip (on the steering button) lists countries steering in each direction, their trade power used to steer and trade steering bonus, and the percentage of power used to steer in each direction. Notice the trade power listed in the window for Lithuania, Teutonic Order and Sweden, which is used to pull trade forward, and thehttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ir power listed in the tootip, which is used for steering and is higher due to their trade steering bonuses.

   In this equation, "modified trade power" means the country's trade power multiplied by 1 + its Trade steering.png trade steering modifier. If thttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/his would be a division by zero (i.e. no trade power is used to steer), it is instead set to

          [MATH: <semantics> <mrow class="MJX-TeXAtom-ORD"> <mstyle displaystyle="true" scriptlevel="0"> <mrow class="MJX-TeXAtom-ORD"> <mtext>Steered trade value</mtext> </mrow> <mo>=</mo> <mrow class="MJX-TeXAhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/tom-ORD"> <mfrac> <mtext>Outgoing trade value</mtext> <mtext>Number of outgoing nodes being transferred to</mtext> </mfrac> </mrow> </mstyle> https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ </mrow> <annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{\displaystyle {\text{Steered trade value}}={\frac {\text{Outgoing trade value}}{\text{Number of outgoing nodes being transferred to}}}}</annotation> </semantics> :MATH]
          {\displaystyle {\text{Steered trade valuehttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/}}={\frac {\text{Outgoing trade value}}{\text{Number of outgoing nodes behttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ing transferred to}}}} .

   In other words, if no one is steering in any direction, trade value is divided equally between all outgoing nodes. (But in this situation a downstream node will only be considered for transferring trade vhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/alue if someone is transferring between those nodes, i.e. they have trade phttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ower in both of them. For example, at the start of the game when all provinces in the Caribbean and Polynesian Triangle are uncolonized, all trade leaving Mexico goes to Panama; when the Caribbean is colonized, it's divided between there and Panama, but still none goes to the Polynesian Trianglehttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/.)

   There are two important consequences of this equation: /eu4.paradoxwikis.com/p>
     * Countries that are not steering with a merchant have no influence whatsoever over the direction in which trade flows. They only influence how much trade value leaves the node.
     * If the amount of trade power used to steer towards a particular outgoing node is zehttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ro, then value of trade steered there is zero (unless it is zero for all outgoing nodes).https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ In other words, if there are merchants steering, but one outgoing node has no merchants steering to it, then that node receives no transferred trade value at all. If only one country is steering, all trade leaving the node goes to the node that country selected, no matter how tiny their trade power is.

Transfers from traders downstream[edit | edit source]

   Ming has 14.1 provincial trade power in the Yumen node. They don't collect here or anywhere downstream, but 20% of their https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/unmodified provincial power transfers to the incoming node Beijing. You see this bluhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/e left-facing arrow in nodes not upstream of any collection, but the transfer happens also in collecting and transferring nodes.

   Any nation that has at least 10 https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/provincial trade power in the node enjoys the prhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/opagation of that power upstream. An amount equivalent to 20% of the nation's provincial trade power is added to the total trade power of that nation in every immediate upstream node, where it is denoted as transfers from traderhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/s downstream. Global trade power modifiers do not apply to the amount considered for propaghttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ation, but are applied in the upstream node instead.^[2]

   If a country has a ship tradepower propagation modifier also a corresponding part of the ship trade power is added to the provincial trade power. E.g. with Ship tradepower propagation.png +20% ship tradepower propagation 20% × 20% = 4% of ship trade power is also added to upstream node.

Trade company[edit | edit source]

          Main article: Trade company

   Wealth of Nations.png Dharma.png Available only with the Wealth of Nations DLC or the Dharma DLC enabled.
   Ambox outdated info.png
   Please help with verifying or updating this section. It was last verified for version 1.30.

   A country that owns a province in a trade node that is not in their home node but is in a trade company region can add it to a Tradecompany icon.png trade company. Provinces in trade companies get Province trade power modifier.png +100% local https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/trade power. There are 63 trade company regions throughout the old world.
   /eu4.paradoxwikis.com/h3>Protect trade[edit | edit source]

Having the ships out of port for the Protect Trade mission costs Sailors.png −1 sailor per ship per month.

Supply range[edit | edit source]

   Light ships on protect trade missions can only be sent to trade nodes where the country already has trade power and the /eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ href="https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/Supply_range" class="mw-redirehttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ct" title="Supply range">supply range
   is met. The limitation on supply range applies even when naval attrition is removed at Diplomatic tech.png https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ diplomatic tech 22. If the trade range permits, a country can send a merchant to a node without any initial trade power and then follow up with light ships protecting trade https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/(as long as these are within supply range). A good way to arrange for a favorable supply range is by gaining fleet basing rights from a nation in the vicinity of the target trade node. /eu4.paradoxwikis.com/h3>Other sourhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ces of trade power[edit | edit source]
     * Merchant Present: The presence of a merchttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/hant increases a nation's trade power by +2.
     * Main trade port in area: A nation gets additional +5 trade power in its home node.
     * Colonial nations provide their overlord with 50% of their trade power.
     * With Mare Nostrum.png Mare Nostrum, members of a Trade league.png trade league:
          + provide 50% of their trade power to the leader of the league
          + provide an extra Trade steering.png +2.5% trade steering to the leader of the league (cumulative with the bonus from other members); for example 10 league members would provide +25% trade steering power to the merchant republic leading the league
          + get an additional Ship trade power.png +20% ship trade power.
     * Other nations can be persuaded (through diplomacy) or forced (through war) to enter into a Transfer Trade Power relation, which does not count towards the diplomatic relhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ations limit. This transfers one country's trade power to another:https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ a transfer enforced in a truce transfers 50%, while a diplomatically arranged transfer can transfer any amount from zehttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ro to 50%. Personal unions and vassals do not transhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/fer trade power to their suzerain. Only nodes where both countries have power are affected. The trade power gained this way is not halved due to collecting outside the country's main trade node.
     * Countries that have vassals or marches have a subject interaction for them to divert trade, which transfers 100% of their vassal's trade power, https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/at a cost of Liberty desire.png +30% liberty desire.

Merchants[edit | edit source]

   Ambox outdated info.png
   Please help with verifying or updating this section. It was last verified for version 1.25.

   Merchants are envoys used to alter the flow of Trade value.png trade value by collecting or shttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/teering trade. A merchant must be stationed at a trade node to have any effect and can only travel a distance defined by a country's Trade range.png trade range. A merchant present in a trade node gives a bonus of +10% to https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/Trade efficiency.png trade efficiency and also increases the Global trade power.png trade power by 2 in that node.

Trade with no merchant[edit | edit source]

   In the absence of merchants:
     * In the country's home node, the country will collect trade.
     * In non-home nodes that are not upstream from any nodes where the country is collecting trade, their trade power does not affect the flow of trade. It still propagates upstream if the country has at least 10 provincial trade power.
     * In all other nodes, trade power is used to pull trade forward, increasing the share of trade value transferred. There is no influence on the direction of trade (if at least one country is steering), only the amount transferred.
          + Exception: If no one is steering at a node, and no one with power there has power in a given downstream node, no trade is transferred there. Subsequently a country can induce trade to be transferred to that node by merely having trade power in both, if there is still no one steering.

Merchant actions[edit | edit source]

   Merchants can be sent to a trade node to perform one ohttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/f two missions (as denoted in game interface):
     * Collect from Trade: Use the country's trade power to retain trade in the node, and turn it into Gold Icon.png income.
          + In other nodes than the country's home node, this gives a multiplicative penalty of Global trade phttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ower.png −50% trade power.^[1]
     * Transfer Trade Power: Usehttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ the country's trade power to pull trade forward in the trade networhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/k, and simultaneously to influence trade to flow preferentiallyhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ into one of the downstream nodes (see § Steering trade above). The player can choose the direction to steer trade in using the trade map mode. (The name of this mission is a misnomer, as it is trade value that is being steered, not trade power.)
        https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/
          + A merchant steering trade in inland nodes enables the Caravan power.phttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ng caravan bonus.

/eu4.paradoxwikis.com/span class="mw-headline" id="Trade_range">Trade range[edit | edit source]

   Merchanthttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/s can only reach nodes at this distance from a cored province (or a corehttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/d province of a junior partner, colonial nation or client state). The distance is measured to the central province of the node, visible on the trade map mode. Base trade range is increased by Diplomatic tech.png diplomatic technology (100 at tech 1 and 400 at tech 32) and some decisions and ideas.

Merchant bonus[edit | edit source]

   If no merchant is currently collectinhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/g outside the home node, then the home node receives a +10% bonus to trade power for each merchant who is steering trade. This is a cumulative bonus, hence it is a big decision and sometimes hard to make the analysis depending on whether one should collect ihttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/n other nodes or only steer trade. The quickest check is to compare the trade value in your income tab beforhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/e and after your proposed changes; keeping the combination with the highest final result to your trade income. At most you'll lose some income during the envoy travel time of the merchants while experimenting.

   Note that during times of war when they embargo your home node, and hence siphon your income, set some of the other upstream nohttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/des to rather collect trade than to steer to the home node. This will avoid losing much of your trade incomehttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ during the war.

Trade steering[edit | edit source]

   Trade steering.png Trade steering has two effects:
     * Trade steering is appliedhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ as a multiplicative bonus to trade power used for steering when determining which outgoing node trade is steered to.
     * Additionally it is used to increase the trade value that a nation steers in a given direction (see § Multiple merchant bonus).

This means for example that 10 league members would provide +25% trade steering power (being 10 × +2.5%) to the merchant republic leading the league.

Embargo[edit | edit source]

   Ambox outdated info.png
   Please help with verifying or updating this section. It was last verified for version 1.25.

   Embargoing is an option in the diplomacy screen that allows a country to leverage their trade power against another nation's, decreasing that nation's trade power in shared trade nodes. The trade screen shows icons for each nation embargoed and those embargoing your nation. Placing the mouse over each nation icon breaks down the penalties in each shared trade node.

   Embargoing a country has the following effects:^[5]
     * The defending countryhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ suffers a penalty to trade power in all trade nodes that both countries have power in. The base magnitude of the penalty is half of the attacker's trade power share in the trade node before the embargo. This penalty stacks multiplicatively with other modifiers.
     * The defending country's opinion of the attacking country is modified by −15. The defender also gains a Trade Dispute casus belli against the attacker unless the embargo is mutual.
     * The attacking country's trade efficiency suffers a −5% trade efficency penalty unless the defender is a rival.
     * Embargoes do not count against the Diplomatic Relation limit.
     * The attacking country gains up to Power Projection.png +10 power projection if the target is a rival, the amount depending on how severely the embargo affects the target's trade.

   Winning a Parliament.png parliament debate "Issue Letters of Marque" provides +10% embargo efficiency for 10 years.

   Each point of mercantilism provides /eu4.paradoxwikis.com/n class="effect-green">+0.5%
   embargo efficiency, capped at +50%.

   Embargo Efficiency can be increased by the following:
   Embargo efficiency.png Traditions                                Ideas                                 Bonuses Policies
   +25%                   —
     * Vermont idea 2: The Boston Tea Party

   —                      —
   +10%                   —
     * Betsimisaraka idea 2: https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/Pirate Ports
     * Cebu idea 5: 'The Place for Trading' /eu4.paradoxwikis.com/li>Cypriot idea 7: Raid Turkish Commerce
     * Malagasy idea 3: Pirate Ports
     * Mindanao idea 7: Pirates of Mindanao
     * Montenegrin idea 4: Balkan Gusars

Privateering[edit | edit source]

   Ambox outdated info.png
   Please help with verifying or updating this section. It was last verified for version 1.25.

          Main article: Naval warfare#Privateering

   Wealth of Nations.png El Dorado.pnghttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ Mare Nostrum.png Golden Century.png Available only with Wealth of Nations, El Dorado, Mare Nostrum or Golden Century DLC enabled.

   Any fleet that contains light ships can be sent on a privateering mission to any trade node within trade range. The fleet will hoist the Jolly Roger and add the trade power of its light ships (plus a bonus) to a dummy "pirate" nation in the node, thus reducing the trade power share of everyone in the node – including their controller, though a portion of the trade value lost this way is returned to the controller, listed in accounts as "spoils of war". This effectively behaves as though they are collecting. Unlike protecting trade, privateers can be sent to nodes a nation has no power in, making it a way of weakening the nation's enemies or gaining revenue from nodes ithttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ can't touch otherwise. Privateering a rival's trade generates power projection.https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ Privateers can also intercept treasure fleets, stealing a portion of the gold transported from a colonial nation.

Hunt pirates[edit | https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/edit source]

   https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/

          Main article: Naval wahttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/rfare#Hunt pirates

   Mare Nostrum.png El Dorado.png Available only with the Mare Nostrum DLC or the El Dorado DLC https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/;enabled.

   This mission is available to fleets which conhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/tain at least one ship that isn't a transporthttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/. Fleets containing heavy ships or light ships may hunt pirates in any non-inland trade node; however, fleets containing only galleys (as well as fleets which are a mixture of galleys and transports) can only hunt pirates in nodes whehttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/re all nearby sea provinces are inland seas.

   Pirate-hunting fleets reduce the tradhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/e power taken by the dummy "pirates" nation in the chosen trade node byhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ reducing their privateer efficiency. They do not actually damage or take damage from any ships.

Strategies[edit | edit source]

   Strategy The below is one of many player suggested strategies for Trade. Bear in mind, due to the dynamic nature of the game, it may unfold differently for other players.

   Effectively managing trade is key to give a nation the economic edge it needs to both survive and gain an adhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/vantage over its neighbours. Therefore, knowing how to both https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/optimise one's trade income and undermine its competitors' income is instrumental in securing most of thhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/e game's objectives, both militarily and economically.

/eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ class="mw-headline" id="Secure_the_home_node">Secure the home node/eu4.paradoxwikis.com/n class="mw-editsection">[edit | edit source]

   While most great orienhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/tal nations (Mamluks, Ottomans and Ming), and those dominating the end nohttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/des (England, Aragon/Spain, Venice), do not struggle in controlling thehttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ir home trade nodes, for other countries, it is often a nightmare to https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/merely secure the trade benefits that derive from their production. Several steps must therehttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/fore be taken by all nations, in order to asshttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ert their control over the trade transiting from their territory, as without it, most of their growth will feed other nations' economies.
     * Choose carefully the location. One elementary step is to look carefully at the current nodes and the streams that go in and out of them. For instance, most land trade nodes will have a hoard of nations with caravans within them, and https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/should therefore be avoided as building up a consequenhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/t share of the trade power there will require far too extensivhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/e resources at first. Also take into account your expansion plans, ahttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/nd try to pick the coastal node where you hold significant powhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/er located the most downstream from all your present and future possessions. Finally, chttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/heck for any powerful country that holds trade power in the nodes yohttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/u're targeting, as dislodging them may be very difficult if sthttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/arting small.
     * Check for all the centers of trade within it: In https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/the node you have chosen, ensure that you hold enough centers of trahttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/de to build up your bonus trade power, once they'll be upgrhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/aded. Also check for the ones held by other countries. Your future whttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ars should be waged at least in part to secure these centers of thttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/rade in order to further assert your dominance over the node, and in https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/turn boost your income.
     * Ensure that enough trade value can flow in it: As you build your empire, you'll eventually reach other nodes. Ensuring that these are locahttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ted upstream of your home node will earn you considerable wealth. Also, check for any upstream land node, where you'll be able to send your merchants. They will be far more effective there than in most coastal nodes, and this will help you earn good trade income right from the beginning of the game even if your starting region is devoid of valuable trade resources.

Expand one node after another[edit | edit source/eu4.paradoxwikis.com/an class="mw-editsection-bracket">]

   Wihttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/th your home node chosen and secured, you should lohttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ok at taking control of the upstream nodes. One should be pahttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/rticularly careful about securing one node after another, as extracting trade valhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ue from a node only to see it collected by a rival in thehttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ next one is both fruitless and dangerous. While expanding, keep in mind some of the following aspects:
     * Go for the centers of trade first: Even if said centers of trade aren't in a strategically important region or may be hard to defend, ensuring that you get to control these will significantly increase your trade phttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ower. Especially in company regions, asserting control of them will help yhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ou by both granting you truly massive trade power and undhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ermining your rivals' efforts, as they also tend to aim these firhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/st.
     * The coastline means everything:https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ It is also important to take into accounthttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ that while monitoring trade in a rich land trade node may require extensive wars, simply going for the coastal nodes and taking all of their provinces if possible will be far more beneficial in the long run. Not only will they allow you to snippet away inland trade through merchants, they may also grant you the ability to "sthttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/eal" the trade value other nations will have extracted farther upstream, as most of intercontinentahttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/l trade flows through oceans and thus coastlines.
     * Be greedy: While going for https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/trade domination, no effort should be spared to enact total control over the nodes you'll https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/be targeting. Even if a nation isn't much of a threat, and you have more important issues to dealhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ with, attacking and taking control of the most provinces possible is essential, especihttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ally in company zones. While you'll be distracted farther away, you may go back 10 years later and find out that your rivals bought off provinces or simply conquered their way in, ruining most of your precedent efforts. Special attention must be paid if you're planning to core your overseas conquests in order to boost your income, as shohttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/rt of the company total trade power bonus every province lost to a rival will severely comprhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/omise your hold. If you're approaching your governing capacihttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ty,
       remember you can make more room by building courthouses, especially in your most developed provinces (and a statehouse can be more valuable than a manufactory in a province with a bad trade good in a large, rich area).

Develop and build[edit | edit source]

   Once your inhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/come gets comfortable enough to allow you to stop conquering a bithttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ and starting building up your provinces, https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/there comes the time to build and develop your provinces.
     * Go for the richest: There is no use in maintaining a homogeneous development in all your provinces. Provinces producing trade goods worth 3.00 ducats or more should be the ones you'll be developing first. Even if they are overseas (as long as they are in trade companies), they can become very vhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/aluable very quickly, and you'll be able to use the newfound money for fhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/urther development projects.
     * Manufactories and workshops are the name of the game: Even if tax income seems to be very lucrative, and in respect production income negligible, keep in mind that autonomy applies fully to tax, half to production income, and not at all to goods produced – and more goods produced also means mhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ore trade value created. With your controlhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ asserted over the node the province is in, your income will rise very quickly once these buildings have been built. Both buildings synergise very well, and it may often be worthwhile to demolish less important buildings (such as churches) to ensure that every valuable province at first, and later on every province, has both of these buildings. Despite their https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/high cost, manufactories increases income from both production anhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/d trade. Since a manufactory give the equivalent of +5 base production in the province it’s built in, you should only build
       manufactories based on the trade good and any local goods produced modifiers. The more expensive a trade good is, the better your manufactory will be and the quicker it will pay off.
     * Strive to be the richest: Using the Trade Value map mode, you cahttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/n quickly check which of your provinces are the most adhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/vanced, and which ones have the most potential. By developing ahttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/nd building up in these, every single one of https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/your provinces should, after a couple decades of attention, reachhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ 10 or more trade value. Also check for policies that increase both production and trade efficiency, as these may give you the decisive edge over your rivals you'll need.

   With these principles in mind, you may be able, starting as any nation, to reach by late game the podium of the world's wealthiest nations. Thhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/is, in turn, will ensure your continued survival throughout thhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/e game history and, as the Industrial Revolution closes in, put you in the best position possible to steamroll the world as its foremost industrial power.

Starting a war[edit | edit source]

   Ambox outdated info.png
   Please help with verifying or updating this section. It was last verified for version 1.30.

   Like most diplomatic actions, declaring war requires a diplomat. War may not be declared on an ally, a subject, a guaranteed nation or a nation transferring you commercial power without first breaking that relation. /eu4.paradoxwikis.com/p>

Cashttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/us belli[edit | edit source]

          Main article: Casus belli

   The aggressor may pick a casus belli when declaring warhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/. This determines the wargoal, the options available in the subsequent peace deal, and their associated costs in warscore, aggressive expansion, and diplomatic power.
   Declaring War with a Casus belli

/eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ class="mw-headline" id="No_casus_belli">No casus belli/eu4.paradoxwikis.com/an class="mw-editsection">[edihttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/t | edit source]

   Declaring war without a casus belli will result in -20 Ae impact.png aggressive expansion, a -2 drop in Icon stability.png stability, and +2 War exhaustion.png war exhaustion. These penalties are halved with full Diplomatic ideas.

/eu4.paradoxwikis.com/span class="mw-headline" id="Good_relations">Good relations[edit | edit source]

   A country dechttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/laring war on another whose opinion of them is higher than 100 will cause -1 stability and +1 war exhaustion. If opinion is higher than 150, penalty increases to -2 stability and +2 war exhaustion.

Co-belligerence[edit | edit source]

   If a country is not marked as a co-belligerent:
     * That country can't call its allies to arms in that war (but its subjects are called as normal). Beware that the Holy Roman Emperor defending the empire is always a co-belligerent.
     * Taking that country's provinces in a peace incurs Ae impact.png +50% aggressive expansion and costs War score.png +100% warscore.

   If a couhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ntry is marked as a co-belligerent:
     * That country chttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/an call on its own allies to fight as well
     * If that country has a guarantor, it is also called tohttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ war
     * Taking that country's provinces will cost the same as the war leader's provinces

   Note: If a nation is marked as a co-bellighttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/erent, but are also a tributary of another nation, neither the tributary overhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/lord, nor the co-belligerent's allies will be called in. A similar loophole also applies in the HRE. If a free city or an HRE member is marked as a co-belligerent neither the Emhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/peror nor the Emperor's allies will be called in. But in this case the allies of the https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/co-belligerent will be called.

Things you cannot do while being at war[edit | edit source]

   https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/Note that while your country is at war you cannot do quite a lot of things:
     * Abdicate ruler
     * Seize estate lands
     * Reduce local autonomy in provinces
     * Upgrade or downgrade Centers of Trade
     * Return, sell, or buy provinces, or grant them to your subjects. However, you still can seize land from your vassals and marches.
     * Release subjects
     * Provoke revolts in your country
     * Sell ships#Sell_ships" title="Diplomacy">Sell ships
     * Threaten war
     * Asking an ally to Prepare for war
     * Offer vassalization to your allies that join the war
     * Establish tributaries, or become a tributary yourself
     * Annex vassals which don't have Scutage enabled
     * Create or revoke a march
     * Intervene in war as a great power
     * Move capital
     * Move main trade city

   The following diplomatic actions can't be used with countries that become your war enemies until war ends:
     * Issue embargo
     * Fabricate claim
     * Send an insult
     * Send warning
     * Give subsidies; existing subsidies are automatically cancelled

   Also, when your country is fighting offensive war AI will reject any alliance offers from you.

Sides in a war[edit | edit source]

   Ambox outdated info.png
   Please help with verifying or updating this section. It was last verified for version 1.24.

   A war consists of two opposing sides of one or more countries. A side may be made up of a coalition, the emperor, allies or the defender of the Faith who honour their treaties and/or vassals and other subject countries.

War leader[edit | edit source]

   The war leaders are denoted with a star in the war screen. The war leader on the attacking side is the country that declared the war, while on the defending side the leader is the country on which the war was declared (the target of the war goal) or, if that country is a non-sovereign subject, their overlord.https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ For each side in a war the leader is the country that may call in its allies and may negotiate peace on behalf of all their war allies, simultaneously ending the war for everybody. They may negotiate a separate peace with each of the hostilhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/e belligerents, except subject nations or coalition members. They may surrender territory of their war allies, but not their allies' treasury.

   When a war leader is annexed in a separate war, one of their allies will become the new war lhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/eader. The new war leader can call their own allies into the war if the war has not lasted long enough to close the window for calling allies to it. If the war leader is vassalized (by event or fohttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/rce) the new overlord will become the new war leader and can call their allies with the same caveat about calling allies to long wars.

Military andhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ port access[edit | edit source]

   All nations on the same side in a war have military achttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/cess to each others' lands. They may also dock at each others' ports, although their fleet supply range will not be extended. Furthermore, all participants have military access to all nations that have given acchttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ess to any participant, and all participants in a war involving the Holy Roman Emperor have access to all members of the empire.

Joining a side[edit | edit source]

   After a war has started, a country usually cannot join any of the sides unless called in later. There are three exceptions to this rule. The enforce peace action allows for a country to force the attacking war leader to sign a white peace. If the attacker does not accept, the enforcer will join the war on the defender's side. Additionally, a country that subjugates a participant will join the war on its new subject's side. Finally, a great power may intervene in a war involving at least three other great powers on the side that has fewer https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/great powers.

   A way of indirectly fighting in a war is for a country to rent out condottieri to one of the countries involved.

Fighting a war[edit | edit source]

          Main articles: Land warfare, Nahttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/val warfare

   War may be fought on both the land and the sea. See the appropriate articles for more information.

War exhaustion[edit | edit source]

          Main article: War exhaustion

   War exhaustion represents the will of a country's population to fight. High war exhaustion will sap the abihttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/lity of a country's armies to fight and reinforce.

Call for peace/eu4.paradoxwikis.com/span>[edit | edit source]

   If the warscore is substantial (66.6%+) and it has been at least 5 years since the war was declared, a country's abstracted population may call for peace. This modifier increases the nation's monthly War exhaustion.png war exhaustion, beginning at +0.005 per month, and ticks up by another +0.005 per month indefinitely. This means a call for peace will eventually start increasing a country's war exhaustion even if it has a monthly reduction, e.g. from being Defender of the Faith, having the 6th Innovative idea, or having the Kind-Hearted ruler trait. Only human players get call for peace.

   Call for peace will also occur if the country fails to submit a peace offer within 3 months of an enemy surrendering unconditionally. In this case the ticking war exhaustion begins at +0.05 per month and increases more quickly.

Warscore[edit | edhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/it source]https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/

   Ambox outdated info.png
   Please help with verifying or updating this section. It was last verified for version 1.29.

   Warscore is the means of measuring whether a war is going in the favor of the aggressor or the defender. It is a common metric used across a number of Paradox Interactive titles, including Europa Universalis III, EUIV, Crusader Kings III and Victoria II.

   The scale ranges from +100% (a complete victory for the side currently being viewed) to −100% (complete defeat for the side currently being viewed).

   Warscore is measured using a number of different parameters:
     * Occupied provinces
     * Battles won or lost, to a maximum of 40% in either directiohttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/n.
     * Blockaded ports
     * Met war goals. A met war goal will cause war score to gradually tick up for whichever side has met it, to a maximum of 25%.

   Note that both sides have symmetrical war goals. It is possible for no one to have met the goal; in particular, Show Superiority warscore won't tick if neither side has more than 10% warscore from battles, and a province goal won't tick if a third party (e.g. rebels) controls it. Hence, for provinces that are being colonized and yet are the war goal, rather seize them for yourself during the war, otherwise the enemy may destroy or abandon them and the target will then cease to exist – unable to provide a ticking war score.

Occupation[edit | edit source]

   Occupation is the term used to describe when a province has been successfully taken over by an enemy country. It requirhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/es the successful siege or assault of the local fortification. Upon occupation of a province, the owner of the province can no longer use the province for many purposes:
     * Regiments, ships and buildings can no longer be built in the province, and any unit or improvement buihttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/lding that was underway (including cores and religious or cultuhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ral conversion) is immediately halted.
     * All province income and trade power is no longer given to the owner; a portion of the province's production income and trade power is now given to the occupier.
     * The owner can no longer use the province for a fleet base; any ships currently in the port are forced out to the adjacent sea zone. The controller does have access to these ports.
     * The province does not count for the owner for calculating naval supply, colonial range and trade range. Thttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/his is important, as one may have to unsiege certain provinces far away in order to take provinces in a peace deal (due to lack of colonial range). Force limits are unaffected.
     * The contrhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/oller of the province can recruit mercenaries there.
     * Occupied forts project a zone of control over unfortified land owned by countries that aren't allied to their occupier.

Transfer occupation[edit | edit source]

   Countries can give up controhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/l over occupied provinces to their allies in war. (The Transfer occupation.png ‘transfer occupation’ button is located on the province screen.) This will make it possible to ensure that nations are rewarded for their participation in the war.

   If you called an ally in with a promise of land, you may often find in the peace deal that they "do not want" the province in question - even if they highlighted it as a "province of interest" in the Diplomatic Feedback window. Hence, they will lose trust in you if you take any land or war reparations. However, there is a solution: before you peace out, make sure that ALL the land they highlighted as "province of interest" are under their control (hence you have transferred occupation to them), then even if you give them nothing, they will not lose trust in you (shown as a thumbs down warning in the peace menu, instead it will be neutral).

Administrative efficiency[edit | edit source]

          Main article: Overextension#Administrative efficiency

   Administrative efficiency is a country wide bonus that is unlocked at administrative technology levehttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/l 17 and increases at 23 and 27, up to a total of 30%. Additionally Absolutism.png Absolutism provides additional administrative efficiency scaling with amount, up to 30% at 100. Administrative efficiency directly reduces core creation and diplomatic annexation costs, as well as the impact of province development on overextension and warscore cost, allowing for much larger territories to be conquered at once.

Sue for peace[edit | edit source]

   https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/
   Ambox outdated info.png
   Please help with vehttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/rifying or updating this section. It was last verified for version 1.24.
   Peace interface, on the "Demand tribute" tab.

   This option will open the peace negotiation screen whttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/here the country will negotiate their demands, the terms of their surrender or simply a white pehttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ace. The leader of each war alliance can make peace separately with each independent country on the other side (except any that joined as part of a coalition), in which case only individual warscore against that country and its subjects is taken into account (battles only count towards overall score). This can be essential to get the desired peace deal - the overall warscore may be https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/lower than against a single participant, so the country can get more out of the war by picking off participants one by one.

Unconditional surrender[edit | edit source]

   Wiki letter w.png
   Please help improve this article or section by expanding it with: when exactly the AI surrenders unconditionally.

   Upon offering unconditional surrender, all of the currently unoccupied provinces will fall under enemy control and the enemy will gain 100% warscore. Armies of the country that surrendhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ered will become exiled and unable to fight in future battles until peace is signed. For the recipient of an unconditional surrender, it will be alerted of the enemy’s surrender and from then on will be able to enforce any possible peace up to 100% warscore cost. If the recipient country does not sign peace after a couple months, they will get call for peace giving them monthly war exhaustion which increases faster than normal. https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/The peace will be automatically accepted by the nation that surrendered. When naturally reaching 100% warscore, the AI will usually uncondihttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/tionally surrender. There are also some other cases in which the AI unchttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/onditionally surrenders.

Peace terms[edit | edit source]

   Each term in a peace offer has an associated cost in warscore, Prestige gain/loss for both sides and possible aggressive expansion for anyone making sizable, selfish demands. An appropriate casus belli may modify any or all of these values, and is required to enable certain terms. A country making peace separately may only accept terms relating to itself and its subjects, not other participanthttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/s in the war.

   Unjustified demands.png Unjustified demands are peace terms that are not part of the wargoal. They will cost 2 Diplomatic power.png per development of affected provinces^[1]:
     * Annex province
     * Return core
     * Cancel https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/subject
     * Release nation
     * Force vassalization

Distribution of spoils[edit | edit source]

   The Cossacks.pnhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/g Available only with the The Cossacks DLC enabled.
   Shows distribute spoils in game.

   Spoils of war are distributed between its participants with prestige and money going to the belligerents of the war based on their war contribution rather than only to the war leader. For example, if Spain and France fight in a war against Great Britain and France gets 70% war contribution and Spain 30% then the prestige and money will be divided so that 70% goes to France and 30% goes to Spain.

Truce[edit | edit source]

   Once a peace deal is accepted, it results in a state of truce between every country on the offering side andhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ every country on the accepting side. Specifically, when a country othhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/er than a war leader accepts peace, or offers a peace deal the other side's war leader accepted, it enters truce with every enemy country still in the war, but its war allies are not affected.

   The duration of the truce depends on the amount of warscore that was used to demand or offer trhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ibute in the peace deal. The formula is
   [MATH: <semantics> <mrow class="MJX-TeXAtom-ORD"> <mstyle displaystyle=https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/"true" scriptlevel="0"> <mrow class="MJX-TeXAtom-ORD"> <mtext>peace duration ihttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/n years</mtext> </mrow> <mo>=</mo> <mn>5</mn> <mspace width="thinmathspace" /> <mo>+</mo> <mspace width="thinmathspace" /> <mn>0.1</mn> <mspace width="thinmathspace" /> <mo>×</mo> <mspace width="thinmathspace" /> <mhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/row class="MJX-TeXAtom-ORD"> <mtext>percentage of war score the peace deal is worth</mhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/text> </mrow> </mstyle> </mrow> <annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{\displaystyle {\text{peace duration in years}}=5\,+\,0.1\,\times \,{\text{percentage of war score the peace deal is worth}}}</annotation> </semantics> :MATH]
   {\displaystyle {\text{peace duration in years}}=5\,+\,0.1\,\times \,{\text{percentage of war score the peace deal is worth}}}

   so a white peace will result in a 5-year truce, whereas a peace deal at 100% war score will produce a 15-year truce. https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/When a country is released in a peace deal, it starts with a 5-year truce withttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/h both the releasing nation and the opposing war leader.

   A country cannot embargo or join a coalition against a country it has a truce with, though ongoing embargoes are unaffected. A country with a truce also cannot be designated co-belligerent. It can still declare or join a war with the country with a truce, but with the following consequences if it is an offensive war:
                      Ideas                    Icon stability.png Stability War exhaustion.png War exhaustion Ae impact.png Aggressive expansion
                     Normal                    −5                           +5https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/   −50
   Full Diplomachttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/y −3                           +3                                −30

   These stack with the penalties for other reasons. So attacking inhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ breach of a truce without a CB and without full diplomacy results in −7 stability, +7 war exhaustion and −70 aggrehttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ssive expansion. As seen above, breaking a truce has very negative effects when declaring war or joining an offensive war against a country with whom a truce exists. The AI has −1000 reasons to join an offensive war if they have a truce with the defenderhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ and appears to never declare war, join as an ally in an offensive war, or call an ally into an offensive war if that would break a truce. Joining defensive wars, or where the country with a truce ishttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ a secondary participant, does not give a penalty.

Revanchism[edit | edit source]

   An example of revanchism.

   Revanchism is a mechanic that helps prevent a "death spiral" after losing a war where a country would go bankhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/rupt, lose manpower and have huge revolts, followed by other countries declaring war as well, leading the nation to ruin. Revanchism is gained from losing provinces in a war and scales in dihttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/rect correspondence to the war score taken in a peace deal, with a max of 100% revanchism at 100% warscore. Revanchism decreases at a rate of 10% per year. Releasing nations and returning cores does not grant revanchism.

   With maximum revanchism of 100% (from having 100% warscore worth taken in a peace deal), a country gets the following modifiers: ^[3]
   Global tax modifier.png     +50% National tax modifier
   Defensiveness.png           +25% Fort defense
   Manpower recovery speed.png +50% Manpower recovery speed
   Yearly army tradition.png   +1%  Yearly army tradition
   Yearly navy tradition.png   +1%  Yearly navy tradition /eu4.paradoxwikis.com/td>
   National unrest.png         −5%  National unrest
   Interest.png                −1%  Interest per annum
   Yearly horde unity.png      +10% Yearly horde unity

   These modifiers scale linearly with revanchism from 0% to 100%.

   Note that revanchism caps out at 100%, even if a peace deal worth more than 100% warscore in total was taken (such as in multiplayer that allows peace deals over 100% warscore or from multiple peace deals).

Full Annexation[edit | edit source]

   https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/Upon annexing all of the provinces of a participant of a war in a peace deal, all subject nations of the annexed nation except personal unions become subjects of the annexing nation. This costs nothing above the cost of annexing the overlord. Junior partners of the annexed nation become independent insteahttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/d.

Negotiating peace[edit | edit source]

   Ambox outdated info.png
   Please help with verifying or updating this section. It was last verified for version 1.24.

   Human players are largely free to accept or refuse any peace deal. However, as with other diplomatic actions, the AI will accept a peace deal if and only if it has more positive than negative reasons to do so.

Warscore[edit | edit source]

   The warscore is of primary importance. Each point of warscore will give +1 reason for the AI to accept a peace deal, whereas each warscore cost of the peace terms will give −1 reason for the AI to accept a peace deal. The AI will refuse all demands if individual warscore is less than 10.

   Demands exceeding warscore will give additional negative reasons for the AI to accephttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/t the peace deal, up to −100 at 99% warscore and lower. Demands exceeding 100% warscore will give −1000 reashttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ons (unreasonable demands, not to be confused with Unjustified demand). Individual demands that would cost over 100% warscore, such as vassalizing a country that is too lahttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/rge, can't be selected.

   If one side of the war has 100% warscore, the country is forced to accept any peace offer of 100% orhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ less warscore. This also applies to losing human players. Note that 100% warscore only happens when one side fully occupies the other and ihttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/s itself completely unoccupied. Otherwise, warscore is capped at 99%.

   Regardlhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ess of warscore, the AI may refuse peace deals that contain terms that they do not desire; for example, provinces they will be unable to core. Such offers cannot be submitted (the "Send Demand" button is greyed out). The only exception is stated above, where the AI is forced thttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/o take a province they are unable to core if the othhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/er side has more than 100% warscore.

   If you called an ally in with a promise of land, you may often find in the peace deal that they "do not want" the province in question - even if they highlighted it as a "province of interest" in the Diplomatihttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/c Feedback window. Hence, they will lose trust in you if you take any land or war reparations. However, there is a solution: before you peace out, make sure that ALL the land they highlighted as "province of interest" are under their control (hence you have transferred occuhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/pation to them), then even if you give them nothing, they will not lose trust in you (shown as a thumbs down warning in the peace menu, instead it will be neuthttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ral).

Provhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ince cost[edit | edit source]

   Each province that changes control in a peace deal requires a corresponding https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/"Province warscore cost. The factors that influence each province's warscore cost are:
   Base 5 per province.
   Developmenhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/t 1 per development, cap at 30^[4]
   Trade power &[4&]
   Trade power 0.2 per base trade power (before modifiers applied)
   Capital 0.2 × (5 + development) if the province is a capital
   Building +20% for every manufactory in the province^[5].
   Great Project +33% for every great project in the province.
   Local autonomy −0.33% per percentage point
   Is colony −75% if the province belongs to a colonial nation

   Reduced to −45% if the province contains a manufactory building
   Size of nation −1% per 15 development of nation (owner or colonial overlord), cap at -33% at 500 dev.
   Administrative efficiency −1% per point of the annexing country's Administrative efficiency.png administrative efficiency

   All the percentage modifiers(Building, great project, local autonomhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/y, "Is colony", size of nation and administration efficiency) are applied multiplicatively, but the tooltip displays them as additive effects.

  War enthusiasm[edit |https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ edit source]

   Ambox outdated content.png
   Warfare may need to be updated. https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/Please update this article to reflect recent events or newly available information, and remove this template when finished. Please see the talk page for more information.

   Other factors also give reasons for the AI to accept orhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ refuse a peace deal. These are summed up as war enthusiasm in the war screen. Positive War Enthusiasm is applied as negative reasons for that country to accept peace deals.
     * Length of war: +45 at start of war, decays by https://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/−0.75 at the start of each calendar month thereafter (5 years until it becomes negative).
     * Casus belli "Religious League" and "Crush the Revolution": +50
     * Casus belli "Coalition": +30 for attackers
     * Relative strength of alliances: −20 to +20 for war leader only
     * Ally in war: +10 for allies called in by war leader, +50 for Holy Roman Emperor (defensive war)
     * Military strength: −20 to +20, depending on proportion of manpower and land force limit that is filled, as well as battles lost or won
     * Recent gains: −20 to /eu4.paradoxwikis.com/n class="effect-green">+20 for war leaderhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ only.
     * Hold their own capital: /eu4.paradoxwikis.com/span class="effect-green">+5
     * War exhaustion: −1 per point of war exhaustion
     * Occupied and besieged provinces: scales linearly with base tax of provinces affected, up to −20 for full besiegement, and −40 for full occupation. The formula is roughly

   If war enthusiasm is between 0 and 20 it's classified as medium; below 0 is low and above 20 is high.

  Stability hit[edit | edit source]

   If a player refuses a peace offer that entails demands for less than 50% of the current warscore, and the warscore itself ihttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/s higher than 50%, the declining party takes a −1 hit to Icon stabilityhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/.png stability. When a player is already at −3 Icon stability.png stability, any qualifying offer is automatihttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/cally accepted on behalf of the player. There is a Diplomatic power.png icon displayed above the 'send peace request' button which shows that if the playehttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/r refuses this peace, they will lose stability

   This mechanic aims to prhttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/event players from unreasonably dragging out lost wars to harm their opponents (by deliberately causihttps://eu4.paradoxwikis.com/ng war exhaustion to rise or rebels to spawn).

   The AI has other rules for accepting peace deals and does not get a stability hit.
